Sale routes for a Chicago owner who wants speed

Three routes exist: work with a broker, sell it yourself, or accept money from a cash purchaser. A two-flat, a bungalow and a high-rise condo each point toward a different choice, so start with the building's condition and your deadline.

  • Broker listing. Showings come first, then a buyer whose lender sends an appraiser. Inspection findings turn into repair credits or price cuts.
  • Sale by owner. You save the commission and take on pricing, showings and the paperwork, usually with an attorney reviewing the contract.
  • Cash purchase. The purchaser accepts the building as it stands. Expect a lower figure than a polished retail sale, and compare it with your net after repairs and carrying costs.

Every route ends with the same public filings: a transfer tax declaration, a recorded deed and a seller disclosure report.

Chicago housing in brief

Chicago is a very large city made of many separate housing markets, so a street-by-street view matters more than the citywide average. Population is 2,731,585 across 227.73 square miles of land. Only 46.0 percent of households own their residence. The middle owner-occupied value is $334,100 and the middle gross rent is $1,440. There are 1,160,205 households averaging 2.29 people.

The city recognizes 77 community areas, containing more than 200 informal neighborhoods, which is why two houses a few miles apart can sell on very different terms.

Chicago transfer tax

Three layers of transfer tax can apply to a Chicago sale: a state tax, a city tax and a surcharge for the Chicago Transit Authority. At the state level, Section 31-10 of the Property Tax Code taxes a transfer at fifty cents per $500 of the value stated in the declaration, or fraction of $500.

The City of Chicago adds its own real property transfer tax. The Department of Finance prints the rate as $5.25 per $500 of transfer price, made up of a $3.75 city portion and a $1.50 CTA portion. In general the buyer owes the $3.75 and the seller owes the $1.50. Section 3-33-060 of the municipal code lists the exemptions, and none applies unless the declaration describes supporting facts and attaches documents.

Where each piece of Chicago transfer paperwork goes
PaperworkWhere it is handled
Transfer tax declarationFiled online through MyDec; the city does not take declarations by mail
Transfer stampsDepartment of Finance counter at 121 N. LaSalle, Room 107, or a registered title company
Deed recordingCook County Clerk, Recordings Division
State transfer taxFifty cents per $500 of declared value

One break is worth knowing about. The city offers a refund of the CTA portion for a buyer who is at least 65, lives in the home for a year or more and paid $250,000 or less. Have the title company confirm which lines apply to your contract, since the buyer and seller can agree to split charges differently.

Who records a Chicago deed

Recording belongs to the Cook County Clerk's Recordings Division, not to City Hall. Its public search finds recorded land documents by property index number and party name.

The counter keeps nine-to-five hours and stops taking customers at 4:45 pm. The Clerk's site also lists a Property Fraud Unit for owners who spot a questionable filing against their home.

At most closings the title company or attorney prepares the declaration, buys the stamps and sends the deed, so a seller seldom needs to go downtown in person.

What to gather before closing: the property index number, any lease copies, recent tax bills and a list of open permits or violation notices. Your title company will ask for each, and having them ready keeps the declaration, stamps and deed filing from slipping a day or two. If you are selling for cash, ask the purchaser to name who files the MyDec declaration and who pays for the stamps before you sign.

Cook County exemptions on a Chicago house

Missing exemptions are a common reason a Chicago bill runs high. The Homeowner Exemption subtracts $10,000 from equalized assessed value, continues each year once granted, and the Assessor puts its average saving near $950 a year.

  • Senior Exemption: a further reduction for owners 65 and over who live in the home.
  • Senior Freeze: household income at or under $65,000 for 2024, refiled yearly.
  • Long-Time Homeowner Exemption: about 2 percent of owners qualify, and the Assessor mails applications to likely candidates.
  • Home Improvement Exemption: applied without an application for up to $75,000 of added value, for four years at most.

The second installment bill lists the exemptions applied. If one was missed, a Certificate of Error can recover savings for tax years 2021 through 2025. Mention any pending certificate to whoever runs your closing, and ask how the current year's installments will be split between you and the buyer.

What a Chicago seller must disclose

A written disclosure report must reach the buyer before a contract is signed. Section 20 of the Residential Real Property Disclosure Act sets the duty and Section 35 prints the form.

Questions that matter in older Chicago housing include basement or crawl space leakage, foundation and roof defects, outdated electrical or plumbing, radon, asbestos, and lead paint or lead service and plumbing pipes. Termites, buried fuel tanks, boundary disputes and open violation notices appear too.

The seller answers from actual knowledge, may still sell as-is, and must update the report if conditions change before closing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Chicago houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Winter, older buildings and a quick sale

Chicago winters and aging buildings go together: freeze and thaw cycles, snow into early April and summer heat all work on roofs, walls and basements. The disclosure form asks directly about basement leakage and roof, wall and foundation defects, so expect buyers to start there.

Before taking any offer, list what an inspector would flag and estimate each repair. A long list favors a buyer who takes the property as-is over a retail listing that may stall on repair credits. Selling in winter, when showings thin out, can also make a cash buyer's certainty more attractive.

How to compare Chicago offers

Compare what each offer leaves in your bank account after every cost. Request each proposal in writing with a closing date and a list of who pays what.

  • Which side covers each transfer tax portion, and whether the contract departs from the usual split.
  • Whether open city violations travel with the building.
  • How leases are handled in a multi-unit property.
  • How leftover property tax installments and water balances are settled.
  • Whether the purchaser waives a mortgage contingency and appraisal.

A second offer or a broker's price opinion gives you something to measure against.

Frequently asked questions

How fast can a house sell in Chicago?

Title work, tenants and the speed of the declaration and deed filings set the pace. A cash purchaser removes the lender and appraiser from the timeline.

Who pays the Chicago transfer tax?

The buyer generally owes $3.75 per $500 and the seller $1.50 per $500. The state tax is separate and the contract may shift either piece, so confirm with your title company.

Do I need to repair my Chicago house before selling?

No. An as-is sale is allowed, but the disclosure report still has to be delivered first. A purchaser who takes the house as-is will price the needed work into the figure.

Where does the deed get filed after a Chicago closing?

The Cook County Clerk's Recordings Division records it, usually through the title company along with the MyDec declaration.

Can I sell a Chicago house that has tenants in it?

Yes. Hand the buyer the leases and rent records, and ask your attorney about deposits and lease handling at closing.

Aurora and its four counties

Aurora straddles the Fox River in northeastern Illinois and ranks second in the state by population, behind only Chicago. The 2020 count was 180,542 residents, and the July 2025 estimate is 181,505. The city began in Kane County and has since spread into DuPage, Kendall and Will. For a seller, that decides which recorder files the deed and which treasurer sends the tax bill, so start with the parcel number.

Aurora homes, rent and income
Housing figureAurora
Households, 2020-202461,317
Share of homes occupied by owners66.4%
Midpoint home value, owner-occupied$274,800
Midpoint monthly cost for mortgaged owners$1,995
Midpoint gross rent$1,596
Midpoint household income$93,633

West Side, East Side and Far East Side

The river splits the city, and each bank has its own character. East Aurora and West Aurora merged into one city in 1857, and public buildings went up on Stolp Island, in the river itself, because neither side would yield.

  • The West Side is everything west of the Fox River.
  • The East Side runs east from the river to the DuPage County line.
  • The Far East Side is the part of Aurora beyond that line.

Ten wards divide the city, and the three regions also track police boundaries and school districts. When you describe a house to a buyer, name the side of the river: it signals the school district and often the county in one phrase.

Older houses

Near downtown you find Italianate and Queen Anne houses, with Prairie School homes in the neighborhoods beside the core. The city also counts over 50 Sears Catalog Homes and seven Lustron all-steel houses. Owners of those, or of any pre-1950 house, will hear buyer questions about old wiring, lead paint, aging plumbing and settling foundations.

A cash offer for such a house is usually priced with the repairs in mind, while a buyer from a listing tends to raise them after the inspection. Keep records of any updates so the conversation starts from facts.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Aurora house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Which school districts serve Aurora houses?

The answer changes with the address, because several systems share the city.

  • West Aurora District 129 covers the west bank.
  • East Aurora District 131 covers the east bank.
  • Indian Prairie District 204 covers the far eastern portion in DuPage County.
  • Oswego District 308 runs four schools within Aurora's limits, while parts of the far north end go to Batavia schools and a southwestern corner to Kaneland.

Check the district for your exact street before you repeat a school claim in a listing.

Flood history and basements

A storm on July 17 and 18, 1996 dropped a state-record 16.94 inches of rain in one day, and floodwater reached nearly every low spot and the neighborhoods along the Fox River. Buyers near the river therefore tend to raise basement moisture, sump pump age and flood insurance.

Keep repair invoices handy and answer honestly about past water. Your insurer or the city's engineering staff can tell you whether your parcel sits in a mapped flood zone.

Rental licensing when your house has tenants

Each non-owner-occupied unit needs a license and gets inspected once a year, inside and out. The program dates to June 1, 1982, when the city council adopted its Property Maintenance Code. Renewals fall due by August 31, and the Property Standards Division mails renewal forms and schedules inspections by letter.

When a building with a rental license sells, the code asks for the new owner to be reported to the Operations Department within 3 working days. Property Standards is at 77 S Broadway, 1st Floor, and the licensing line is 630-256-3770. The division also handles high weeds, junk and trash, unsafe stairs, illegal basement apartments and unregistered landlords, and it runs vacant property licensing.

An empty inherited house, or a rental whose tenant has left, can draw a violation notice, so clear those items first.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Aurora houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Deed and transfer tax on an Aurora sale

The state's transfer tax is collected as revenue stamps through the recorder of the county where the parcel lies, and the same stamp can show payment of a county tax. Buyer and seller sign Form PTAX-203 for filing at that county.

Since Aurora touches four counties, ask the title company which recorder handles your address before you set a signing date, and ask whether any home rule charge applies.

Listing or cash offer?

Buyers here range from first-time families to investors, so a tidy house on a quiet street draws different interest than a fixer on a busy corner. A listing may reach a higher price but adds repairs, showings and loan risk. A cash purchase trades some price for a faster, steadier closing.

Compare what you would take home from each route after repairs and fees. Before you decide, call Property Standards about open violations, confirm your county from the parcel number and find out whether a rental license or vacant property license applies to the house. Settle those items first and the closing goes more smoothly under either route.

How an Aurora sale moves step by step

A smooth sale starts with the parcel number. It tells you the county, the recorder, the treasurer and often the school district. From there the steps run in a predictable order.

  • Confirm the county and call that county's treasurer for the tax balance and any open installment.
  • Call Property Standards at 630-256-3770 to ask about open violations, rental licenses or vacant property licensing on the address.
  • Choose a route: a listing, a private sale or a buyer who takes the house as it stands.
  • Sign the contract, then give the title company the payoff letter from any lender along with your tax bill.
  • At closing, buyer and seller sign Form PTAX-203, and the title company sends the deed to the recorder for the parcel's county.

Keep your copy of the recorded deed and the final closing statement once the county returns them.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What to gather before you talk to buyers

Buyers of older Aurora houses ask for paperwork before they ask for a price. Having it ready shortens the back and forth and makes a cash offer easier to compare with a listing.

  • Repair invoices for roofs, plumbing, wiring and any sump pump or drainage work.
  • Any insurance history on water damage, along with notes on what was fixed.
  • For a rental, the license, the most recent annual inspection result and the lease.
  • Your latest tax bill and the name of the county on it.

If the house is empty, an inherited property or a former rental, walk the exterior first. High weeds, trash, unsafe stairs or an illegal basement apartment are the items Property Standards writes up, and clearing them before a buyer visits avoids a notice during the sale.

Frequently asked questions

Which county is Aurora in?

Parts of four: Kane, DuPage, Kendall and Will. The parcel number on your tax bill tells you which one holds your house, records the deed and sends the tax bill.

Does a tenant-occupied house need a license to sell?

The license belongs to the owner who rents the unit and is renewed by August 31 each year. Report the new owner to the Operations Department within 3 working days after a sale, and call Property Standards at 630-256-3770 with account questions.

Will past flooding hurt the sale?

It can, mainly because buyers worry about repeat water. Tell them about past problems, keep repair records, and mention any sump pump or drainage work. Near the Fox River, expect flood insurance to come up.

Can a house with open code violations be sold?

Yes, and many buyers take houses as-is. Still, find out what is open at your address before you sign anything. Property Standards can explain what it takes to close a case.

Listing or cash offer: how do I decide?

Compare take-home money and timing. A listing may reach a higher price but adds repairs, showings and loan risk, while a cash purchase trades some price for a faster, steadier closing.

Selling in Naperville?

Naperville at a glance

Naperville sits about 28 miles west of Chicago and spans two counties, DuPage and Will. Population is 153,114 as of July 1, 2025, and the typical owner-occupied home is worth $540,200. About 74.8% of homes are lived in by their owners, and the median household income is $155,105.

Housing ranges from older downtown properties to subdivision homes built in the 1980s and 1990s, and buyers and appraisers treat those two groups differently. The city also spreads across six townships. Winfield, Milton, Naperville and Lisle are on the DuPage side, and Wheatland and DuPage townships are on the Will side. Some pockets, such as the unincorporated Tamarack neighborhood in the southwest, are cut out of the city limits, so a Naperville mailing address does not always mean the property is inside the city. That matters because the city's transfer stamp applies only to incorporated property.

Which county records a Naperville deed?

It depends on which side of the county line the parcel is on. Your tax bill or your last recorded deed shows the county. DuPage parcels go to the DuPage County Recorder, and Will parcels go to the Will County Recorder of Deeds in Joliet.

The two offices charge different fees for the same kind of document. Fees can change, so ask the recorder for the current figure before closing.

Standard deed recording fees by county
RecorderStandard deed feeWhat it includes
DuPage County Recorder$86.00Recording, document storage ($10), GIS ($31), real property ($1) and Rental Housing Support Program ($18)
Will County Recorder of Deeds$90.00 (effective October 1, 2025)Includes a $19.00 Rental Housing Support Program surcharge, dropped for government filers

For questions about the state transfer declaration, call the Illinois Department of Revenue MyDec help line at 844-445-1114. On the Will side, a deed needs the preparer and return addresses, the permanent index number, a legal description, a notarized original deed, the grantee name and address, a tax bill name and address, and a completed transfer declaration or exemption.

How the Naperville transfer tax stamp works

The buyer of a residential or commercial property inside incorporated Naperville buys the transfer tax stamp. The rate is $1.50 per $500 of purchase price, rounded up to the next $500 step. The stamp applies only to incorporated property, and the city's Your Place application, under Planning/Zoning Info, shows whether an address is inside the limits. Naperville is also among the municipalities whose stamps must be on a deed recorded with Will County.

The city asks for three things:

  • A Statement of Open Account letter, requested online no later than seven business days before closing.
  • A sales contract, a PTAX (MyDec) form or a sheriff's receipt carrying both buyer and seller signatures.
  • A copy of the deed that will be recorded with the county.

Allow up to seven business days of processing, whether you apply online or drop a packet at the Finance Department. The Customer Care Center at 630-420-6059 answers questions Monday through Friday, 7 am to 7 pm. The open account statement has its own seven business day lead time, so a closing set only a week out leaves no slack.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Naperville house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Exempt stamps for deed changes

An exempt stamp is for a deed change on property you already own, with no sale price involved. It costs nothing and covers properties inside the city limits only.

The city's examples:

  • Moving the property into or out of a trust.
  • A divorce, or removing a name.
  • A marriage, or adding a name.
  • A legal name change.
  • A refinance.
  • A foreclosure where the sheriff's deed puts the property in bank ownership. If an individual buys at the sheriff's sale, that buyer purchases a regular stamp.

The exempt packet needs the open account statement, a Certificate for Exemption (mailed and in-person applications only) and a copy of the notarized deed. If you are moving a house between names before a sale, start with this packet, and give yourself the same seven business day cushion.

Permits to check before listing

Start with any work done after you bought the house. Naperville's permit list has separate entries for decks, patios and sheds, driveways, fences, generators, lawn sprinkler systems with an RPZ backflow preventer, plumbing, electrical work, swimming pools and residential room additions or alterations.

If you cannot find paperwork for a finished basement, a deck or a sprinkler system, call the city and ask whether a permit was issued for that address. Learn the answer before a buyer's inspector or attorney asks.

If the house has unfinished work you do not want to complete, a buyer paying cash can take it as it stands and handle permits afterward.

Flood risk and older homes

Flood history is the weather topic that affects a sale here. The area took 14 inches of rain in under 24 hours in 1996, DuPage County was declared a disaster area, and damage topped $30 million. A second major flood followed in 2013.

Much of the land along the West Branch of the DuPage River belongs to the Forest Preserve District, which keeps development out of the floodplain. Even so, ask your insurance agent about your parcel before you list, since buyers' lenders will ask about flood zones too. Average precipitation runs about 37.7 inches a year, so on older homes buyers look first at sump pumps, gutters and grading.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Naperville houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Schools and commuting

Naperville Community Unit District 203 serves central and northern Naperville, with Naperville Central and Naperville North high schools. Indian Prairie School District 204 serves much of the rest. Small areas fall in District 200 on the DuPage side, and Plainfield District 202 and Valley View District 365U on the Will side. Confirm the district for your address before you advertise.

Interstate 88 crosses the north end, and Illinois Route 59 meets it at a diverging diamond interchange. Metra and Amtrak both stop in Naperville on the BNSF line, and the average commute is 30.5 minutes each way.

Selling without repairs and getting ready for closing

You can sell a Naperville house as it is. Whether a buyer takes the property in present condition is a term of your contract, and the city side of the closing is the stamp packet and the statement of open accounts, neither of which asks for repairs.

A workable order of steps: confirm the county and whether the parcel is inside city limits, gather permit records, request the Statement of Open Account online, and collect the signed contract or PTAX form. Have the deed ready for the county recorder. A cash buyer usually accepts the house in its current state and works to your closing date, which suits a seller who wants to skip showings and repair lists.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell my Naperville house without fixing it up?

Yes. Whether a buyer takes the property in present condition is a term of your contract. The city side of the closing is the transfer stamp packet and the statement of open accounts, and neither asks you to make repairs first.

Who pays the Naperville transfer tax stamp?

The buyer does. The city ordinance requires buyers of residential or commercial property inside incorporated Naperville to buy the stamp, at $1.50 per $500 of purchase price.

How early should I start the Naperville paperwork before closing?

At least seven business days early. The Statement of Open Account request is due no later than seven business days before closing, and stamp processing can take up to seven business days.

Does it matter if my Naperville home is on the Will County side?

It changes where the deed is recorded and the fee. Will County's standard document fee is $90.00 from October 1, 2025, while DuPage County's is $86.00. The city's own stamp rules are the same on both sides.

Which deed changes in Naperville need an exempt stamp?

Any change of name on a house you already own, such as adding a spouse, removing a name after a divorce, moving the property into a trust or refinancing. A sheriff's deed that puts the property in bank ownership also qualifies, with no fee.

Joliet at a glance

Joliet is the Will County seat, about 40 miles southwest of Chicago, and a small part of the city lies in Kendall County. Population was 150,362 in the 2020 census and is estimated at 152,241 for 2025. The city reaches into nine townships: Joliet, Plainfield, Troy, New Lenox, Jackson, Channahon and Lockport in Will County, and Na-Au-Say and Seward in Kendall County.

That patchwork has a practical result. Your address may sit in a different school district, assessor's office and tax bill from a neighbor a few blocks away, so check the parcel before assuming anything. Locals speak of an east side and a west side relative to the Des Plaines River, plus a far west side that includes the Kendall County land.

For 2020 to 2024, 73.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied, with a median home value of $265,800 and 51,055 households. Median gross rent is $1,276. Owners with a mortgage have median monthly costs of $1,960, compared with $819 for owners with no mortgage. About 26.3 percent of homes are not owner-occupied, so landlords and tenants figure in many Joliet sales, and with 28.8 percent of residents speaking another language at home, bilingual paperwork can be useful.

Older houses and historic districts

Joliet was settled in 1833 and reincorporated as a city in 1852. During the 1930s many owners could not keep up their large houses, and in the 1940s big Victorian homes were divided to house several families. Absentee landlords and deferred maintenance followed, and heavy use of vinyl siding changed several historic limestone buildings. The Joliet East Side Historic District, created in 1980, and the Upper Bluff Historic District, created in 1991, are both listed on the federal historic register.

  • If your house stands in one of those districts, ask the city's Planning and Zoning staff what review applies before you plan repairs.
  • If a large older house was ever split into units, bring any records of that conversion.
  • Buyers of pre-war houses commonly ask about foundations and wiring, so have repair records ready.

Roads, trains and schools

Joliet has moved from a steel and manufacturing town to a commuter city. I-80 and I-55 meet near Channahon, and US 6, US 30, US 52 and US 66 also cross the city, as do Illinois Routes 7, 53, 59 and 171. The Joliet Transportation Center is the final stop for the Metra Heritage Corridor and Rock Island District lines, and Amtrak stops at Joliet Union Station. Pace buses leave a downtown terminal about once an hour, six days a week. The mean commute is 28.8 minutes.

Schools vary by address. Joliet Public School District 86 and several smaller districts feed Joliet Township High School District 204. Other parts of the city fall in Plainfield District 202, New Lenox District 122 and, in Kendall County, Minooka and Oswego districts.

City requirements before a house sells

The seller of residential or commercial property inside city limits buys the transfer tax stamp. The city prints the cost as $3.00 per $1,000 of purchase price. The stamp applies only to incorporated Joliet, and the city offers an address verification map and a phone line for borderline addresses.

  • A completed water and lien letter must reach the city at least four business days before closing. Forms received later may not be processed before the closing date.
  • An exempt stamp, with no charge, is needed on any deed change inside city limits, such as adding or removing a name, moving a property into or out of a trust, or a divorce.
  • Exempt stamps require the original signed and notarized deed, not a copy, with exempt language on it or a completed city exemption form.
  • Start or stop water service through Customer Service at 815-724-3820, option 2.

Questions about stamps go to the Customer Service real estate transfer stamps desk at 815-724-3902. Most exterior projects, including fences, decks, pools, patios, garages, additions and concrete work, need a building permit and a plat of survey, so look for those before you list.

Recording a deed in Will County

The Will County Recorder of Deeds is at 158 N. Scott Street in Joliet, phone 815-740-4637. The fee schedule effective October 1, 2025 lists $90.00 for a standard document and $118.00 for a non-standard one. A standard document stays within up to five property index number references and up to five related document references.

A deed needs a notarized original deed, grantee name and address, a tax bill-to name and address, a property address, a permanent index number, the real estate transfer tax declaration or exemption, and the municipal transfer tax stamp. Joliet is one of nine Will County municipalities that require that stamp.

If the house is a rental, the city runs a Rental Inspection Program with an owner registration form, a landlord checklist and a fee schedule. Ask Neighborhood Services at 815-724-4090 whether the property is registered before you tell a buyer anything about it.

The city also bans parking on streets automatically when 2 inches or more of snow falls within 24 hours, under City Code Sec. 19-142, and prohibits boats, RVs, trailers and trucks over 8,000 pounds on streets and in residential parkways. Buyers who own a trailer or boat will ask about both.

Order of tasks before closing

Each step waits on the one before it, so work backward from the closing date.

  2. Get the original deed signed and notarized, with exempt language if the transfer is exempt.
  3. Send the completed water and lien letter to the city at least four business days before closing.
  4. Buy the stamp before recording.
  5. Record the deed with the Will County Recorder of Deeds, or through the Kendall County offices for a parcel there.

Missing any one of these can push a closing back. If you are moving out, call Customer Service about stopping water service.

What are the realistic ways to sell a Joliet house fast?

Each option suits a different situation.

  • List with an agent. A house in good repair does well on the open market.
  • Sell on your own. You handle the contract, the city stamp and the water and lien letter yourself.
  • Accept a cash offer. It can fit an inherited house, a rental with tenants or a property with a failed inspection, and closing can follow the schedule you need.

A cash sale has no lender appraisal to wait on, so the city paperwork above is usually what sets the pace.

How early must the water and lien letter reach the City of Joliet?

At least four business days before closing. Forms received later than that may not be processed before the closing date.

Where do I record a deed for a Joliet house?

Joliet is the Will County seat, so deeds go to the Will County Recorder of Deeds at 158 N. Scott Street. The fee for a standard document is $90.00.

Does a Joliet house in Kendall County use a different office?

Yes. A small part of Joliet is in Kendall County, so that parcel's tax bill and deed run through Kendall County offices. The city's address verification map and the tax bill show which county applies.

Which sale route fits a Rockford homeowner?

A Rockford owner can hire an agent, try selling without one, or deal directly with a buyer who pays cash and takes on the repairs. The right pick depends on the condition of the house, what you still owe and how soon you have to move.

Rockford has 61,324 households and a large rental share, so the people shopping range from owner-occupants to investors with very different budgets. See which of these sounds like you:

  • The structure is sound and you can live through showings and a buyer's loan approval.
  • A failing roof, tired mechanicals or code citations make a pre-sale renovation unappealing.
  • The property is a rental, either with a tenant in place or sitting empty and costing you money.
  • You inherited it, or you live elsewhere and cannot babysit a long listing.

A cash offer sidesteps the lender's appraisal, a common source of delays. Compare any offer with what a listing might realistically net, and get the terms in writing.

Prices, renters and who buys

About 147,384 people live in Rockford, slightly fewer than the 148,655 counted in 2020. Only 54.9% of occupied units are owner-occupied, so landlords and investors drive a good share of demand. The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $129,000, and the middle gross rent is $985.

At those values, repair costs weigh heavily against a sale price. That is one reason owners of older houses look at as-is sales rather than spending money on a roof or furnace they will not get back.

What buyers' inspectors look at

Rockford sits along the Rock River, and storms and hard winters are part of life here. Buyers and their inspectors tend to look closely at a few things:

  • Roof age and shingle condition after hail and wind.
  • Basement moisture near the river and creek corridors.
  • Furnace age.
  • Large trees, which give Rockford its Forest City nickname but can damage roofs and sewer lines.

Fixing or documenting these items before a showing helps, and it also helps you fill out the state disclosure report accurately. Keep receipts for roof, furnace and drainage work so you can hand them over when a buyer asks.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Rockford house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

City rules for rentals and property standards

Rockford keeps a Rental and Short-Term Rental Registry that supports its Residential Quality Support Ordinance and its Short-Term Rental Ordinance. Landlords register and update their details on the registry website, and the aim is fewer chronic nuisance problems through better communication between the city and owners.

The Property Standards division inspects exteriors and interiors for code and ordinance violations. Several items on its list would also come up in a buyer's inspection:

  • Roofs must be sound, and a tarp is not a repair. A roofing permit is required for any roofing work.
  • Heat must be supplied from October 1 to April 1 and keep habitable rooms at 68 degrees or warmer.
  • Insect screens are required from April 1 to October 1 on doors, windows and other openings.
  • Smoke detectors go outside each sleeping area, and carbon monoxide alarms must be within 15 feet of every room used for sleeping.
  • Property addresses must be visible from the road.

The city does not inspect for mold. If a buyer's inspector flags it, a private specialist is the next call. Before you list, ask Property Standards whether a case is open at your address, and make sure your registry entry is current if the house is a rental.

Which school district is the house in?

Most of Rockford sits in Rockford Public School District 205, with Auburn, East, Guilford and Jefferson as its high schools. Small parts of the city fall in Winnebago Unit District 323, Harlem District 122 and Meridian District 223, and the Ogle County portion is in Meridian. Buyers with children often start with the district, so call to confirm yours before you describe the house to anyone.

Recording the deed in Winnebago County

Deeds and mortgages for Rockford parcels are indexed by the Winnebago County Recorder's Office at 404 Elm Street, Room 405. The fee schedule dated January 1, 2025 is short:

A standard document uses white 8.5 by 11 inch paper, black ink, margins of at least a half inch, and a blank 3 by 5 inch space at the top right of page one. The office takes no copies, and every document needs a return-to name and address. The deed must also carry the state transfer declaration or an exemption statement.

E-recordings are processed daily, with the last review at 2:30 p.m. Anything sent later waits for the next business day, so tell whoever handles your title work if timing matters at closing.

Which county records my deed?

Rockford lies mostly in Winnebago County, with a sliver reaching into Ogle County. Look at the parcel number on your tax bill to see which county records your deed. Illinois counties must keep a review process for deeds that look fraudulent and a property fraud alert system, and owners can sign up free online for alerts about suspicious filings against their property. That is worth doing if you will leave the house empty during a sale.

From offer to closing in Rockford

Whatever route you choose, the paperwork follows a similar path. Gather the basics early so nothing stalls the day you accept an offer:

  • Your deed or the parcel number, and a recent tax bill.
  • Payoff information for any mortgage or lien.
  • Receipts for major repairs and permits, especially roofing.
  • Leases and deposit records if tenants live there.
  • The completed state disclosure report.

Once a contract is signed, the title company clears the title, prepares the transfer declaration and sends the deed for recording. With a cash buyer there is no lender timeline to wait on, which is why those sales can close faster. Ask the buyer to put the closing date, the price and any repair terms in the contract itself.

What an as-is sale leaves off your list

Selling to a cash buyer as is means you skip the roofing permit, the repainting and the trip to the hardware store before showings. You also skip weeks of open houses and the risk that a buyer's loan falls through at the last minute. You still owe any open code case, so ask Property Standards about your address first. Unpaid balances and liens come out of the proceeds at closing.

If the house is vacant, keep the lawn cut, the heat on in winter and the mail collected while you wait. A neglected property draws code complaints, and a complaint opened mid-sale can stall a closing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Does a landlord have to be on the Rockford rental registry?

The city runs a Rental and Short-Term Rental Registry for landlords, so make sure your entry is up to date before a sale. A buyer or title company may ask whether the property is registered.

What does it cost to record a deed in Winnebago County?

The schedule dated January 1, 2025 lists $54.00 for a standard document and $66.00 for a non-standard one. Check with the Recorder's Office before closing, since schedules change.

Will Rockford inspect for mold before I sell?

No. The city does not inspect for mold, so a worried buyer would need a private specialist.

Is Rockford in one county or two?

Mostly Winnebago County, with a small portion in Ogle County. Check the parcel number on your tax bill to see which county records your deed.

What time should an e-recording go in?

The Recorder's Office reviews e-recordings daily, with the last review at 2:30 p.m. Later submissions wait for the next business day.

Selling fast in Elgin

Selling quickly in Elgin generally means either a cash buyer or a listing that is ready on day one, and condition plus your calendar usually decide between them. With 115,476 residents, buyers and investors are active, but permits, rental licensing and Kane County or Cook County paperwork still decide how smoothly a closing runs.

Elgin straddles two counties, Kane and Cook, so recording and tax bills depend on which county holds your parcel. Check the county named on your tax bill before you contact a recorder.

  • Confirm the parcel number, the county and the township that assesses your home.
  • Request a mortgage payoff figure and look for liens or judgments.
  • Pull permit records for roofs, windows, water heaters and furnaces.

A cash buyer skips the appraisal and the lender's review, so the schedule depends on title, payoffs and county paperwork. Ask each buyer for a written offer with a closing date, and compare it with what a listing would net after commission, repairs and carrying costs.

Elgin's older housing stock

Older housing is part of Elgin's character. The city has Queen Anne homes built for watch company executives, Sears catalog kit homes from 1908 to 1940, and early cobblestone houses, with two districts listed in the federal register of historic places. Newer housing sits on the west and southwest sides. Downtown has gained townhouses, lofts and condo towers in recent years.

The Fox River Trail, Lords Park (112 acres) and Wing Park (121 acres) give the city parkland that appears in many listings. If your house is in a historic district, say so, since buyers either prize that or worry about exterior rules.

Elgin housing figures

Elgin has 39,317 households with 2.88 people each, and 71.9 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Owner-occupied homes have a middle value of $273,000, and rent at the midpoint is $1,361 per month.

School districts and commute routes

Five public school districts serve Elgin. Elgin Area School District U-46 covers most of the city, with Elgin High School and Larkin High School in town. Community Unit School Districts 301, 300 and 303 serve western and northwestern pockets.

Commute access is a selling point. Interstate 90 and U.S. 20 cross the city, along with Illinois Routes 19, 25, 31, 47, 58, 59 and 72 and Randall Road. Metra's Milwaukee District West Line has three Elgin stations, National Street, Elgin and Big Timber Road, with service to Chicago Union Station. The Pace bus system meets at the Elgin Transportation Center at 102 West Chicago Street.

Describe the district and nearest station in a listing, since buyers filter on both. A house in a western pocket may report a different district than one near downtown.

Permits and historic rules

Elgin's Community Development Department, at 150 Dexter Court, issues building permits. Review takes about 3 to 5 business days for quick permits such as roofs, windows, water heaters and furnaces, 7 to 10 business days for projects needing planner review such as sheds, fences, patios and driveways, and 10 to 15 business days for plans examiner review such as basement remodels, in-ground pools and decks larger than 100 square feet. Applications go to permits@ElginIL.gov.

Work started without a permit can draw a stop-work order and fines, and unpermitted work may have to be removed if it does not meet requirements. If the property is a designated landmark or lies in a historic district, exterior changes require a Certificate of Appropriateness. Elgin keeps an interactive historic property map so you can check an address.

Fixing permit gaps before you list helps, and for houses with several unpermitted changes, a buyer who purchases as-is can take them on directly. Call 311, or 847-931-6001 from outside the city, to find out whether a past project needs a permit record.

Elgin rental license and a sale

Elgin requires a rental license for any residential property occupied by someone who is not a blood relative. Licenses are not transferable and are voided automatically when the property sells, and the new owner has 30 days from closing to apply. Operating without one can bring a $500 citation from Code Enforcement.

Fees depend on unit count. The schedule is $149.00 for one to five units, with one unit inspected. A license lasts one year, and a property that passes its initial inspection with landlord training completed receives a two year extension. For single-family rentals, inspectors review the entire interior and exterior, and any code violation found must be corrected within 30 days or the license can be suspended or revoked.

  • Sellers of occupied rentals should tell the buyer about the 30 day licensing window.
  • Unpermitted changes found in an inspection are subject to enforcement no matter who made them, which concerns buyers.
  • Short-term rentals through Airbnb or VRBO also need the license.

Recording, taxes and utilities at closing

On the Cook side, the state charge is .50 per $500 and the county charge is .25 per $500, and the seller is the liable party. A deed recorded there costs $107. For parcels in Kane County, ask the Kane County Clerk's office for the current transfer declaration and recording fee instructions. Your title company normally manages submissions in both counties.

In Kane County a tax bill follows the property regardless of who owned it during the billing year, so check your closing statement to see whether the seller credits the buyer. A Kane County assessment complaint has to reach the Board of Review within 30 days of the township's published assessment notice. Elgin Township has its own assessor.

For a final meter reading, call Elgin's 311 line, where a Citizen Advocate schedules it for the owner's account. Ask the city at the same time whether any balance must be settled before closing.

Bring the parcel number, the payoff letter and a copy of your latest tax bill to the closing. If the house has a rental license, hand the buyer a copy of the license and any inspection notes so they know what the city will expect during the 30 day window.

Frequently asked questions

Does Elgin charge a transfer tax on home sales?

For parcels on the Cook side the state charge is .50 per $500 and the county charge is .25 per $500. Ask Elgin's Finance Department whether any city-level stamp applies, and have your title company confirm the full charges before you close.

Is my Elgin rental license transferable to a buyer?

No. Licenses cannot be transferred and are voided automatically when the property is sold. The buyer has 30 days from closing to apply for a new license, and the first license year carries an inspection.

How long do Elgin permit reviews take?

Quick permits such as roofs, windows, water heaters and furnaces take about 3 to 5 business days. Planner-review projects take 7 to 10 business days, and plans examiner reviews take 10 to 15. Contact permits@ElginIL.gov for the status of a specific application.

Which county records an Elgin deed?

It depends on where the parcel sits, because Elgin lies in both Kane and Cook counties. The tax bill names the county, and the title company files with that county's office.

Can I sell an Elgin house that has unpermitted work?

Yes, but disclose it and expect questions. Unpermitted work can be ordered removed if it fails requirements. Many sellers close permit gaps first, while an as-is buyer may take on the work and the risk for you.

Which selling path suits a Springfield homeowner?

Springfield homeowners usually weigh a brokered listing, a do-it-yourself sale and a cash purchase of the house exactly as it stands. Price, speed and repair work set them apart, and the best fit follows from the condition of the property and your move-out date.

  • Brokered listing: works for a sound house when you can wait out showings and a buyer's mortgage approval.
  • Do-it-yourself sale: you control price and buyer pool, and you arrange the paperwork yourself or through counsel.
  • Cash purchase: fits an estate house, an empty house or one with deferred upkeep, because no mortgage underwriting is involved.

Every month of utilities, insurance and mowing on a vacant house eats into a slow listing. Weigh the amount you keep after repairs and carrying months against the asking figure.

Springfield prices and renters

About 112,989 people live in Springfield, down from 114,394 in 2020. Housing costs sit well below the Chicago region. The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $162,100, and 64.3% of units are owner-occupied, so renters make up more than a third of households. Middle gross rent is $975. Owners with a loan pay a middle $1,400 a month, and debt-free owners pay $630.

The housing stock spans more than a century, and an older house may have outdated wiring or plumbing that buyers price in. A cash purchase can sidestep that negotiation. Check your village too: Jerome, Leland Grove, Southern View and Grandview sit entirely inside Springfield's borders. If your mailing address says Springfield but the village differs, that village's permit, tax and transfer rules apply instead.

Schools and commute

District 186 covers most of Springfield. Fringe areas belong to Ball-Chatham 5, Rochester 3A, Riverton 14, Williamsville 15, Pleasant Plains 8 and Unit 16. Buyers who work for the state or a hospital often search by commute and district, so name both when you talk to them.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Springfield house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What buyers' inspectors check

Inspectors for a buyer typically look at roof age, gutters, sump pumps and basements. Hold on to storm repair receipts and any claim paperwork, because a buyer's insurer may ask for them. A cash buyer purchasing as-is will still want to see the roof and foundation, but the negotiation stays between two parties.

The city's public works page notes that basement backups caused by private sewer laterals are not counted as city sanitary sewer overflows. If your house has flooded, say so plainly to buyers and keep plumbing records.

Permits, code orders and vacant buildings

The city's Building and Zoning Department, in Municipal Center West at 300 S. 7th Street, handles building permits. Its registration form for vacant buildings quotes a rule from the International Property Maintenance Code. An owner who has received a compliance order or notice of violation may not sell, transfer or mortgage the building until the order is complied with, unless the buyer gets a copy and signs a notarized statement accepting responsibility for the corrections.

A certificate of occupancy must be obtained before a vacant building is occupied again. A vacant house with two or more violations calls for a written plan with a repair schedule or a demolition plan. Ask the department for current fees and forms before you register or sell a vacant house.

Property tax assessment and appeals

Springfield sits in Capital Township, and Sangamon County's Supervisor of Assessments keeps ownership, sales and assessment records for every parcel. Non-farm property is reassessed once every four years, and an assessed value is one third of market value before a multiplier is applied.

  • A value dispute begins at the township assessor's desk and moves to the county Board of Review, which usually takes filings from July 1 through September 10.
  • If you disagree with that ruling, you have 30 days from its mailing to go on to the state Property Tax Appeal Board.
  • Exemption forms and mailing address changes: Supervisor of Assessments, 217-753-6805.
  • Bill copies and payments: County Treasurer, 217-753-6800.

Tax bills and the closing

Taxes paid in one year are for the prior year. Bills come due in June and September, and the annual tax sale follows in November for anything left unpaid. Closing papers normally give the new owner an allowance for the months the seller held the house, so ask your title company how the proration will look.

After the deed is recorded, the county says it takes about four to six weeks for the ownership record and the tax bill address to change. A buyer should confirm where the next bill is going. Address changes go to the Supervisor of Assessments in writing, by fax or in person, and the owner is responsible for sending the new address.

The recorder's office number is 217-535-3150. A standard document means letter-size paper with a 3 by 5 inch blank area at top right.

A cash sale in Springfield, step by step

Selling as-is to a cash buyer spares you the repair list and a lender's timeline. A sensible order of work is to check for open code orders, confirm which village the house is in, collect the deed and a recent tax bill, and then agree the price and closing date in writing. The title company handles the stamps and the recording. If the house has been vacant, ask the Building and Zoning Department about registration before you list, since a vacant building with violations needs a plan on file. Keep the utilities running and the yard maintained while you wait, and confirm in the contract who handles any correction the city may still ask for after closing.

Papers to gather first

Whatever route you take, a short folder saves days. Put your deed or parcel number, the latest tax bill and any storm or roof receipts in one place. Add leases and deposit records if tenants live in the house, and any code notice you have received. Note the names of the people you spoke with at each office. If you inherited the property, ask the title company early what documents the estate must supply. Share the folder with the buyer's side as soon as there is a signed contract, so the title company can move straight to the stamps and recording without waiting on you.

Is a Springfield house with open code violations sellable?

Yes, with conditions. The property maintenance rule on the city's form requires either that the violations be corrected first or that the buyer receive the notice and sign a notarized statement accepting the repairs.

What transfer stamps apply to a deed in Sangamon County?

The recorder prints 50 cents per $500 for the state and 25 cents per $500 for the county. Your title company can say whether anything further applies.

Who do I call to change the tax bill address after a sale?

Send the request in writing, by fax or in person to the Supervisor of Assessments, 217-753-6805. The county does not take address changes by phone.

How often is a Springfield house reassessed?

Sangamon County reassesses non-farm property every four years, though individual parcels can change sooner when there are physical changes or corrections.

What does it cost to record a deed in Sangamon County?

A standard real property document costs $64 to file, and anything outside that format costs $84. Call the recorder at 217-535-3150 to confirm before closing.

Selling a Peoria house fast

With a median value of $156,200 and a large rental share, a house that needs work often sells to an investor. Those buyers pay cash, close on your schedule and buy as is, while a listed sale usually means repairs, showings and a lender's appraisal.

  • Decide whether the house is owner occupied, vacant or rented, since that sets the registration steps below.
  • Collect the deed, tax bills and any code notices.
  • Compare a cash offer to a listing by what you net after repairs and carrying costs.

Peoria is the largest city on the Illinois River in this part of the state, about 110,920 people now, down 2.0 percent from 113,150 in 2020. Only 57.5 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, so landlords and investors are a real part of the buyer pool.

Neighborhoods differ a great deal. Several areas, such as Averyville and El Vista, began as separate towns that the city absorbed, so a sale on the East Bluff, in the Uplands or in North Valley can look very different from one across town.

Registering a rental or vacant property

Peoria wants every rental, every vacant residential property and any other dwelling where the owner is not living to be on its registry. Owners renew by February 28 each year. A new registration is due within 30 days after closing or after the home becomes non-owner occupied.

Fees listed by the city:

  • Renewal for a single-family home is $75. A multi-family property pays $75 for the first unit and $20 for each additional unit.
  • New single-family registrations cost $75 from January 1 to September 30 and $50 from October 1 to December 31.
  • A late registration fee of $150 per property applies after February 28 or more than 30 days after purchase.

You can register as exempt when the property is vacant and for sale, with an MLS or other listing as proof. The same goes for a property in probate or estate settlement, one where an immediate family member lives, one that holds a city Mothball Permit, or an owner-occupied home that is temporarily vacant for up to six months.

An owner whose home is outside Peoria, Tazewell and Woodford counties has to name a local property manager. After a sale, tell the city and use the Change of Status form to deactivate the sold property's registration.

The Peoria transfer declaration at closing

The city's real estate transfer declaration carries a tax of $2.50 per $1,000 of consideration or part thereof. It also asks you to check whether the property will be owner occupied or non-owner occupied. If the non-owner box is checked, section 5-522(a) of the city code requires the property to be registered as non-owner occupied at the time of closing.

Exempt deeds include those with actual consideration under $100, tax deeds, deeds that only confirm or correct an earlier recorded deed, and deeds to or from governmental bodies.

The county filing is separate: Peoria County accepts the PTAX-203 electronically through the state's MyDec system before the deed is recorded. Ask your closing attorney or title company to prepare the city form alongside the county filing so nothing holds up the recording.

Which school district is your Peoria address in?

Peoria Public Schools District 150 serves most of the city. Dunlap Community Unit School District 323 serves the far north and northwest, and Pleasant Valley School District 62, Limestone Community High School District 310, Peoria Heights District 325 and Illinois Valley Central District 321 cover edge areas.

A few blocks can change a child's district, so give buyers the district name that matches the address and confirm it with the district first. A buyer who is relocating with children will often ask for this before anything else, and a wrong answer on a flyer can cost you a showing or a signed contract.

How does Peoria's weather affect older houses?

Peoria has a humid continental climate, with hot summers and cold winters. The temperature swing from summer to winter is hard on older roofs, flashing, chimneys and basement walls. A buyer's inspector will ask how old the roof, chimney and basement walls are and when they were last repaired. Collect receipts and permit records before you list, and be ready to say plainly what has been done.

When a house needs more work than you care to take on, that is where an as-is cash sale makes the most sense, since the buyer prices the repairs into the offer and you skip the inspection back and forth.

Step by step for a Peoria seller

A quick Peoria sale usually runs like this on the seller's side.

  1. Work out whether the house counts as owner occupied, vacant or rented, because that decides what the city asks of you.
  2. Pull together the deed, recent tax bills and any code notices, then walk the house the way a buyer's inspector would.
  3. Get a cash offer in writing and compare it with a listing's net after repairs, showings and months of carrying costs.
  4. Choose a closing attorney or title company who will prepare the city declaration and the PTAX-203 together.
  5. At closing, hand over keys and records, then notify the city and deactivate any registration on the property you sold.

Peoria investors are used to older houses, tenant-occupied properties and homes with deferred work. That experience is the main reason a cash buyer can often close faster than a buyer who needs a mortgage, since there is no appraisal to pass and no lender to wait on. Ask any buyer to put the price, the closing date and who pays which costs in writing, and read it before you commit to anything.

What to gather before you close

A Peoria sale goes faster when the paperwork is ready. Bring the deed, recent tax bills, any city code notices, and proof of listing if you plan to register a vacant property as exempt. Ask your closing attorney to confirm whether the non-owner box on the city declaration applies to the buyer. If the buyer is an investor who will rent the house, the new owner must register it as non-owner occupied at closing.

Frequently asked questions

How much is the City of Peoria real estate transfer tax?

The city's transfer declaration carries $2.50 per $1,000 of consideration or part thereof. The form includes a list of exempt deed types. Ask your closing attorney to complete it with the PTAX-203 filed through the county.

Do I have to register a Peoria house I am selling?

Only if it is not owner occupied. Vacant homes listed for sale qualify for an exempt registration when you give the city an MLS or other listing as proof. After a sale, tell the city and use the Change of Status form to deactivate the registration.

When is Peoria's non-owner-occupied registration due?

Renewals are due every year by February 28, and new properties must be registered within 30 days after closing or after becoming non-owner occupied. A $150 late fee applies after those dates.

Which school district is my Peoria house in?

Most of Peoria is in District 150, but Dunlap District 323, Pleasant Valley District 62, Limestone District 310, Peoria Heights District 325 and Illinois Valley Central District 321 cover other parts. Check the address with the district before you list.

Is Peoria a good market for a quick cash sale?

A cash sale is an option for many houses. Investors and landlords are part of the buyer pool, so compare any offer against a listed sale after repairs, fees and carrying costs.

How the university shapes Champaign sales

Champaign is a city in Champaign County in east-central Illinois. It shares the main University of Illinois campus with its twin city, Urbana. The 2020 census counted 88,302 residents, and the city covers 22.99 square miles of land.

The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign enrolls more than 50,000 students a year, and Parkland College adds about 9,000. Whether a house sits near campus, near Parkland on the northwest side or out toward the newer southwest subdivisions changes who the likely buyer or tenant is. Check the Champaign Unit 4 attendance boundary before you advertise a school connection.

A single-family seller a few blocks from Campustown or downtown should expect buyers to ask about parking, noise and nearby rental density.

Who is likely to buy

The university and health care dominate local jobs. The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign has 13,934 employees and Carle Foundation Hospital has 6,921, and that mix with technology work tends to hold housing demand steady. Employees often want a short drive or a bus line, so say which applies to your house.

Interstates 57, 72 and 74 meet at or near Champaign, and Illinois Terminal is the hub for Amtrak, intercity buses and the local transit district. Houses near a bus line to campus are easy to describe to investors and to students' parents.

Showing a house during the school year

Campus calendars drive local life. Semester start and finish dates bring waves of movers, and a house on the market near campus will see more traffic when students and staff are in town. Choose showing times that avoid move-in weeks, and keep rental tenants informed so they stay cooperative. If a tenant lives in the house, give the required notice before any visit and ask whether the lease allows photos.

Drainage and older houses

Champaign sits on relatively high ground for the region, and downtown drains toward Boneyard Creek. If your street is near the creek, ask your insurer or the city about drainage, since a buyer's inspector will notice a wet basement.

The area has hot summers and cold winters, so inspectors tend to look at roofs, gutters, sump pumps, furnaces and air conditioners. A seller with an aging system can expect the issue to come up in negotiations. A cash buyer purchasing as-is usually prices it in directly.

When building work needs a permit

The city requires a permit whenever you build, enlarge, alter, repair, move or demolish a structure. The same goes for installing or replacing electrical, gas, mechanical, plumbing, sprinkler or fire alarm systems. Since January 1, 2025, applications go through an online portal. The city adopted the 2021 International Codes on January 9, 2024.

Property maintenance and rentals

Property maintenance, nuisance and blight rules are enforced by the Neighborhood Code Compliance Division, and neighbors can file complaints with the city. An open complaint on your house should be cleared before you list.

The city has described a registry of residential rentals and vacant commercial buildings, meant to give it current owner and agent contact information. If you own a rental, ask the Neighborhood Services department whether registration has taken effect.

Downtown property owners should know about the snow rule. When public works declares the ordinance in effect after more than two inches of snow, owners in the designated areas have 24 hours to clear sidewalks, or the city clears them and bills the owner plus an administrative fee.

Your deed goes to the Champaign County recorder. Before a closing date is set, put one question to the recorder, the city and your title company: does any local transfer or utility step apply to this property?

Listing, selling yourself or taking a cash offer

A house in good repair, with an owner who can handle showings through the school year, does well on the open market. A property with deferred maintenance, or a rental aimed at students, can fit an investor who intends to renovate. Cash shortens the calendar and ends the repair haggling, though the price lands under what a finished house would earn.

Start every conversation with buyers armed with the permit history, utility details and any tenant lease.

Preparing a student rental for sale

A rental near campus carries extra paperwork. Gather the current lease, a rent roll if the building has several units, and repair records. Give buyers the lease end dates, since those decide when a new owner can move in or re-rent. Neighborhood Services can answer rental registration questions, and Neighborhood Code Compliance can report open complaints.

Investors who buy student housing think about turnover and condition. Give a cash buyer a plain list of what needs work and what you have replaced.

What to bring to your title company

  • The deed and the most recent property tax information for the parcel.
  • Permit history, plus any repair receipts for the roof, furnace, plumbing or electrical work.
  • Current leases, if any tenant lives in the house.
  • Utility account details, so final readings can be arranged.
  • A note of any open complaint with Neighborhood Code Compliance.

Having this folder ready speeds up a title search and lets a cash buyer make a firm offer without a second visit. If something is missing, say so plainly, and tell the buyer who you called to find it. That honesty usually builds trust and keeps the deal moving.

Steps from signed contract to deed recording

Start by choosing a title company and giving it the contract. Complete the Illinois transfer declaration in MyDec. Check with the city for any local requirement tied to the property, such as a utility step. Then sign the deed and send it for recording with the Champaign County recorder.

Book each step in order and keep copies. If the house has open permit work or a code complaint, resolve it or agree in writing with the buyer who will take it on. Sheds up to 120 square feet and fences are exempt from building permits, but zoning rules still apply to fences. Ask the Building Safety Division before you build.

How do I report a property maintenance problem?

File a complaint with the Neighborhood Code Compliance Division of the City of Champaign. The division enforces property maintenance, nuisance and blight rules.

What is the Illinois transfer tax on a sale?

The state rate is 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 stated in the transfer declaration. The declaration is completed in the state's MyDec system.

The 2020 census counted 88,302 residents. That makes Champaign the tenth most populous municipality in Illinois.

Ways to sell in Waukegan

Listing with an agent, selling without one and taking a cash buyer's as-is bid are all open to a Waukegan owner. The city paperwork is the same for all three, so the choice mostly turns on how much repair work, waiting and showing you want to take on.

Waukegan faces Lake Michigan, roughly 11 miles below the Wisconsin line and 37 miles up the shore from downtown Chicago, and no other Lake County city has more people. The 2020 census counted 89,321, and the mid-2025 estimate is 87,940. The city has about 32,000 households, and it adds a transfer step that many Illinois towns do not have, covered next.

Zoning certificate and closing letter

Every change of ownership in Waukegan needs a zoning certificate, a life-safety inspection and a closing letter, under Ordinance 23-0-294. The city's Closing Letter / Zoning Certificate page has the application.

File the online application when you list, and in any case at least 30 days ahead of closing. A code officer calls within five days of the fee payment to book a minimal code and life-safety inspection. The certificate has to hang where it is fully visible, as near the front entrance as possible, for the whole time the home is on the market.

The ordinance has no exceptions, so foreclosure and tax-sale transfers need the same documents. Each parcel number in a sale needs its own closing letter, and a missing number can hold up the closing.

  • Seller side: property details, occupancy status, number of bedrooms or units, MLS number if listed, and the listing agent's contact information.
  • Buyer side, once you have one: a driver's license number for the water account transfer, receipts for any city amounts already settled, and a notarized affidavit.
  • Utility side: call the Water Department at least five business days before closing to schedule the final meter reading (847-360-0535).

Costs and steps of a Waukegan sale

These city and county items attach to a house sale.

Waukegan and Lake County items attached to a house sale

Zoning certificate application fee$150.00, due when you submit

The closing letter is issued only after the fees and the final water bill are paid. Any liens on the property are disclosed in the record, and the payoff statements can be settled at closing.

Is an as-is sale allowed?

Yes, with conditions. The city allows an as-is sale when the zoning certificate inspection is done and the buyer signs a notarized affidavit. The city provides no template, so the affidavit has to carry a date, the buyer's address, phone number and email, a list of the items the buyer takes on from the inspection report, the buyer's signature and the notary's confirmation.

A cash buyer who agrees to take the inspection items does not hold the closing up for repairs, though the inspection itself still has to happen. Sellers who wait until a contract is signed to apply risk running into the 30-day window.

State law adds a separate duty: residential sellers give the buyer a completed disclosure report before signing (765 ILCS 77/20). Transfers from an estate fiduciary, by court order or in lieu of foreclosure are among the exempt ones listed in Section 15.

Homes and prices in Waukegan

Owners and renters split the city almost evenly: owners occupy 50.2% of homes. The middle value of an owned home is $190,900, well under suburbs to the south, and the middle rent with utilities is $1,205 a month. The city has 32,042 households of about 2.72 people, with a midpoint household income of $71,919.

The city has also pursued a lakefront plan to replace much of the old industrial shoreline with residential and recreational space. Most of Waukegan belongs to Waukegan Community Unit School District 60, but pieces fall inside Gurnee School District 56 and a small section sits in Beach Park District 3 and Zion-Benton District 126, so check the district named on your tax bill before describing schools in a listing. Commuters look at the Metra Union Pacific North line, the Tri-State Tollway and the Amstutz Expressway.

Selling a Waukegan rental

The city's rental license page explains that every rental inside city limits needs a license before anyone moves in. Licenses expire each December 31, the fee is $60 per rented unit, and an application needs planning and zoning pre-approval plus a passed inspection by the Building and Code Department. A code officer reaches out within five business days to schedule it.

Where tenants occupy the house, keep the license current while it is listed and tell prospective buyers about the lease early. Ask the city's License Department how the license is handled when ownership changes.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Waukegan houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Recording the deed in Lake County

Deeds for Waukegan homes are filed in the county building at 18 N County Street, 6th Floor, with the Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office (phone 847-377-2575). Its fee schedule lists a $70 standard document fee and an $82 non-standard fee, and the only other charges at recording are state and county transfer taxes.

The county's deed packet lists what must be on the document.

  • Signed and dated by the grantor, with a notary acknowledgment
  • The buyer's address, a full legal description and the preparer's name and address
  • A "mail to" address and the name and address for tax bills
  • A completed PTAX-203 declaration or a signed exemption statement

The state tax follows 35 ILCS 200/31-10, which prints the rate as 50¢ per $500 of the value stated in the declaration, counting any fraction of $500. The same packet names six Lake County municipalities that require a local stamp before recording. Waukegan is not on that list, though the closing letter described above applies.

A cash sale from start to finish

Start the city application the day the house is under agreement, or sooner. While the inspector's visit and the closing letter move along, the title company searches the record, and you gather payoff statements for any mortgage or lien.

Before closing day, call the Water Department for the final meter reading and pay the last bill. At the table you sign the deed, the buyer signs the affidavit if the sale is as-is, and the deed goes to the Lake County Clerk for recording. With no lender involved, the city steps and the title work are the whole schedule.

Frequently asked questions

Must a Waukegan seller repair every item the inspector lists?

No. The city allows an as-is sale if the buyer signs a notarized affidavit accepting the listed items. The inspection still has to be done and the certificate issued, so apply as soon as the house is listed or under agreement.

What does the Waukegan closing letter process cost?

The city lists $300 at submittal, split into a $150 zoning certificate fee and a $150 closing letter fee. Any other invoiced amounts owed to the city, including the final water bill, are settled before the letter is issued.

Do foreclosure and tax-sale transfers in Waukegan skip the certificate?

No. The city's ordinance lists no exemptions for transfers such as foreclosure or tax sale, so those transfers also need the application, inspection and closing letter.

Who files the deed after a Waukegan closing?

The Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office takes it, at 18 N County Street in Waukegan. Bring it in or send it by mail; the office phone is 847-377-2575.

How soon can a Waukegan cash sale close?

The city's steps set the minimum: apply at listing, at least 30 days before closing, with an inspector calling within five business days. An as-is buyer can follow that schedule, and title work sets the rest.

Two local steps on nearly every Cicero sale

Cicero requires Real Estate Transfer Stamps and a Certificate of Compliance on nearly every home sale. The Building Department covers both on its "Buying Or Selling A Home?" page, and they affect how fast a sale can close and who ends up paying for repairs.

A seller here usually has three paths: fix everything the Town flags and sell with a certificate in hand, sell as-is and let the buyer take on the compliance work, or complete a transfer that the Town classes as exempt. Each is described below with the paperwork it needs.

How the Certificate of Compliance works

A Town building inspector walks the property, hands the owner a list of everything out of line with the Town Code, and the property must meet that list before a certificate is issued. The steps run in order: an inspection, a compliance checklist and then bringing the property up to code.

The Town treats a "transfer" broadly. It covers a deed, articles of agreement for a deed, an assignment of the beneficial interest in a land trust, using real property as loan collateral and adding a present beneficiary to a land trust. Purchasing transfer stamps is mandatory for all transfers, including those that are otherwise exempt from the compliance step.

The three ways to transfer a home in Cicero
RouteWho handles complianceHow it works
Sale with a current certificateSeller, before the saleThe property already meets Town Code, so the transfer is straightforward for the buyer
As-is saleBuyer, after the purchaseThe buyer assumes responsibility for bringing the property into compliance and obtaining the certificate
Exempt transactionNo certificate neededApplies to categories such as court-ordered or familial transfers and vacant land

Talk to the compliance staff early and allow ample time, because the review covers multiple parts of the property.

Transfers exempt from the compliance step

Four categories are exempt, and for those no inspection or certificate is required. Transfer stamps are still required for every one of them.

  • Court-ordered transfers: tax deeds, sheriff's deeds and transfers made under orders of local, county, state or federal courts.
  • Vacant land: transactions involving only vacant land.
  • No change in ownership interest: transfers that do not give a new party an ownership or beneficial interest.
  • Familial transfers: adding a spouse to a deed under Section 22-281 of the Town's Code of Ordinances, in effect since March 24, 2017.

If you inherited a Cicero home and are unsure which category applies, ask the Building Department before you list. The Town Hall is at 4949 West Cermak Road, open Monday through Friday from 8 AM to 6 PM, and the main line is (708) 656-3600.
