State and county paperwork

Cicero deeds are recorded by the Cook County Clerk's Recordings Division, and the state transfer tax is 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 stated in the declaration. That rate is set in 35 ILCS 200/31-10.

The Clerk's office records and maintains land records, lets the public search them by property index number or party name, and runs a Property Fraud Unit that helps owners investigate suspicious filings against their property. It is open 9 am to 5 pm and takes its last customer at 4:45 pm. Ask the Building Department what the transfer stamps cost, and ask your title company which other charges appear on the closing statement.

Illinois law also requires the seller of residential property to complete a disclosure report and give it to the buyer before the contract is signed. Section 20 of the Residential Real Property Disclosure Act sets that rule, and the report asks about basement leakage, roof and foundation defects, radon, lead paint and lead pipes, among other items. A house that needs work can still be sold in as-is condition, but the questions have to be answered honestly.

Cicero housing at a glance

Cicero has about 81,858 residents in roughly 5.87 square miles, and its homes are family-sized. Owner occupancy is 54.6 percent, the median value of an owner-occupied unit is $249,400 and median gross rent is $1,154. There are 24,432 households averaging 3.36 people, and median household income is $70,842. About 95.0 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so many owners have been in place a long time.

Large, long-tenured households are the group most likely to shop for a family-sized house, which helps a seller who has kept the home in decent shape.

Cook County tax items to check before closing

Check whether the house has the Homeowner Exemption on its tax bill. The Cook County Assessor's exemption cuts the equalized assessed value by $10,000, renews automatically once granted, and requires that you own and live in the home as your principal residence.

  • Seniors 65 or older may also qualify for the Senior Exemption.
  • The Senior Freeze has an income limit of $65,000 or less for calendar year 2024 and must be filed each year.
  • Missing exemptions for tax years 2021 through 2025 can be redeemed with a Certificate of Error.

Taxes in Illinois are billed in installments, and the second installment bill shows the exemptions that were applied. At the closing table, ask the title company to show how the current year's bill is split between you and the buyer, and whether any installment is still unpaid.

Weighing a cash offer in Cicero

The main question is whether a buyer who takes the house as-is leaves you with more or less than repairing it for the Town and listing it. A compliance checklist can include items you would never fix for your own use, so get the inspection list first, price the work with a contractor, and then compare it with the cash number.

  • Total of the repair bids needed to earn a certificate.
  • Months of mortgage, utility and tax payments while the house is listed.
  • Who buys the transfer stamps and who pays for the compliance inspection.
  • Whether the contract states plainly that the buyer will obtain the certificate after closing.

Put every figure side by side before deciding. A quick, certain closing is worth something, but only you can say how much.

Steps from decision to closing

Start by calling the Building Department to ask whether your transfer falls in an exempt category. If it does not, request the compliance inspection and read the checklist line by line. Then decide: repair and list, or sell as-is to a buyer who accepts the checklist. Bring the title company in early so the stamps, the state declaration and the deed recording are lined up before the closing date. On closing day, confirm that the contract says who obtains the certificate if the sale is as-is.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a Certificate of Compliance to sell my Cicero house?

Usually yes, unless the transfer is exempt. The Town lets you sell with a current certificate or sell as-is, in which case the buyer takes on the work of obtaining it after the purchase.

Are transfer stamps required for every Cicero sale?

Yes. Real Estate Transfer Stamps are required for all real estate transfers, even those that are exempt from the compliance step.

Can I sell a Cicero house with code violations?

Yes, through an as-is sale. The buyer assumes responsibility for bringing the property into compliance, so the price usually reflects what the Town's checklist would require.

Who records the deed for a Cicero home?

The Cook County Clerk's Recordings Division records it. Your title company or attorney normally files the deed along with the state transfer declaration.

Is adding my spouse to the deed treated as a sale in Cicero?

It counts as a transfer, but adding a spouse to a deed under Section 22-281 is an exempt familial transfer. No inspection or certificate is required, though the transfer stamps are.

Bloomington housing at a glance

Bloomington is the McLean County seat in central Illinois, covering 27.24 square miles. The count was 78,680 in 2020 and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 78,804. Median value of owner homes is $203,300, 61.9 percent of homes are owner-occupied, median gross rent is $1,050 and the average commute is 16.8 minutes.

Employers such as State Farm and Illinois State University in neighboring Normal supply a steady stream of local buyers. Many shoppers tour houses in both towns on the same weekend, so check recent sales in each before pricing.

Schools and districts

Two public districts cover the city. Bloomington Public Schools District 87 serves the interior with Bloomington High School, Bloomington Junior High and six elementary schools. Growth pushed the city well into McLean County Unit District No. 5, which runs Normal Community High School and Normal Community West High School. A small part of the city lies in Olympia Community Unit School District 16, and Central Catholic High School is a private option.

Attendance lines do not follow city limits, so look up the exact district for your street before the listing goes live. Families ask this first at a showing.

Rental registration and inspections

Landlords in the city must register each residential rental and hold a Certificate of Inspection before a unit is rented or leased. When you sell a rental, these rules decide what the next owner starts with.

Bloomington rental program costs
Fee or taxAmount
Registration, per building$65
Added per rental unit, buildings of three or more units$5
Follow-up inspection$100

  • The first inspection is included in the registration fee, and each owned condo needs its own registration.
  • A registration lasts through December 31 and does not pass to a new owner, so the buyer files a fresh one.
  • Inspectors give owners at least 15 days' notice and check the building against the International Property Maintenance Code, the Fire Code and other ordinances.
  • A building rated fair may be required to post a $5,000 letter of credit or pledged account until it receives a passing rating.
  • Violations not fixed by the reinspection date lead to a court appearance and possible court costs.

Hosts who rent for short stays remit the tax by the 25th of the next month and owe a 5 percent penalty if they pay late. They also register the unit every year in the rental program. Clear any unpaid tax or open inspection item before you close.

Investors who pay cash will often accept a tenant-occupied building, or one with violations, in its current state. That can spare you a round of repairs and reinspection. The city's rules still follow the building to its next owner, so put in writing who handles reinspection after closing.

Anything tied to your time as owner, such as unpaid fees or a pending court date, is yours to clear first. Ask the city what is open on the address, and file inspection reports and any passing rating with your sale papers.

Deed recording in McLean County

The McLean County Clerk's office handles recording at 115 E. Washington Street, Bloomington. Its Predictable Recording Fee Schedule, effective July 1, 2023, sets a standard document at $61.00. Documents exempt from the Rental Housing Support fee, such as government filings and powers of attorney, are $41.00, and a non-standard document is $75.00.

A document counts as non-standard if it uses legal- or ledger-size paper or has six or more PIN or related-document references. Recorded documents must be originals or certified copies. Certified copies cost $18.00 and additional copies $1.00 per page. The recording phone is (309) 888-5170.

The state transfer declaration and any transfer tax come on top of the recording fee. Your title company collects them at the table. Request an itemized settlement statement a few days early and check each line.

How to appeal your assessment

You have 30 days from the publication date shown for your township to file an assessment complaint with the Board of Review, and a late complaint will not be heard. The county posts each township's publication and deadline dates in a table, and the Board of Review office is at (309) 888-5132. For 2026 the equalization factors were 1.0534 for the Bloomington township and 1.0385 for the City of Bloomington township.

Non-farm complaints go on Form PTAX-230. Values rest on market activity in the three years before January 1 of the assessment year, and a multiplier brings the statutory assessment to 33.33 percent. The City of Bloomington Township Assessor holds property record cards and an online lookup, which helps when you want to see how neighbors are assessed.

Where a buyer's questions usually land

Bloomington buyers who shop with a mortgage tend to ask about three things: the school district, the property tax bill, and whether the building is a registered rental. Having those answers on one sheet makes your house easier to say yes to. Add the township, the last tax amount and any inspection rating, so the buyer's agent does not have to chase you.

Taxes at closing

Taxes are the part of a Bloomington closing most likely to surprise a seller who has not looked at a bill lately. Pull your current statement and note both installment amounts, and tell your title company if you hold an exemption.

Before closing, call the County Treasurer for installment dates and a payoff figure. Which installments are already paid drives the proration on your statement. If you appeal, keep the Board of Review decision with your records so a buyer can see the outcome.

Steps from offer to closing

Without a buyer's lender in the picture the timeline shortens, yet recording and taxes work the same. A typical order looks like this.

  • Collect the deed, newest tax bill, rental registration, inspection reports and repair receipts.
  • Find out which school district and township assessor your address falls under.
  • Get a payoff figure from the Treasurer.
  • Send your title company the buyer's details so the statement is drafted early.
  • At the table, read the recording fee, state declaration and any transfer tax line by line, then sign the deed that goes to the County Clerk.

Tell buyers early if the house is empty or has tenants. An as-is purchaser prices the condition in, and an honest list of known problems saves time. Leases can move the closing date, so show a copy at your first conversation.

Can a new owner use the previous owner's Bloomington rental registration?

No, it does not carry over. A buyer who wants to rent the building registers it fresh, pays the fee and passes inspection.

What does it cost to record a deed in McLean County?

A standard document is $61.00 and a non-standard one is $75.00 under the July 1, 2023 schedule. Phone the County Clerk to confirm before you send payment.

How long do I have to appeal a McLean County assessment?

Thirty days from your township's publication date. Late complaints are not heard, and the county posts the dates each year.

Is the short-term rental tax applied to every Bloomington short-term stay?

Stays under 30 days carry the 6.0 percent tax. Hosts on a listing site still register each property and file monthly certification forms.

Does a cash sale remove the need to fix rental violations in Bloomington?

The rules follow the building, though a cash buyer may take it as-is and handle repairs and reinspection later. Clear fees or court matters from your ownership first, and get the terms in writing.

Schaumburg has an estimated 77,249 residents in 31,655 households averaging 2.41 people. Only 62.9% of units are owner-occupied, so renters make up a large share, and a house with tenants in place is a common thing to sell. Gather leases and deposit records early if that is you. Most of the village was built out between the 1960s and the 1990s, so many sellers are offering a house or unit with decades of wear on its roof, windows and mechanicals. Buyers tend to ask about those items first. Buyers who work along the I-90 and Golf Road corridor often put proximity first, and the Metra Milwaukee District West Line stop gives commuters a rail option.

Drainage and sump pumps

The village sits at the headwaters of the West Branch DuPage River, with the east side draining through West Branch Salt Creek toward Busse Lake. Drainage and sump pump health therefore deserve attention before you list. The village's permit services publish a drain tile and drainage resource guide for homeowners who need work done, and a buyer's inspector will probably test the pump.

Schools and district lines

Most of the village falls in Community Consolidated School District 54 for elementary and middle grades and in Township High School District 211. Not every District 54 school sits inside the village, so check the attendance boundary for the address you are selling before you quote it to a buyer.

Vacant home inspection before the transfer stamp

Schaumburg ties its transfer stamp to the condition of vacant homes. Since a 2015 ordinance change, every vacant single-family home gets an interior and exterior inspection before the real estate tax transfer stamp is released. Occupied homes are not covered by that rule.

Vacant single-family home requirements

If the inspection finds violations that are not corrected, the buyer must provide a notarized letter of intent before the stamp is released. Other holds on the stamp for the property must be cleared as well. Questions go to the Building Division at 847-923-4420.

Registering and maintaining a vacant house

Vacant homes must be registered under Chapter 123.04 of the Village Code, and you return the Vacant Building Registration Form to do it. Minimum upkeep includes:

  • Removing dead shrubs.
  • Clearing accumulated mail and notices.
  • Replacing broken windows or doors.

Code Enforcement can be reached at 847-923-3700. A tidy, registered house moves through the stamp inspection more smoothly than one with open complaints.

The state stamp is 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction (35 ILCS 200/31-15), and recorders will not accept a deed lacking those stamps (35 ILCS 200/31-20). On the Cook County side of the village, the state rate is $0.50 per $500 and the county rate is $0.25 per $500, with the seller as the liable party.

Part of Schaumburg lies in DuPage County, so first look up the parcel number and confirm which county records the deed. Ask the title company or the recording office for the exact stamp amount and any municipal charge. The village's real estate tax transfer stamp is a separate item from the state and county stamps.

Property tax for a seller

Cook County parcels are billed in two installments each year. Ask the Cook County Treasurer or your title company what is paid and what remains open on your parcel, since due dates have moved from year to year. The title company prorates the year's bill between you and the buyer on the closing statement, and the Treasurer's exemption list includes the Homeowner Exemption and senior programs the buyer may need to claim. For a DuPage parcel, ask the DuPage County Treasurer for the matching schedule.

What a cash sale skips in Schaumburg

A cash buyer will usually take the house as is, so you skip repairs, staging and the weeks a lender needs for an appraisal. You do not skip the village steps. Book the inspection as soon as you have a contract, since scheduling follows payment of the fee, and ask the buyer to agree in writing on who handles any violation the inspection turns up.

Step by step for a vacant Schaumburg house

If nobody lives in the house, the order of work matters because each piece feeds the next:

  • Register the vacancy with the village and start keeping the lawn, windows and sump pump in shape.
  • Pay the $100 fee and book the inspection at the Community Development permit counter.
  • Fix anything the inspector flags, or agree with the buyer that a notarized letter of intent will cover it.
  • Clear any other hold on the property so the village can release the stamp.
  • Have the title company confirm the county, buy the state and county stamps, and file the deed.

Skipping a step usually means the closing waits. The stamp is the last gate before recording, so anything unresolved at the village stops the sale on the day you hoped to finish.

Papers to have ready

Keep your deed or parcel number handy, along with a recent tax bill, the leases for any tenant, and receipts for roof, window or drainage work. A buyer who sees that the house has been looked after is less likely to ask for a price cut after the inspection. If you live elsewhere, name one local contact who can meet the inspector and let in the title company's appraiser or the buyer's walkthrough team.

Frequently asked questions

Does Schaumburg require an inspection to sell a house?

Only for vacant single-family homes. They need an interior and exterior inspection before the transfer stamp is released, and the fee is $100 paid when you schedule.

How long does the Schaumburg vacant home inspection take?

It can usually be scheduled within 3 business days after the $100 fee is paid. Call the Building Division at 847-923-4420 to confirm timing before you set a closing date.

What happens if the inspection finds problems?

Uncorrected violations require a notarized letter of intent from the buyer before the stamp is released. Other holds on the property must be cleared first.

Do I have to register a vacant house in Schaumburg?

Yes. Vacant buildings must be registered under Chapter 123.04 of the Village Code, and there is no fee. You return the Vacant Building Registration Form and keep the lawn, windows, sump pump and exterior in order.

Which county records a Schaumburg deed?

It depends on the parcel, because Schaumburg lies in both Cook and DuPage counties. Check the parcel number, then file with that county's recording office along with the required state and county stamps.

Evanston is a lakefront suburb of 76,380 residents, roughly 12 miles north of the Loop on Lake Michigan. The housing stock runs from older frame houses and brick two-flats to condominiums and high-rises near the water.

School districts and your address

Two public districts cover the entire city, and a buyer will want to know which elementary school serves your address. Evanston-Skokie School District 65 teaches pre-kindergarten through eighth grade, and Evanston Township High School, the only high school in District 202, teaches grades 9 through 12.

The district office can tell you the attendance area for a given address, so confirm it before you write the listing.

Transfer tax and the stamp

Evanston's real estate transfer tax is usually paid by the seller, though the contract can say otherwise, and the stamp has to be issued before a deed is recorded.

Evanston transfer tax by sale price
Price bandCharge per $1,000
$1,500,000 or less$5
Above $1,500,000, through $5,000,000$7
Above $5,000,000$9

Stamps are electronic. The practical timeline looks like this:

  • File the stamp request through the city's online service portal or the 311 line. Counter requests are not taken.
  • Plan to file seven to ten business days ahead of closing. The city needs five business days to process, counted from the day after receipt, and it does not rush requests.
  • Complete the Evanston declaration form and add it, with any backup documents, to your service request.
  • A final water bill is created automatically with the request, except for condominiums and vacant land.
  • The stamp is released only once the paperwork checks out and everything you owe the city is paid.

A stamp for an exempt transaction costs $100. Payment rules tighten as the stamp amount grows. Between $5,000 and $50,000 the city will not accept personal or attorney checks, and at $50,000 or more only a cashier's check or wire works. Call the City Collector's office to confirm the current rate and accepted payment types before you schedule a closing.

Rental registration and short-term rentals

A rental house carries registration and inspection duties that a buyer will ask about. Under Ordinance 141-O-18, long-term rentals of single-unit homes, condominiums, multi-unit buildings and accessory dwelling units are registered annually.

New registrations cost $200 plus $12 per unit, and annual renewals cost $12 per unit. Owner-occupied units, buildings registered as vacant, shared housing providers and units used only for short-term stays are exempt, although in a building with several units only the owner's own unit is covered by that exemption. Inspection frequency depends on the last result: within five years when no violations were found, within three when up to seven were found, and within one year when more than seven or an infestation turned up.

Stays under 30 consecutive days fall under the separate short-term rental license. New applicants pay $150 to apply and $250 a year, and the unit must pass a property maintenance inspection first. A buyer who wants to host guests should check this before making an offer, and a condo buyer may need a letter from the association confirming that its bylaws permit short stays. If you rent the house today, gather your registration confirmation and latest inspection report for the buyer.

Permits and unfinished projects

Unpermitted work can surface in a buyer's inspection or a lender's review, so sort out permit status before you list. Building and Development Services handles permits, inspections and property maintenance enforcement for the city.

The city has adopted the 2021 international building, residential, existing building, property maintenance, mechanical, fuel gas and fire codes with local amendments, and it adopted the 2023 Illinois Stretch Energy Code. Permit applications received on or after October 1, 2025 must follow the Stretch Code, which matters if you are finishing a renovation to improve your sale price.

  • Collect permit records and final sign-offs for any addition, deck, finished basement or mechanical upgrade.
  • If something was built without a permit, ask the permit desk what the city will require before you list.
  • Resolve any cited maintenance violation before the closing date.

When repairs make no financial sense, an as-is buyer can take on the open items, as long as the purchase contract states clearly who is responsible.

Cook County assessments and appeals

Cook County, not the city, values Evanston homes and bills their property tax. For a residential property, the assessed value is generally 10 percent of the Assessor's estimated market value, and the Assessor does not set levies, rates or bills.

Appeals cost nothing and can be filed online in as little as 20 minutes. The usual window is 30 days after the reassessment notice, with the last day printed on the notice, and the appeal calendar by township is on the Assessor's website. An appeal rarely changes the bill much when the listed characteristics are accurate and the estimated value is within 10 percent of what you believe the home is worth.

A fresh purchase price does not always match the Assessor's estimate, because the office values every property with the same method. Your closing agent or attorney prorates the tax bill at settlement. For payment status or refund questions, contact the Cook County Treasurer.

Frequently asked questions

Is it possible to close on an Evanston house in under a month?

Yes, an as-is purchase can close within a few weeks, though the city timeline sets a floor. File the transfer stamp request seven to ten business days before closing, and allow five business days for processing.

Which party covers the Evanston transfer tax?

The seller normally covers it, unless the contract assigns it elsewhere. The rate is $5 per $1,000 up to $1,500,000, then $7 through $5,000,000, then $9 beyond that.

Must a landlord register an Evanston rental before a sale?

Registration is an annual requirement for long-term rentals under Ordinance 141-O-18, so keep it current. Owner-occupied units, buildings registered as vacant and units used only for short-term stays are exempt.

Is an as-is sale possible for an Evanston house with open repairs?

Yes. The stamp still requires verified documents and payment of what you owe the city, including the final water bill, so settle those even if the buyer takes the repairs.

Which office should I ask about an Evanston tax bill?

Ask the Cook County Assessor about valuation and appeals, and the Cook County Treasurer about the bill itself. The City of Evanston does not set the amount.

Arlington Heights housing in brief

Arlington Heights lies in Cook County roughly 25 miles northwest of the Loop, and a sliver of the village reaches into Lake County. Its 16.61 square miles are almost entirely developed, so a seller here competes with other established blocks. The 2020 count was 77,676 people, and the July 2025 estimate of 76,216 is 1.9% lower.

The downtown Metra station anchors a walkable district of shops, restaurants and entertainment, and a short walk to it is the sort of detail a buyer remembers.

Older houses and what inspectors look at

The settlement started as Dunton, a depot stop, and took the name Arlington Heights in 1874. Farms and greenhouses covered most of the ground into the postwar years. Then came the 1950s and 1960s, when automobiles, the baby boom and a string of annexations lifted the count to 64,884 by 1970, by which time nearly all open land was gone.

A house from those decades draws close attention from inspectors at the roof deck, the electrical panel, the supply piping and the basement walls. Before you list:

  • Request the village permit file for your address.
  • Collect paperwork showing when the furnace, water heater and roof were replaced.
  • Find out whether a finished lower level or an addition went through permitting when it was built.

Parks and nearby landmarks

The Arlington Heights Park District owns 456.53 acres and leases another 258.56 acres across 58 parks. Lake Arlington, a human-made 50-acre detention lake, sits inside a 93-acre park with a 1.8-mile path around the water. Downtown has the Metropolis Performing Arts Centre, and the village hosts Frontier Days at Recreation Park before Independence Day. Mention whatever is closest to your house in the listing.

What is happening with the Arlington Park property?

The former racetrack at 3200 W. Euclid Ave. covers 326 acres, and the Chicago Bears Football Club bought it in February 2023. The village keeps a redevelopment page for it, and the team has since said it would focus on a stadium opportunity in Indiana. The village still regards the property as a highly viable redevelopment site because of its size, transportation access and place in the northwest suburbs.

For a seller nearby, the future use of that land is unsettled. Buyers will ask what you know, so read the current village page before you answer.

School districts

Elementary and middle students in most of the village attend Arlington Heights School District 25, and District 214 runs the high schools. Parts of the village belong instead to Districts 15, 21, 23, 57 or 59, which means two neighbors can have different schools.

  • South Middle School and Thomas Middle School are District 25 schools.
  • John Hersey High School is the only public high school inside village limits. Some areas feed Buffalo Grove, Prospect, Rolling Meadows or Wheeling, and a few feed Palatine High School in District 211.

Verify the assignment for the exact street before writing it into a listing.

Short-term rentals and the 30-day rule

A buyer cannot use the house for stays under 30 consecutive days. The Village Board's March 2, 2026 ordinance set a 30-day minimum on all residential rentals, effective July 1, 2026, and it did not grandfather existing short-term rentals. Shorter stays count as nuisances, and the village acts on complaints.

Hotels, motels and lodging rooms are exempt. Sellers get a carve-out: if the rental agreement is signed along with the contract to sell, a seller may stay on after closing for fewer than 30 consecutive days. Ask the closing attorney to draft it that way.

Permits and building codes

Permits run through the Building & Life Safety Department and its online Civic Access Portal, where applicants can track a permit, book inspections and upload documents. The counter is open 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays, with a 9:30 a.m. start on the first and third Wednesday. The phone is 847-368-5560.

Work may take place between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. on weekdays and between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. on weekends. The village has adopted the 2024 International codes to replace the 2018 editions, effective January 1, 2027, and the department tells applicants to read the updated requirements before submitting. If you plan repairs before listing, finish and close them out under the current rules.

Deed and transfer tax on an Arlington Heights sale

State transfer tax is paid with revenue stamps bought through the county recorder. Both sides sign the PTAX-203 declaration, filed where the parcel is. Ask the title company whether a county or home rule municipality adds a charge of its own.

In Cook County, the Clerk's schedule prices a deed at $107, a total that bundles recording, GIS, storage, state housing and filer fees, and that schedule has applied since April 1, 2024. The Lake County slice of the village records with that county.

When a cash sale makes sense

Cash works when the roof or kitchen is dated, when an estate or divorce sets the clock, or when months of showings and loan approvals are not an option. The trade is simple: speed and certainty in exchange for the price a fully updated listing might reach.

  • Line up any offer against what a listing would put in your pocket after agent fees and repairs.
  • Ask who covers the title search and recording, and get it in the contract.
  • Confirm the day of closing, plus what happens to utilities and your belongings that day.

A signed purchase agreement, a title commitment and a clear closing statement protect you on either route.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Closing steps for either route

Whether you list or take a cash offer, the order of work is similar. Pull the permit record from Building & Life Safety and finish anything open. Gather the dates for the roof, furnace and water heater. Decide which county your parcel sits in, because the Cook County Clerk and Lake County handle recording separately. Then sit down with the title company and go through the contract clause by clause, including who pays each transfer charge, what day you hand over keys, and how utilities and belongings are handled on that day.

If tenants live in the house, the new 30-day rule matters to the buyer, so put any lease terms in writing and share them early.

Frequently asked questions

How fast can an Arlington Heights cash sale close?

On whatever date the contract names, since no lender has to approve anything. Recording in Cook County runs through the County Clerk, so give the title company time to prepare the deed.

Must I repair the house first?

No, but open permits deserve attention. Pull the record from Building & Life Safety and finalize anything unfinished. Cosmetic work is optional when you sell as-is.

Can I stay in the house after closing?

Yes, for a short time. The village lets a buyer and seller sign a rental agreement of under 30 consecutive days if it is executed together with the contract to sell. Without that paper, short stays at a residential rental are treated as nuisances.

Who writes the check for transfer taxes?

Whatever the contract says, so read that clause. Your title company can itemize each tax and name the party responsible.

Where does my deed get recorded?

At the recorder for the parcel's county. That is the Cook County Clerk for most of the village and Lake County for the small piece there. Look up your parcel number to be sure.

Which selling route suits a Bolingbrook house?

Three paths lead to a Bolingbrook closing: a listing, a sale you run yourself, or a direct purchase by an investor who takes the property in its current condition. The route changes your timeline and net proceeds, yet the village's stamp office sits at the end of all three.

  • An agent listing draws the most showings, and you wait while a buyer's lender finishes underwriting.
  • A sale by owner keeps the commission in your pocket and hands you the contract, deed and village errands.
  • A direct purchase trims showings and repair negotiations, and the price usually reflects that convenience.

Get any offer in writing, with proof of funds or a loan approval attached, and find out who orders and pays for the title search before you sign.

The Bolingbrook market

Bolingbrook lies roughly 28 miles southwest of downtown Chicago, across Will County and DuPage County. Nearly everything there was built after 1960, and the village incorporated on October 6, 1965. Population grew from 7,651 in 1970 to 37,261 in 1980, and the mid-2025 estimate is 74,803.

The typical home value is $314,700 for 2020 through 2024, and owners live in 79.1 percent of housing units. The village has 23,959 households averaging 3.08 people, typical gross rent is $1,749, middle household income is $108,400 and the one-way commute is 30.0 minutes. Of residents, 91.2 percent did not move within a year, so a seller is often one of only a few resale homes on the market in a given subdivision.

Houses from the 1970s through the 1990s are old enough that roofs, furnaces and water heaters tend to wear out around the same time. That cluster of repairs is the usual reason an owner here looks at an as-is sale.

Transfer stamp requirements

The village sells its own transfer stamp at $7.50 per $1,000 of price, with the cost split equally between buyer and seller. It will not issue a stamp until the property is clear of all village debts. The village words the base as "per $1,000.00 or fraction rounded to the next highest $500.00 of purchase price."

What if the village is owed money?

A closing cannot move forward until the village clears the property. Order the clearance letter early, read every line, and pay what it shows before you head to the stamp counter. Anything left over is a reason for the stamp to be refused, and a refused stamp can push the closing date.

Your title company or attorney can usually pick up the clearance letter for you. Give them the parcel number and the date you expect to close, then ask for the figure again a few days before the closing so the balance is current.

Which county records the deed?

Bolingbrook straddles Will County and DuPage County, so the office that records your deed depends on where the parcel sits. Look at your tax bill to see which county to use. The Illinois Department of Revenue says buyer and seller complete the PTAX-203 and file it with that county, and a county may charge its own transfer tax on top of the state's.

The state revenue stamp is priced at 50 cents per $500 of value under 35 ILCS 200/31-15. For the tax proration at closing, ask the county treasurer for your parcel for the installment dates and the latest bill.

School districts and listings

Valley View Community Unit School District 365U covers most of Bolingbrook, but several other districts claim slices of the village. On the Will County side those include Indian Prairie CUSD 204, Plainfield CCSD 202 and Naperville CUSD 203. In DuPage County, the portions fall under Woodridge School District 68 and Community High School District 99.

Families ask which district serves a house before almost anything else, so name the right one in the listing. Fountaindale Public Library District covers most of the village.

Getting around

Interstate 55 runs through the southern end, Interstate 355 hugs the east edge, and Route 53 (Bolingbrook Drive) divides the village north from south. Pace routes 755, 850 and 851 run express to Chicago with park-and-ride stops, and the Metra Heritage Corridor stops in neighboring Romeoville on weekday rush hours. Commuters will ask, so put drive times in your listing.

What buyers' inspectors look at

Sump pumps, grading, gutters and basement walls draw the most attention here, because the village sits in low, wet ground. Servicing a sump pump or patching a roof before you list can keep a buyer's report short. An as-is buyer simply prices whatever turns up.

Gather receipts for any roof, furnace or water heater work, and write down the age of each system. A seller who hands over that list at the first showing usually gets fewer repair requests later.

From signed contract to closing

Once you accept an offer, the village steps run in a fixed order. Knowing the order lets you book each one without waiting on the last.

  • Order the clearance letter and pay any village debt it shows.
  • Have the seller and buyer sign the Residential Transfer Information and Disclosure form, adding a power of attorney if someone signs for another person.
  • Complete the PTAX-203 with the buyer.
  • Collect the stamp near the closing date, since it expires after five business days.
  • Record the deed with the county where the parcel sits.

A direct purchase can compress this list considerably when the buyer has funds ready and the clearance letter is clean. A financed sale takes longer because the lender sets the closing date.

An as-is sale suits a house where repair bills and carrying costs outweigh the gap in price. Add up the repairs you would need, the months on the market and your closing costs, then compare that net to the offer. The village charges $7.50 per $1,000, with liability split equally between buyer and seller. The amount is figured per $1,000 or fraction rounded up to the next $500 of the purchase price.

Can a Bolingbrook closing proceed if the village is owed money?

No. The village requires the property to be clear of all debts before it issues a stamp. The clearance letter shows what is owed, so pay those items first.

Is Bolingbrook in Will County or DuPage County?

Both. The village straddles the two, and the county where your parcel lies records the deed and receives the PTAX-203.

Most addresses are in Valley View 365U. Some are in Indian Prairie 204, Plainfield 202, Naperville 203, Woodridge 68 or Community High School District 99, so confirm the parcel with the district.

It can, when repair bills and carrying costs outweigh the gap in price. Weigh the net amount after repairs, months on the market and closing costs, and get the terms written down before you commit.

Sales routes for a Decatur homeowner

A Decatur owner has three ways out: list with an agent, sell privately, or deal with a cash buyer who takes the house with its flaws. The state of the roof, furnace and foundation, plus how soon you need the money, usually points to one of them.

Values in Decatur sit far below those in the Chicago suburbs, so one large repair bill can swallow much of a seller's margin. An as-is sale can then net close to what a polished listing would.

Decatur home prices and the market

Decatur is the Macon County seat, in the middle of Illinois. Population has slipped from 71,399 to 67,884, a drop of 4.9 percent, so price from recent local sales and not from older figures. Prices are modest, and nearly four in ten homes are rented.

At roughly $100,000, a single new roof or furnace can equal a noticeable slice of a house's worth. That arithmetic explains why many owners here lean toward selling as-is. Buyers also check which school district a parcel falls in, since most addresses are in Decatur Public Schools District 61 and a few spill into neighboring districts.

Macon County offices for a Decatur sale

Three offices share the Macon County Office Building at 141 South Main Street. Each opens at 8:30 in the morning and closes at 4:30 in the afternoon on weekdays, except legal holidays.

  • Recorder, Room 201, (217) 424-1359. Files deeds and mortgages, maintains a tract index more than 150 years old, and takes electronic filings through vendors such as CSC and Simplifile.
  • Treasurer, Room 302, (217) 424-1426. Sends the annual tax bill and provides duplicates.
  • Supervisor of Assessments, Room 401, (217) 424-1364. Publishes assessments, applies exemptions and serves as clerk to the Board of Review.

The state transfer tax comes from 35 ILCS 200/31-10, which sets 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500. Ask the Recorder's counter whether Macon County adds a stamp of its own.

Property tax billing and unpaid taxes

Macon County runs a year behind: the bill mailed in May covers the previous tax year. The first installment comes due 30 days after the mailing date, and the second falls on September 1, shifting to the next working day when that date is a weekend or Labor Day.

At a sale, read the settlement statement and ask the title company who owes the bill. Paying late is costly: 1.5 percent attaches for every month or part of a month. Once the second installment passes, a certified delinquency notice goes out with $10 added, and the unpaid amount is auctioned to tax buyers who open at 9 percent and bid downward. A house lived in by its owner generally gets 30 to 36 months to redeem.

A duplicate bill costs $1.00 with proof of ownership. New owners should send the Treasurer a change-of-address form by March 15.

Disputing a value has a short fuse: 30 days from the day your township's figures run in the local paper. Complaints are filed with the Board of Review, and the assessor's staff recommend attaching comparable sales, an appraisal or a settlement statement.

If you owe taxes at closing, the title company normally deducts the balance from your proceeds and pays the Treasurer directly, so ask for a written payoff figure a few days beforehand. Bring the parcel number to the Treasurer's office (Room 302), and if the bill is in a former owner's name, ask for a duplicate rather than waiting for a mailing.

Vacant homes and short-term rentals

Two city chapters can follow a property into a sale.

  • At-risk property registry (Chapter 70.2). Lenders register a property within 15 days of starting foreclosure. Owners of a derelict vacant house register within 30 days. Residential registration is $200, renewed every six months, with a late charge of 10 percent of the semi-annual fee per 30-day period. A buyer takes over the duty and must register or update the file within 15 days of the transfer.
  • Short-term rentals (Chapter 51.5). A yearly license is $25 per unit, and an 8 percent tax applies to gross rental receipts, with monthly returns due by the 20th.

A registered vacant house costs money every six months it stays empty, which makes a prompt as-is sale attractive. Ask the city's building department about open permits or violations before you set a price.

Checklist before a Decatur closing

Gather these papers first. Then judge each bid by the amount left in your hands once every payoff is made.

  1. Pull your parcel number and the latest bill from the Treasurer.
  2. Request your recorded deed and make sure the names match the signers.
  3. Check that no city registration charge or code fine is outstanding.
  4. Round up leases and renter contact information if anyone lives there.
  5. Obtain written payoff letters from each lender or lienholder.

Whichever route you pick, closing ends with a title search, a signed deed, the state declaration and county recording. A cash buyer may skip the appraisal, but clean title is still required.

A cash closing can move much faster than a financed one when title is clean, since a financed sale a financed sale waits on the lender's appraisal and underwriting. Ask whoever buys to name the title company, who covers its fee and whether the buyer will take over any leases.

Inspections and older Decatur houses

Central Illinois has cold winters and hot, humid summers, so inspectors pay close attention to roofs, heating systems and damp basements. Before you accept an offer, walk through the house the way an inspector would and note what you would flag. A buyer using a loan may ask for repairs or credits after the inspection, while a cash buyer generally prices those items into the first offer and moves on. Either way, ask for the number in writing and for the closing date the buyer will commit to.

Frequently asked questions

Will a buyer take a Decatur house with open code problems?

Often yes. Investors regularly buy houses with violations and fix them. Learn from the city what is open so your price reflects it, and settle any registration balance first.

Who covers Illinois transfer tax on a Decatur sale?

The state rate is 50 cents for each $500 of value, and your contract decides which side pays. Confirm with your closing agent, and ask the Recorder if a county stamp also applies.

What are the due dates for Macon County tax bills?

Mailing happens in May, the first installment is due 30 days later, and the second is due September 1 or the next working day. Late payments add 1.5 percent monthly.

Is a license required for a Decatur Airbnb?

Yes. Chapter 51.5 requires a yearly license for each short-term unit at $25, plus an 8 percent tax on rental receipts filed monthly with the city's Finance Department.

I inherited a Decatur house with unpaid taxes. Where do I start?

Call the Macon County Treasurer at (217) 424-1426 with the parcel number to learn the balance. If the taxes were sold, redemption runs through the County Clerk and includes penalty, costs and interest.

Ways to sell in Skokie

A Skokie owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or sell directly to a buyer paying cash. The cash route usually saves the most time, since there is no showing schedule and no lender appraisal to wait for. Whichever path you take, Skokie adds paperwork of its own: a village transfer stamp, a final water reading, and for rentals a pre-sale inspection.

  • Use an agent and live with showings, repair requests and a longer wait.
  • Go it alone and take on the contract, disclosures and title work.
  • Take a cash offer, normally as-is, and set the closing day.

Skokie homes, owners and what buyers want

Skokie has an estimated 66,544 residents in 24,382 households averaging 2.68 people, and 74.7% of units are owner-occupied. The middle home value is $387,200, middle gross rent is $1,552 and middle owner cost with a mortgage is $2,510 a month.

The housing is mostly brick bungalows and mid-century houses from the 1920s through the 1950s. That stock tends to need updated kitchens, electrical panels and mechanicals, and many heirs and downsizers sell with original systems still in place. Buyers who ride the CTA Yellow Line or work in health care are the likeliest to pay extra for a renovated house. For schools, several elementary districts serve the village, with Niles Township High School District 219 running the public high schools. Part of Skokie belongs to Evanston/Skokie School District 65. Confirm the district for your street before you advertise schools.

What buyers' inspectors check

Buyers touring a Skokie bungalow commonly focus on the basement, roof and electrical service. Freeze and thaw cycles stress older brick, chimneys and flat roofs, and heavy rain tests basements and sump pumps. Knowing the condition of those items before you set a price saves surprises later, and receipts for past work help your case.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Skokie house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Village transfer stamp and final water reading

Skokie requires a transfer stamp for any change in ownership in the village. The Village Clerk's Office sells it at Village Hall, 5127 Oakton Street. The stamp cannot be issued while the property has liens, code violations or an unpaid balance owed to the village.

To process the stamp, submit the completed Real Estate Transfer Tax Form with a Request for Final Water Reading. The request lists the closing date, a contact name, phone and email, the seller's forwarding address for the last water bill, and the buyer's phone and email. Send documents to transfertax@skokie.org or mail them to the Clerk's Office. The clerk's phone is 847-933-8203.

Rental property inspection

Rentals have one more step. The village will not issue a stamp for a multi-unit rental building, or for a single-family house, duplex or townhouse used as a rental unit, until the Property Standards Division has inspected it and any violations are corrected. Ordinance says to schedule that inspection at least 28 days before closing, and last-minute slots may not exist. Owner-occupied houses are not covered by this inspection.

Transfer taxes on a Skokie sale

A sale here can carry charges at three levels. The Cook County Clerk names the seller as liable for the state and county amounts. Stamps come from the recorder (35 ILCS 200/31-15), and the deed is refused for filing without them (35 ILCS 200/31-20).

Property taxes and exemptions at closing

Cook County bills Skokie parcels in two installments, and the due dates have shifted from year to year. Ask the Cook County Treasurer for the current dates and any payment already posted to your parcel. At closing, the title company usually divides the year's tax between buyer and seller by closing date.

The Treasurer's site lists a Homeowner Exemption, a Senior Citizen Homestead Exemption and a Senior Citizen Assessment Freeze Exemption. A buyer applies for the ones they qualify for after the sale.

Steps to a quick Skokie sale

Count back from your closing date; the village timelines set the pace.

  • Pull the village's lien and violation status and clear any unpaid balance.
  • If the house is a rental, book the Property Standards inspection at least 28 days ahead.
  • Gather your forwarding address and the buyer's contact details for the final water reading request.
  • Order the state transfer declaration through the title company so the stamps and deed are ready together.
  • Record the deed with the Cook County Clerk's recording division after the stamps are affixed.

Selling an inherited or long-held Skokie house

Many Skokie houses have been in one family for decades, so heirs and downsizers are common sellers. Original wiring, an aging furnace and a dated kitchen are the usual issues. If you inherited the house, locate the deed and the latest water and tax bills first, then ask the Clerk's Office whether any balance or violation is open. A cash buyer will often take a house like this as it stands, which spares you from hiring contractors for a property you may not live in. You still need the stamp, the final water reading and a recorded deed.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

If the house has liens or code violations

Open liens, code violations and unpaid village balances all block the stamp, and without the stamp the deed cannot go forward. Pay or resolve each one before closing, or ask the Clerk's Office how an open item affects your date. Give the title company the village's answer in writing so the payoff can come out of your proceeds at the table.

What a cash sale skips here

A direct cash purchase skips staging, open houses, a lender's appraisal and the repair list that follows a buyer's inspection. It does not skip the village steps. The transfer stamp, the final water reading and, for a rental, the Property Standards inspection all apply the same way. Build them into your calendar from the day you sign. If the buyer is paying cash, the village paperwork is often the longest item left, so send the transfer tax form and the water reading request as soon as a closing date is agreed. Keep a copy of the stamped receipt for your records, and confirm with the title company that the deed went to the Cook County recording division the same week.

Frequently asked questions

How much is the Skokie transfer tax?

The village charges $3 per $1,000 of property value, or any fraction. State tax of $0.50 per $500 and Cook County tax of $0.25 per $500 apply on top.

Does Skokie inspect houses before a sale?

Only rental property. The village will not issue a transfer stamp for a rental until an inspection is done and violations are fixed. Schedule it at least 28 days before closing.

Who arranges the final water reading in Skokie?

The seller submits a Request for Final Water Reading with the transfer tax paperwork. The Clerk's Office takes the package at transfertax@skokie.org.

Can I sell a Skokie house with code violations?

You can sell it, but the village will not issue the transfer stamp while code violations or village balances remain open. Clear them first, or ask the Clerk's Office at 847-933-8203 how an open item affects your closing.

Which county records a Skokie deed?

Cook County. The Cook County Clerk's recording division collects the state and county stamps, and the deed needs the village stamp as well. Your title company normally handles the filing.

Ways to sell a house in Palatine

Three routes exist: hire a listing agent, sell it yourself, or take an offer from a cash buyer. Listing gives the widest exposure but means showings, buyer financing and repair requests after inspection. An investor paying cash will accept the property in its current condition and can set closing around your calendar, which suits a house with deferred maintenance, tenants in place, or a probate timeline.

Palatine is a mostly residential village in the northwest Chicago suburbs, mainly in Cook County with a portion in Lake County. Population was 67,908 in 2020 and is 65,842 now, about 3 percent lower. Much of the housing was built in the decades after 1950, and buyers of houses that age tend to ask about roofs, furnaces and basements first.

  • Gather the deed, the last tax bill, any permit records and the rental license if the house was leased.
  • Ask the title company which county and municipality your parcel belongs to.
  • Compare any offer to what a listed sale would net after repairs, carrying costs and fees.

Owners, renters and investors

Roughly two of every three Palatine homes are owner-occupied. With median rent at $1,549 and about a third of units not owner-occupied, some buyers are investors who lease houses out. An investor can price repairs into an offer, which is why an as-is sale can draw interest here.

Which repairs need a Palatine building permit?

The village issues two kinds of permit. Express covers small, listed projects on detached single-family homes, with a stated goal of review within 5 business days. Standard covers larger work, with a goal of 10 to 15 business days. The Building and Inspection Services Division at 200 E. Wood Street answers questions at 847-359-9042.

These projects need a permit:

  • Building or replacing a deck, shed, roof or fence.
  • Installing or replacing an air conditioner, furnace or water heater.
  • Finishing or remodeling a basement, kitchen or bathroom.
  • Adding or altering the electrical system, or replacing an electric stove with a gas model.
  • Drainage work, including regrading and connecting a downspout or sump pump to buried pipe.

Painting, installing flooring, replacing a faucet and swapping a window or door of the same size in the same opening usually do not. If a past owner did permit-required work without one, ask the division how to resolve it before a buyer's inspector finds it. Pull your permit records together early, because a buyer will ask for them whenever a roof, furnace or basement has been redone.

Wet basements and drainage

The village sits in wooded marshland where several streams begin. Most drain to Salt Creek, which rises at Wilke Marsh on the east side, while the northeast corner drains to Buffalo Creek and a small piece of the southeast to McDonald Creek. Wet basements, sump pumps and grading are therefore routine inspection topics.

If your house has had water in the basement, a buyer will want to see repair records and any permit for drainage work. Drainage work is on the permit list above, so check that it was done with one. Selling as is to a cash buyer avoids the repair negotiation, though the buyer will still price the problem into the offer.

What to do before you take offers

A little preparation shortens the sale, whichever route you choose. Start with the paperwork, because most delays in a Palatine closing trace back to a missing record, not to the house itself.

  1. Find the deed and the most recent tax bill, and note which county the bill comes from.
  2. Collect permit records for any roof, furnace, water heater, deck or basement work, and invoices for drainage or sump pump repairs.
  3. If the house was rented, locate the Rental Dwelling License and the current lease, and decide whether the tenant stays.
  4. Ask your title company to confirm the county and municipality from the parcel number.
  5. Request offers, and compare each one with what a listing would net after repairs, carrying costs and fees.

A cash buyer can usually move through this list faster because the offer does not depend on a lender's appraisal or on the buyer's inspection list. A listed sale gives you more time in the market and may bring a higher price, but expect to repair or credit what the inspector finds.

Does Palatine require a rental license?

Yes. Under Chapter 12 of the village code, every residential rental, including single-family homes, townhomes and condominiums, must be inspected and carry an annual Rental Dwelling License. The program dates to 1990.

An owner applies through the Citizen Self Service portal, pays the invoice, calls for an inspection, and attends a landlord seminar while adopting a Palatine lease addendum. The license expires one year after the application date and renews automatically unless the owner asks to close it.

If a tenant lease runs past your closing date, tell buyers whether the license is current. If an investor buys the house, the new owner starts the licensing steps for that address. Ask the village how to close your license once the sale is done.

Transfer taxes and recording

Palatine has no village transfer tax. The taxes that remain are the state and county ones, collected at recording. The state rate is 50 cents per $500 and the county rate is 25 cents per $500. A deed for a sale needs the state transfer declaration (PTAX-203), which is filed through the state's MyDec system.

One detail trips people up. Some Palatine mailing addresses are actually in Rolling Meadows, which charges its own transfer tax. A Palatine address does not guarantee a Palatine location, so have the title company confirm the municipality from the parcel number. If your parcel sits in Lake County instead of Cook, you record with the Lake County Clerk's Recording Division.

Palatine also has a Metra station on the Union Pacific Northwest Line, and a downtown rebuilt since December 1999 with a passenger station, a parking garage, condominiums and rowhouses near the tracks. Commuting is the village's selling point, so mention the walk or drive to the station in your listing.

Frequently asked questions

Does Palatine charge a real estate transfer tax?

No village transfer tax applies. Illinois and the county still collect their own transfer taxes at recording, at 50 cents per $500 for the state and 25 cents per $500 for the county.

Which county records a Palatine deed?

Most of the village is in Cook County, so the Cook County Clerk's recording office handles those parcels. A portion lies in Lake County, and those parcels are recorded by the Lake County Clerk's Recording Division. Your title company can confirm which one applies from the parcel number.

Is a permit needed for a new roof or water heater in Palatine?

Yes. Building or replacing a roof, and installing or replacing a water heater, furnace or air conditioner, all need a permit. Express review is aimed at 5 business days. Call 847-359-9042 if you are unsure about a specific job.

Do I have to license a Palatine house I rent out before selling?

If it is rented, it needs an annual Rental Dwelling License under the village's Chapter 12 program. The license lasts one year from the application date and renews automatically unless you ask to close it.

Will anyone buy a Palatine house that needs work?

Yes. Many buyers, especially investors, purchase older Palatine houses as they are. Expect a buyer to price in roof, furnace, drainage and permit issues, so gather your permit records and any repair invoices before you ask for offers.

Selling in Des Plaines?

Ways to sell a house in Des Plaines

An owner in Des Plaines can hire a broker, go it alone, or take cash from a purchaser who buys the house as it is. Repair needs, tenants in the unit and a firm closing date tend to decide which path fits.

  • A full listing can fetch strong prices where the middle home value is $335,600, but it brings showings, an appraisal and repair requests.
  • Selling alone skips the commission and makes the contract and disclosures your job.
  • A cash deal shortens the calendar and suits estates, rentals and houses with postponed maintenance.

Because Des Plaines sits beside O'Hare and two tollways, buyers range from commuters to investors who want rentals near the airport and the Metra line.

Whichever you choose, ask each buyer or agent for a written net figure that subtracts the transfer taxes, recording fees, repairs and months of carrying costs. A higher headline price can leave you with less than a lower, faster offer.

Des Plaines housing costs

Des Plaines is a Cook County city just north of O'Hare International Airport, with 58,772 residents, down 3.1 percent from 2020. Owners live in most homes.

Des Plaines housing figures, 2020 to 2024
MeasureDes Plaines
Middle value of homes their owners occupy$335,600
Owner-occupied share of housing units78.3%
Median gross monthly rent$1,606
Number of households22,537

Because 92.3 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier, few houses change hands, which leaves sellers with fewer recent nearby sales as price guides. Ask an agent or cash buyer to show the sales they used.

Fewer sales also means a buyer paying cash may negotiate harder, because the comparison pool is thin. A written offer with a firm closing date gives you something concrete to weigh against a longer listing.

Flooding and storms

A buyer or lender will ask about flooding, and the Des Plaines River runs just east of downtown. Disclose any basement water or insurance claims and keep your repair receipts. The O'Hare station nearby averages 38.4 inches of snowfall, which is hard on roofs and gutters, so expect inspectors to look closely there.

One local quirk affects sellers: addresses inside city limits use the Des Plaines numbering system, while unincorporated parts of Maine Township with a Des Plaines mailing address follow Chicago's grid. Confirm with the city whether your parcel is incorporated, since that decides which city rules and which transfer tax apply.

Spring storms can turn severe here too, so inspectors and insurers may ask about roof age and past storm repairs. Keep records of any shingle, gutter or sump pump work you have done, and hand them to the buyer along with the disclosure report.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Des Plaines house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Cook County recording and transfer taxes

A Des Plaines deed is recorded by the Cook County Clerk's recording division at 118 North Clark Street in Chicago. A deed costs $107, a total that folds in the GIS, document storage and rental housing support fees, plus $5 per document for mail-back recording.

Three layers of transfer tax can apply, and the seller is the party liable on each:

  • State of Illinois: .50 per $500.00 of value, matching the rate in 35 ILCS 200/31-10.
  • Cook County: .25 per $500.00.
  • City of Des Plaines: 2.00 per $1,000.00, evidenced by a rubber stamp, with a $10.00 fee for exempt transfers.

Phone the city at 847-391-5325 to confirm the stamp before closing. Your contract can shift who pays, so ask the closing agent to show each line on the settlement statement.

The recording office accepts mail-back requests and the title company can usually submit the deed electronically, so you rarely need to travel downtown yourself. If the deed or declaration has an error, recording can be rejected and the closing delayed, which is why the title company reviews both before you sign.

Property tax bills and appeals

Cook County splits the year's tax into two bills. The first equals 55 percent of last year's total and is typically due March 1, while homeowner and senior exemptions show up on the second. Interest on late payments runs 1.5 percent monthly.

Values come from the Cook County Assessor, and Maine Township, which covers parts of Des Plaines, is reassessed on a three-year cycle. Appeals go first to the Assessor and then to the Board of Review, each with its own window that moves by township every year. Check the Assessor's calendar for the next opening.

Have the PIN ready when you talk to the Treasurer or Assessor, because Cook County identifies every parcel by a 14-digit number. Your closing agent will explain how the year's bill is divided at the table.

If the second bill is unpaid when you sell, the balance comes out of your proceeds at closing. Ask the title company for the payoff figure before you set a closing date, and check that any homeowner or senior exemption was applied, since a missing exemption raises the bill you and the buyer are splitting.

Rentals and repair permits before a sale

Rental owners in Des Plaines need a rental license, and an ordinance passed on February 2, 2009 makes them complete Phase 1 of the Crime Free Multi-Housing Program. A first-time license applicant must attend the seminar beforehand.

Repair permits are filed online through the city's self-service portal, and express guides exist for sheds, decks, fences, driveways, roofs and non-structural kitchen or bath remodels. The 2021 I-Codes took effect January 1, 2026, and construction hours are 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Monday through Saturday and 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Sunday. Inspections of rental dwellings or permitted work are booked at 847-391-5382 or permits@desplainesil.gov.

Closing out open permits before listing keeps unfinished work from surfacing late in a sale. Construction work in the city also needs a registered contractor, and registration runs through the same online portal, so confirm a contractor is registered before repairs start.

If you plan to sell a rental, the city's rental dwelling inspection line is a useful first call, since it lets you learn what an inspector would flag before a buyer's inspector does.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Des Plaines houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

From contract to closing

Once you accept an offer, the title company orders a search, prepares the deed and collects the transfer tax payments. You will sign the deed and a settlement statement, and the lender or lienholder is paid off from the proceeds. Cash buyers skip the appraisal and lender review, which is where most of the delay in a financed sale comes from.

Gather your PIN, your latest tax bill, any permit paperwork and, for a rental, the license and leases before you accept. If the sale involves a rental with tenants, ask the buyer in writing whether they will keep the tenants and how deposits will be credited.

Frequently asked questions

Who is liable for transfer tax on a Des Plaines sale?

The seller is shown as liable for the state, county and city taxes. Your contract can allocate it differently, so confirm with your closing agent.

Where is a Des Plaines deed filed?

With the Cook County Clerk's recording division at 118 North Clark Street in Chicago. Title companies can also submit deeds electronically.

Is a license needed to lease my Des Plaines house?

Yes. Rental property owners must obtain a license and complete the Crime Free Multi-Housing seminar before a new license is issued.

Does a Des Plaines mailing address mean I am in the city?

Not always. Some unincorporated Maine Township addresses carry a Des Plaines mailing address but follow Chicago's numbering. Ask the city to confirm that your parcel is within the limits.

When can I appeal my Des Plaines assessment?

Cook County sets new filing windows by township each year, first with the Assessor and then with the Board of Review. Check the Assessor's assessment calendar for the next opening.

How can you sell a house fast in Orland Park?

Orland Park sellers have three practical routes: a traditional listing, a sale without an agent, or a direct cash purchase. A cash buyer can close the fastest, while a listing often brings the highest price for a house in good order.

Orland Park is a village 25 miles southwest of Chicago, and most of it lies in Cook County with a small piece in Will County. Population is 57,954. Most of the present housing arrived after 1960, and owners live in 85.8% of homes.

  • List with an agent when the roof, furnace and kitchen are in decent shape and you can wait through showings and a buyer's mortgage approval.
  • Sell it yourself when you are comfortable negotiating and coordinating with a title company and the village.
  • Take a cash offer when the house needs repairs, a probate is pending, or a tenant must be dealt with. Compare it against a listing price less commission, repairs and months of carrying costs.

Registering a rental before a sale

The village runs a rental registration program, and it applies to single-family homes, townhomes and condominiums as well as apartment buildings. The annual fee is $100 per unit for a detached or attached single-family residence and $100 plus $15 per additional unit for a multi-family building.

  • Inspections follow the village's tri-annual schedule, and a rental housing sticker is issued when the unit passes.
  • Landlords or their agents must attend one eight-hour Crime Free Housing seminar from the police department.
  • Every lease must carry the village's Crime Free Lease Addendum, signed by each tenant age 18 or older.

When a rental is part of the sale, tell the buyer whether the unit is registered and when the last inspection took place. Development Services answers registration questions at (708) 403-5300.

Water service and the private line

The village bills water every two months, and a high bill should be reviewed by calling 708-403-6175. Property owners are responsible for the private water line from the shut-off valve, usually in the parkway, to the house, plus any leaks inside.

If a buyer's inspection finds a leak on that line, the repair is yours to make or to credit. Check the meter and the line before you list, and keep the bill history to show that the usage is normal. A buyer who sees a clean history is less likely to ask for a credit, and a cash buyer will usually take the line as it is.

How do Cook County taxes work for an Orland Park sale?

Property tax comes from Cook County. Orland Township is in the 2023 and 2026 reassessment group, and the township assessor's office is at 14807 S. Ravinia Ave., phone (708) 403-4222. Cook County bills in two installments, so ask the Treasurer for the next due dates and for a copy of your bill. Then ask your closing agent how the year's tax is prorated between you and the buyer.

A small part of Orland Park lies in Will County. If your house is in that part, ask the Will County treasurer for the schedule on your bill. Check the county named on your tax bill before you call, so you reach the right office.

Steps for an Orland Park seller

Selling a house in Orland Park comes down to a short sequence, and doing it in order saves time.

  1. Decide whether the house is a good candidate for a listing or whether repairs, a probate or a tenant point toward a cash sale.
  2. If a tenant lives there, check that the unit is registered with the village and gather the inspection sticker and the signed Crime Free Lease Addendum.
  3. Walk the water line from the shut-off valve in the parkway to the house, and look for leaks inside.
  4. Find your tax bill, note whether it comes from Cook County or Will County, and call the right treasurer for the schedule.
  5. Ask your title company about village charges and get them in writing before the closing date.
  6. Confirm the school boundary for your street so your listing sheet is correct.

A cash buyer takes the house as it stands, so you skip the repair requests that follow a buyer's inspection, and the wait for a lender's approval. A listing gives you more time on the market and a chance at a higher price, but the same village paperwork applies either way.

Parks and neighborhood features buyers ask about

Buyers mostly ask about parks, shopping and the village's recreation facilities. The village lists more than 60 parks, and Centennial Park holds the Aquatic Center with six water slides, Lake Sedgwick with boardwalks and pedal boats, and a free outdoor ice rink that runs from November to March. The Sportsplex on 159th Street is the largest indoor recreation building.

Shopping centers include Orland Square Mall and Orland Park Crossing. A listing that names the nearest park and shopping center gives a buyer something concrete to picture.

Which school serves your street?

Most of the Cook County part of Orland Park is in Orland School District 135, and all of it feeds Consolidated High School District 230, whose Carl Sandburg High School serves most of the village. Addresses in the northern edge may instead be zoned to Stagg or Victor J. Andrew high schools, so confirm the exact school for your street.

Four elementary districts reach Orland Park in Cook County: District 135, Community Consolidated District 146, Palos District 118 and Kirby District 140. In Will County, Mokena School District 159 and Lincoln-Way Community High School District 210 cover homes in the village. A listing that names the nearest park, Metra station and school boundary answers the questions buyers raise first.

Transfer charges and closing steps

Ask the village finance office and your title company which village charges apply to your closing, and get the figures in writing before the closing date. Cook County reassesses each township every three years, so a new notice arrives in the reassessment year and the township assessor can answer questions about it.

Metra's SouthWest Service stops at 143rd Street, 153rd Street and 179th Street, and Interstate 80 forms the southern edge of the village. Commuters like both, so mention the distance to the nearest station in your listing, along with the main roads: La Grange Road, 159th Street and Harlem Avenue.

Frequently asked questions

Does Orland Park charge a transfer tax when I sell?

Ask the village finance office and your title company which village charges apply to your closing, and get the figures in writing before the closing date.

Which county bills property tax in Orland Park?

Cook County, for almost all of the village. A small part sits in Will County and is billed there. Check the county named on your tax bill.

Do I have to register a rental house in Orland Park before selling it?

If it is rented, yes, the village requires annual registration at $100 per unit for a single-family home, with inspections on a tri-annual schedule. Share the registration and inspection records with the buyer.

Where do I report a high final water bill in Orland Park?

Call the village water billing line at 708-403-6175. The village bills two months at a time, and owners are responsible for leaks on the private line and inside the house.

How is Orland Park's reassessment schedule set?

Cook County reassesses each township every three years. Orland Township is in the 2023 and 2026 group, so a new notice arrives in the reassessment year and the township assessor can answer questions.

Selling in Oak Lawn

Oak Lawn has several local steps: a village transfer stamp, a point-of-sale sewer inspection for houses, and a stamp refund program for some sellers. Each step has its own form, so starting early protects the closing date.

The village borders Chicago on the southwest side. Population is 56,450 (July 2025 estimate), the median owner-occupied value is $281,200, and 82.5% of homes are owner-occupied. Most homes sit on compact lots. Mean travel time to work is 30.8 minutes. The sections below follow the order of a typical sale: the village stamp, the sewer inspection, refunds, Cook County recording and property tax.

The Oak Lawn transfer stamp

The village tax is 5.00 per 1,000 of value, enacted January 1, 1982, with the seller liable and an exemption letter attached to the recording as proof. Exempt transfers pay no fee. The village adds that senior sellers of a primary residence are now exempt, with the rules in section 3 of its exemption list.

  • Request stamps or an exemption letter from the Finance Department. The village accepts only electronic fillable forms, and handwritten forms are rejected.
  • Questions go to 708-499-7775 or transferstamps@oaklawn-il.gov.
  • A Utility Billing Account Change form handles the water account.
  • The village's own address is 9446 S. Raymond St., phone 708.636.4400.

State and county taxes sit on top: 50 cents per $500 for the state under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, and 25 cents per $500 for Cook County.

Point-of-sale sewer inspection

Oak Lawn requires a sewer inspection, called I&I, for single-family homes and qualifying townhomes before the transfer stamp. Schedule it well ahead of closing.

  1. Use the village's online permit portal, search the property address, choose Residential and the Transfer Stamp Sewer Inspection (I&I) permit type, and enter N/A for work details.
  2. The village reviews the request and emails either a record number with a scheduling link or a note that no inspection is needed.
  3. Pick a date for the I&I Sewer inspection. It happens between 10am and 2pm, and someone over 18 must be present with access to the interior.
  4. After the inspection, a payment link arrives by email for $100, and the results follow once payment is made.

Ask the Finance Department at 708-499-7775 whether your address needs the inspection, since the village screens each request first.
