Transfer stamp refunds

Village ordinance 3-2-7 allows a refund in three cases. Each requires the seller to have owned and lived in the house as a principal residence without renting any part of it.

Oak Lawn stamp refund cases
Refund caseWho qualifies
ReinvestmentSeller buys or builds a single-family home or condominium inside the village within one year of paying the tax, and lives there
Senior citizenOne-time refund for a seller age 65 or older who owned and occupied the home for more than one year, with a rule for co-owners under 60
Family saleSale to a child, parent, grandparent, brother, sister or grandchild, step relatives included

Refund requests are due within one year of the sale. Packets for each case are linked from the village's refund page, and the Finance Department's refund line is 708-499-7777.

Cook County recording and property tax

Oak Lawn deeds are recorded with the Cook County Clerk's recordings office at 118 N. Clark St. The seller is liable for both the state and county stamps, and a PTAX-203 declaration accompanies the deed.

For assessments, look up your 14-digit PIN on the Cook County Assessor's site to see your township. The south and west suburban townships follow a triennial reassessment cycle. Ask the Cook County Treasurer for installment status on the parcel, and expect the title company to prorate the year's bill at closing.

Schools, transit and parks

Elementary schools include Kolb, Lieb, Harnew, Columbus Manor, Covington, Hannum, Hometown, Kolmar and Sward, with Simmons and Oak Lawn-Hometown as middle schools. Oak Lawn Community High School and Harold L. Richards High School are the two public high schools. Metra's SouthWest Service runs from the Oak Lawn station toward downtown Chicago, and Advocate Christ Medical Center is one of the largest hospitals in the state.

The village maintains 22 parks on more than 300 acres, with outdoor pools, an indoor ice arena, two fitness centers, an indoor racquet center and an 18-hole golf course. The median owner cost with a mortgage is $2,000 a month, a useful point when a buyer weighs a house here against a rental.

Which sale route fits?

An updated house near 95th Street or the Metra station usually does well in a listing. A house with sewer problems, an old rental history or an estate behind it often fits a direct as-is sale better, since the inspection and stamp steps still apply either way.

Whichever route you take, work in this order: confirm with Finance whether the sewer inspection applies, book it, pay the $100 fee, request the stamp or exemption letter, and then send the stamped deed and PTAX-203 to the Cook County Clerk. If you may qualify for a refund, keep your closing statement and the packet deadline in mind, since requests are due within one year of the sale.

What to have ready for Finance

Before you contact the Finance Department, have the property address, the names of the buyer and seller, and the Cook County PIN in hand. Say whether the property is a single-family home, a townhome or another type, since that decides whether the sewer inspection applies. Say also whether the seller is 65 or older and whether the house was ever rented, because both change which exemption or refund path fits.

Fill in the village's electronic forms on screen. Handwritten forms are rejected, and a rejected form costs days you may not have. For the water account, submit the Utility Billing Account Change form so the final bill lands with you and the new owner starts clean.

When the inspection is done and the payment link is paid, the results arrive by email. Keep them with your closing file. The buyer's lender or attorney may ask to see them, and the stamp step depends on them.

If you are selling to a relative, mention it at the start. The family sale refund is its own packet with its own paperwork, and it is easier to gather the proof of relationship before closing than after. The same goes for a seller who plans to buy again in the village: keep both closing statements so the reinvestment refund can be claimed within the one-year window.

Frequently asked questions

Does Oak Lawn charge a transfer tax?

Yes. The village rate is 5.00 per 1,000 of value, paid by the seller, with exempt transfers needing an exemption letter. Contact the Finance Department at 708-499-7775 for the stamp.

What does the Oak Lawn sewer inspection cost?

The village charges $100, paid by a link emailed after the inspection. It applies to single-family homes and qualifying townhomes and runs between 10am and 2pm.

Are seniors exempt from the transfer stamp?

The village states that seniors selling a primary residence are now exempt, with details in section 3 of its exemption list. A separate refund route exists for sellers 65 or older under ordinance 3-2-7.

How long do I have to ask for a stamp refund?

Refunds must be requested within one year of the date of sale. The village lists reinvestment, senior and immediate family cases, each with its own packet.

Where is an Oak Lawn deed recorded?

With the Cook County Clerk's recordings office at 118 N. Clark St., phone 312.603.5050. The sale also needs the PTAX-203 declaration and stamped deed.

Selling in Mount Prospect

Mount Prospect is a Cook County village about 20 miles northwest of downtown Chicago and roughly 4 miles north of O'Hare Airport. A sale here can carry transfer charges at three levels: state, county and village. The village stamp is its own step, separate from county recording, so schedule it early.

Population is 55,395 (July 2025 estimate). The typical owner-occupied home is worth $397,400, and 68.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Owners usually choose between an agent, an investor who pays cash, or a sale handled alone, and the facts below apply to all three.

Transfer taxes on a Mount Prospect sale

The Cook County Clerk lists two charges: the State of Illinois at fifty cents for each $500, and Cook County at twenty-five cents for each $500. The seller is the liable party on both. The state figure matches 35 ILCS 200/31-15.

The village adds a real estate transfer tax of its own, paid by buying a stamp. The Finance Department offers an online stamp application and in-person stamps by appointment. It also has a rebate form and an affidavit of no consideration for exempt transfers such as taking a person off a deed. Call Finance for the current village rate and who pays it.

The Clerk's site also has a lookup showing the transfer fee for each municipality in the county. Put all three charges in your net sheet early.

Cook County property tax bills

Cook County splits each year's property tax into two bills. For tax year 2025 the due dates were April 1, 2026 and October 1, 2026, and both are behind us. Other years landed on other days, so rely on the date printed on your own bill.

The title company typically splits the year's tax between buyer and seller from the latest bill, so bring that bill and your parcel number to the closing. The Treasurer's office describes homeowner, senior, senior freeze, disability and disabled veteran exemptions that a qualifying buyer may look into afterward.

The village also runs a property tax relief grant for qualifying single-family owners, a rebate on part of the village share of the county bill. Call Finance to learn whether it is open before counting on it.

Which school district is your house in?

Several elementary districts divide the village, and the district for your address often matters more to buyers than the village name. Confirm it before you advertise.

  • Central Mount Prospect: Mount Prospect School District 57.
  • North and somewhat east: River Trails School District 26.
  • South and somewhat west: Elk Grove Community Consolidated School District 59.
  • Small northern, north central and northwest pockets: Buffalo Grove-Wheeling CCSD 21, Arlington Heights District 25 and Prospect Heights District 23.

Township High School District 214 covers the whole village. Park services also vary by address, with the Mount Prospect, Arlington Heights, Des Plaines, Prospect Heights and River Trails park districts all serving parts of the village.

Transit and location

Commuters board Metra's Union Pacific Northwest Line in the village: southeast to Ogilvie Transportation Center, northwest toward Harvard and McHenry. Pace buses cover local routes. The Metra station and the closeness to O'Hare are the location points most listings lead with, and Randhurst Village is the best-known shopping address.

The climate brings muggy summers and snowy winters, which is why inspectors look hard at roofs, sump pumps and furnaces. Have those three in good order before showings.

Disclosures and village rules

Illinois puts the disclosure duty in 765 ILCS 77/20: the report is completed and delivered before a contract is signed. Local buyers also ask about permit history on additions, finished basements and mechanical work.

The Village Code is posted online, and Community Development is the office for permit, inspection and code questions. For a rental, ask the village what license or inspection covers your address before you list.

  • Request permit records for work done during your ownership.
  • Resolve open code notices, since an unresolved notice can complicate the closing.

Any past basement water belongs on the report, with repair invoices on hand.

Agent, owner sale or cash buyer

Listing through an agent reaches the most people, with showings, inspections and a lender's schedule attached. An updated house in a favored school zone may draw competing offers.

  • Agent: fits a house that shows well and an owner able to wait out a standard closing.
  • Owner sale: skips the listing fee but leaves the disclosure form, contract and stamp paperwork to you.
  • Cash buyer: fewer conditions and a closing date you may help choose, at an offer reduced for needed repairs.

Whichever you pick, get the offer on paper and settle who pays each transfer charge. Then gather the latest tax bill, parcel number, permit records and any payoff statement so the title company can set the closing date.

From offer to closing in Mount Prospect

A sale here runs in a handful of steps, and most delays come from paperwork that waited until the last week.

  1. Sign the contract and settle who pays each transfer charge: state, county and village.
  2. Deliver the Illinois disclosure report before the contract is signed, with repair invoices for any past basement water.
  3. Contact Finance about the village transfer stamp. Ask whether it is bought online or in person by appointment, and what the current rate is.
  4. Bring your latest Cook County tax bill and parcel number to the title company so it can split the year's tax between buyer and seller.
  5. Pay off any loan, confirm the water, sewer and refuse account is settled with the village, and record the deed with the county.

A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting schedule, which is why the closing date is often the part you control. If the deed only removes a person, such as after a divorce, ask Finance about the affidavit of no consideration instead of the standard stamp.

Keep copies of everything you sign. If a question comes up later about permits, taxes or the water account, those papers are your answer, and a buyer's attorney will ask for several of them anyway.

What to bring to Finance and the title company

Before you call Finance, have the property address and parcel number ready, along with the name on the deed and the name of the buyer. If the transfer has no price, say so up front, because that points to the affidavit of no consideration. If the deed is a standard sale, ask whether the village stamp can be bought online or whether you need to book an in-person appointment, and how far ahead of closing to do it.

The title company will want the latest tax bill, the payoff figure for any loan, and a list of any open code notices or permits. Handing these over together saves a round of calls and keeps the closing date from slipping.

Frequently asked questions

Does Mount Prospect have its own transfer tax?

Yes. Finance sells the village's transfer stamps, online or in person by appointment. Ask it for the current rate and who pays, because the village sets this apart from the state and county charges.

How much is the Cook County transfer fee?

Cook County charges twenty-five cents per $500 and the state charges fifty cents per $500, with the seller liable for each.

Which school district is my Mount Prospect house in?

It depends on the address. Central areas are in District 57, north and east areas in River Trails District 26, south and west areas in District 59, and small northern pockets in Districts 21, 25 and 23. Township High School District 214 covers the whole village.

What if I need to remove someone from a Mount Prospect deed?

Finance has an affidavit declaring no consideration for exempt transfers like taking a person off a deed. Ask Finance whether your situation qualifies.

When are Cook County property taxes due?

Tax year 2025 bills were due April 1, 2026 and October 1, 2026. Other years use different dates, so check your own bill.

Sell My House Fast in Tinley Park, IL: Options, Costs and Cash Offers

Cash Home Buyers in Illinois

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Tinley Park, IL sale

Sell Your Tinley Park House for Cash

Tell us about your Tinley Park house.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Tinley Park?
We buy Tinley Park houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Ways to sell a Tinley Park house

A Tinley Park owner can list with a broker, market the house alone, or sell as-is to a buyer paying cash. Each route ends the same way, with a deed recorded at the county, but the time and the conditions along the way differ a lot.

  • A listing reaches the most buyers, though a buyer's lender may ask for an appraisal and repairs.
  • Selling on your own saves the commission, and you handle showings, the contract and the paperwork.
  • A cash buyer takes the house as it stands. Without a mortgage there is no underwriting to wait on, so title work, payoff letters and the closing date you agree on set the pace.

Cash Home Buyers CA is built for the third route: you describe the house, and you decide whether the offer works for you.

Tinley Park at a glance

Tinley Park is a southern suburb of Chicago with 55,971 residents in 2020 and an estimated 55,140 in July 2025. It holds 22,320 households of about 2.45 people each, and 86.9% of occupied homes are owner-occupied. The middle value of an owned home is $299,900, and the middle rent is $1,495 a month. Most residents stay put: 92.0% lived in the same home a year earlier.

The 2020 count showed 22,751 housing units with 3.3% vacant. That is a tight market, and it tends to favor sellers whose homes are in decent shape.

Cook County or Will County?

The village straddles two counties, and the one that holds your parcel number sends the tax bill, hears assessment appeals and records the deed, whatever the village line says. Cook County covers the townships of Bremen, Orland and Rich. Will County covers Frankfort Township, including the Brookside Marketplace area.

Look at your latest tax bill to see which county you are in, then call that county's treasurer to ask where the account stands. Note the township from the parcel record too, since it matters when you look up an assessment or a past appeal.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Tinley Park house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Property tax due dates and exemptions

Cook County's installment dates move from year to year. The first installment was due March 4 in 2025 for tax year 2024, and the Treasurer's Office posts each new schedule on its due dates page. Check it before you set a closing date so you know which installment is open and who pays it.

The Treasurer also lists exemptions Cook owners can apply for: homeowner, senior citizen, senior assessment freeze, disability, home improvement, military, disabled veteran and first responder's surviving spouse. If you qualify, the savings can stay with you until you sell.

Selling with taxes owed

On the Will County side, delinquent taxes become a lien that tax buyers purchase at an annual sale. Homeowners typically have one to three years to redeem before a buyer can start court action. That window is real money and real time, so talk to the Will County Treasurer early if you are behind.

A sale can clear the debt. Title work turns up the unpaid taxes, the payoff comes out of your proceeds at closing, and the deed goes to the buyer free of that balance. Ask for a payoff figure before you accept any offer so you know what you would net, and keep a copy of every letter the treasurer sends you.

Building Division permits

Most home improvements and additions call for building, electrical or plumbing permits. The Building Division asks owners to call 708-444-5100 before starting if they are unsure. A homeowner may do work on their own property, except that changing electric service needs an electrical contractor. Any contractor you hire must be bonded and registered with the village before work starts.

Permit basics for a Tinley Park home project
Permit stepWhat the village expects
ApplicationOne copy of your plat of survey, normally provided at closing, plus any drawings or sketches
During workBuilding permit placard posted at the site until the work is complete
InspectionsPlan-review consultant inspects weekday mornings until noon
No permitStarting without one can bring a fine

Unpermitted work can slow a sale, so sort it out before a buyer's inspector finds it. A cash buyer is usually more relaxed about it, but you still disclose what you know.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Tinley Park houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

If your mortgage is in default

The Building Division runs a Foreclosure Property Registration Program through ProChamps, with a separate page for defaulted mortgage property registration. If your lender has started foreclosure, ask the Building Division whether registration applies to you.

State law treats a few transfers differently. Under 765 ILCS 77/15, a borrower who hands the lender a deed in place of foreclosure, or who agrees to a consent judgment, is excused from the seller disclosure report. A regular sale still needs the report in the buyer's hands before signing, as 765 ILCS 77/20 requires.

Commercial buyers in the village use a separate Change of Use/Owner application with a $50 fee. It does not apply to homes.

What to gather before you sell

A little preparation shortens the whole process. Pull together your latest tax bill so you know which county and which township apply, your plat of survey from the original closing, and any permit paperwork for additions or remodels. If a lender holds a mortgage, ask for a payoff figure in writing.

Walk through the house with a notepad and jot down known problems such as the roof, furnace, foundation or water damage. The disclosure report has to reach the buyer before signing, and an advance list makes that form quick. If you owe taxes in either county, call that treasurer first so the number you hear is current.

Then compare your options side by side. A listing may bring a higher price but adds showings, an appraisal and repair requests. A cash sale trades some of that price for speed and fewer conditions. Which one wins depends on the condition of the house and how soon you must be finished.

What closing looks like

After you say yes to an offer, a title company combs the records for your parcel and flags every claim against it, such as unpaid taxes or a leftover mortgage. Payoff letters get requested, the disclosure report reaches the buyer, and both sides pick a closing date.

At the table you sign the deed and settlement papers. The lender gets paid, the rest is yours, and the county records the deed afterward. A cash buyer has no loan approval pending, so the calendar mostly follows the title work and your own plans.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Which county does a Tinley Park address belong to?

Either one. The village covers parts of Cook and Will counties, and the county named on your bill decides which treasurer and which recording office you deal with.

What are the tax installment dates for a Tinley Park house in Cook County?

They shift from year to year. The first installment was due March 4 in 2025 and April 1 in 2026, so check the Treasurer's due dates page for the current schedule.

Does a Tinley Park basement remodel need a permit?

Most improvements and additions need a permit of some kind. Call 708-444-5100 for the Building Division to confirm your project, and bring the plat of survey from your closing.

What if a Tinley Park owner gives the lender a deed in lieu?

The state exempts that kind of transfer from the seller disclosure report. The deed itself still gets recorded at the county.

How quickly can a cash buyer close on a Tinley Park house?

Title work, payoff letters and the agreed closing date set the pace. Without a mortgage there is no underwriting to wait on, and the county records the deed afterward.

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Berwyn, IL sale
  • Turn the Berwyn, IL offer down and you owe us nothing

Sell Your Berwyn House for Cash

Tell us about your Berwyn house.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Berwyn?
We buy Berwyn houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Selling a house in Berwyn

Berwyn is a dense inner-ring suburb in Cook County, packed into 3.90 square miles with Oak Park to the north, Cicero to the east, Stickney to the south, and Lyons, Riverside, North Riverside and Forest Park to the west. It calls itself the City of Homes, and the housing fits: small bungalows on the north side around Roosevelt and Cermak roads, larger houses toward the south, and plenty of duplexes and three-unit buildings in between.

Population is 55,001 as of July 1, 2025, down 3.9 percent from 57,235 in April 2020. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $299,800, 61.1 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and median gross rent is $1,215.

Before it was settled the area was grassy marshland, with Mud Lake reaching nearly to today's southern border, and the south end flooded often in heavy rain. Buyers' inspectors look hard at basements and sewer laterals. If your house has a history of flooding or sewer backup, pull together repair records and any sewer scope reports before you list.

What the city checks before a transfer

Berwyn handles its own transfer paperwork through the Collections and Licensing office and the Compliance Department at City Hall, 6700 W. 26th Street. The city's checklist for quit claim transfers shows what the offices look at. On a regular sale, ask the same departments which items apply to you.

  • Building: a property inspection is required when all parties are coming off title, and any fines or liens must be paid and open permits closed out.
  • Police: parking tickets and fines must be paid in full.
  • Water: the water bill balance must be current.
  • Collector: bring the original deed that will be recorded with Cook County, the completed Berwyn Declaration form and a payment of $100.00, payable to the City of Berwyn by cash, check, money order or credit card.
  • Trusts and corporations: add the trust agreement or corporate papers only if the property is coming out of the trust or corporation, and add an Attorney's Certification form when someone is added to or removed from title.

City stamps are processed at the counter or by mail. The counter is open Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday from 9 a.m. to half past four, and on Tuesday until half past seven in the evening. A mailed packet needs a return envelope with postage. The Compliance Department number is (708) 788-2660, extensions 6445 or 6449.

Certificate of compliance and occupancy

Berwyn issues a certificate of compliance and occupancy after a city inspection, and the fee depends on the type of building.

Residential certificate fees
Property typeFee
Single-family house$100.00
Two to three units$125.00
Four to six units$175.00
Each unit over six$70.00

Inspections are scheduled in person at the first-floor Compliance Department window in City Hall. Payment is due when you schedule, with no exceptions. Cash, check, money order and credit cards are accepted. The window opens at 9 a.m. every weekday, closes at 5 p.m. on four of them, and stays open until 8 p.m. on Tuesdays.

An inspection report stays valid for six months from the inspection date. Book it close to your target closing instead of months ahead, or you may pay for a second one. Ask the Compliance Department whether your sale needs a certificate at all, since the answer can depend on the building type and who is on title.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Berwyn house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Do I need a permit for past work?

Permits go out at the Building Permits Department until half past four on most weekdays and half past seven on Tuesdays. You can apply in person or email buildingpermits@berwyn-il.gov. Incomplete applications are not sent for director review, so check the forms before you submit.

Homeowners may do some non-commercial repairs themselves under the city's Work By Owner handout, and the city publishes guides on what needs a permit and on hiring contractors. The codes in force include the 2024 International Residential Code, the 2012 International Property Maintenance Code, the Illinois State Plumbing Code 2014 and the 2021 Illinois Energy Conservation Code.

Open permits have to be closed out before a transfer is processed. If a prior owner finished a basement or added a bathroom without a permit, sorting it out can take weeks. Ask for the permit file for your address early, then decide whether to finish the work, credit the buyer or sell as-is to someone who will complete it. Buyers who plan to rehab a property often accept the inspection list as part of an as-is price.

Recording the deed with Cook County

Cook County deeds are recorded by the Clerk's Recording Division at 118 N. Clark Street, Room 120, in person or by mail. The deed needs the property index number (PIN), the full legal description, the property address, a mail-to address, the grantee's name and address, the name and address for future tax bills, and city, state and county transfer tax declarations and stamps or a stated exemption.

The Clerk tells filers to check with the municipality for its own requirements, so Berwyn's declaration and payment are a separate step before recording. Illinois stamps have been $0.75 per $500.00 since September 15, 1989, split into $0.50 for the state and $0.25 for the county.

Only title companies may e-record deeds that carry consideration. Fully exempt deeds can be e-recorded by other filers. A document that misses the Clerk's format standards is charged an additional fee equal to the normal recording fee, so have the title company or your attorney check the deed before it goes in.

Assessments and tax bills

Cook County reassesses one-third of the county each year. A reassessment notice shows the PIN, characteristics, estimated market value and assessed value. Residential assessed value equals 10 percent of fair market value, then a state equalizer and exemptions are applied. You can appeal to the Assessor or to the Cook County Board of Review.

The Cook County Treasurer mails two installments a year, and the first installment is exactly 55 percent of the prior year's total. Recent due dates have moved around: tax year 2025 installments were due April 1, 2026 and October 1, 2026, and tax year 2024 installments were due March 4, 2025 and December 15, 2025. Read the Treasurer's due-date page or your own bill before you choose a closing day.

Exemptions on file include homeowner, senior citizen, senior assessment freeze, persons with disabilities and home improvement. Check which ones your bill shows, because they affect the proration at closing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Berwyn houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

If you sell for cash

A cash sale skips the lender's underwriting and appraisal, but not the city's steps. The inspection, the water balance, parking fines, open permits and the transfer declaration still apply to a Berwyn house, so start those calls while you compare offers.

A cash buyer who takes the house as-is can agree to finish permit work or repairs after closing. Get that written into the contract, along with who pays for the certificate and the city payment. Ask whether the buyer will close on a date that fits the six-month inspection window.

Frequently asked questions

Does Berwyn require a city inspection to sell my house?

It depends on the transaction, so ask the Compliance Department at (708) 788-2660, extension 6445 or 6449. The quit claim checklist requires an inspection when all parties come off title, and a single-family certificate of compliance and occupancy costs $100.00.

How long is a Berwyn inspection report good for?

Six months from the inspection date. If closing slips past that window, plan on a new inspection and a new fee.

What is the transfer tax rate on a Cook County deed?

Illinois stamps run $0.75 per $500.00 of value, made up of $0.50 for the state and $0.25 for the county. Berwyn adds its own declaration and a city payment, so ask the Collector's office what applies to your transaction.

Where do I pay water and parking fines before closing?

Call the Water Department at (708) 788-2660, extension 6463 or 6466 for the balance, and the Police Department at (708) 795-5600 for parking tickets. Both must be current before the transfer goes through.

Can I sell a Berwyn house with open permits?

Open permits must be closed out for a transfer to be processed. Ask the Building Department for the permit file, then decide whether to finish the work, credit the buyer or sell as-is to a buyer who will complete it.

Sell My House Fast in Wheaton, IL: Options, Costs and Cash Offers

Cash Home Buyers in Illinois
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Wheaton, IL: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Wheaton, IL sale
  • Turn the Wheaton, IL offer down and you owe us nothing

Sell Your Wheaton House for Cash

Tell us about your Wheaton house.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Wheaton?
We buy Wheaton houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What is different about selling in Wheaton?

Wheaton adds a city transfer stamp to every sale, and the buyer pays for it. The city also wants the seller's final utility bill settled before the stamp is issued, so the two sides of a closing depend on each other. Wheaton is the DuPage County seat and sits about 25 miles west of Chicago, in Milton and Winfield Townships.

The same rules apply whether the house is listed, sold privately or bought for cash as-is. What changes is who files the stamp application and how early the final water reading is booked.

The Wheaton transfer stamp

The stamp costs $2.50 per $1,000 of full consideration, taken from line 11 of the Illinois MyDec PTAX-203 declaration, with the price rounded to the nearest thousand. The buyer, called the grantee, buys it. Illinois collects its own tax too, at half a dollar for each $500 of declared value (35 ILCS 200/31-10).

The city's Finance Department accepts stamp requests four ways:

  • Online through the transfer stamp portal, after creating an account.
  • By email to finance@wheaton.il.us.
  • By UPS or FedEx to the Finance Department at 303 W. Wesley St., Wheaton, IL 60187.
  • In person at City Hall, first floor.

Paper filings need a signed stamp application, a copy of the completed PTAX-203 or the deed, and a completed city utility account application form.

Exempt transfers

Most Wheaton sales are non-exempt because they carry money. The full list of exempt deeds sits in City Code Chapter 66, Article VII, Section 66-190, and these are common ones.

Common exemptions from the Wheaton transfer stamp
Exempt situationNote
Transfer to or from a trustStill needs a $0 value stamp
Actual consideration under $100.00Same $0 stamp
Property acquired by or from a governmental bodyDocumentation required
Buyer sold a Wheaton primary home and is buying a new principal residence in WheatonExemption 13
Buyer is the natural or adopted child of a sellerExemption 14

An exempt stamp carries a $25 administrative fee and needs a signed, notarized deed. Since October 1, 2025 Wheaton no longer pays transfer tax refunds. Situations that once qualified for a refund are now handled as exemptions when the stamp is bought, so supporting documents must be ready on the closing timeline.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Wheaton house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Seller duties before the stamp is issued

Call the city 5 to 7 days before closing to book a final water reading, at 630-260-2000 or waterbilling@wheaton.il.us. The final bill, or an estimate of it, then has to be paid in full. The city also checks for other unpaid charges.

  • Water, sanitary sewer and stormwater utility fees.
  • Inspection fees.
  • Building permit fees.
  • Property maintenance fines.

Because building permit fees and property maintenance fines are on the list, ask the city for a balance on your account a couple of weeks ahead and clear anything outstanding before the contract date.

Wheaton prices and households

Wheaton is an upper-priced market. The median home value is $455,700, median gross rent is $1,799 a month and median household income is $120,008. Owners live in 71.7% of the housing, across 19,588 households averaging 2.54 people. Population is estimated at 54,065 for July 2025, essentially level with the 2020 count of 53,970.

Monthly costs for owners average $2,764 with a mortgage and $1,138 without one, and 86.4% of residents had the same address a year earlier. Little turnover means few comparable sales, so pricing a house takes care.

Property taxes for a Wheaton seller

Wheaton parcels are billed by DuPage County. Taxes arrive a year behind, with bills mailed in spring and installments recently falling on June 1 and September 1. The general homestead and senior exemptions are each $8,000 on the county's current notice, and you should confirm both appear on your bill. For assessed value questions, the county treasurer points owners to the local assessor's number printed on the bill.

On the settlement statement the title company divides the unpaid tax for the year. State law also requires sellers of one to four residential units to hand over a completed disclosure report before a contract is signed (765 ILCS 77/20). For a rough house, that report is where known problems get written down.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Wheaton houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What can slow down a Wheaton closing?

Most delays come from the utility step or from a missing exemption record. The city will not issue the transfer stamp until the final utility bill is paid, so a late call to the utility office can hold up the stamp and the recording that follows.

  • Booking the final water reading later than the 5 to 7 day window the city requests.
  • Forgetting that the buyer, not the seller, submits the PTAX-203 copy and the utility account application.
  • Claiming an exemption without a notarized deed or supporting documents.
  • Leaving building permit fees or property maintenance fines unpaid.
  • Counting on a refund after closing, which the city no longer issues.

Sellers who need to leave quickly, such as an estate heir or an owner relocating for work, should line up these items with the title company the week the contract is signed.

From contract to closing day

Once the contract is signed, call the title company and ask who is filing the PTAX-203 and who is sending the stamp application. Book the final water reading inside the 5 to 7 day window, and settle any permit fees or maintenance fines with the city. Get your payoff letter from any lender.

On closing day you sign the deed, the lender is paid from your proceeds, and the stamped deed goes to DuPage County for recording. A cash buyer has no loan approval to wait on, so the stamp and the utility bill are usually the last items standing between you and the keys. Save the final utility receipt, since the city needs it before the stamp issues, and keep a copy of the stamped deed for your records.

Schools and neighborhoods

Most of Wheaton lies in Community Unit School District 200, feeding Wheaton North and Wheaton Warrenville South high schools. The northeast corner is in Glen Ellyn District 41 and one elementary school in the southeast belongs to District 89. The Union Pacific West Line runs through downtown, where the Wheaton Center apartment complex is a recognizable landmark. Mention the school district and the train when you describe the house.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Who pays the Wheaton transfer stamp, the buyer or the seller?

The buyer, also called the grantee, buys the stamp. The seller's job is to book the final water reading and pay the final utility bill, because the city will not issue the stamp until that bill is settled.

What is the Wheaton transfer stamp rate?

It is $2.50 per $1,000 of full consideration from line 11 of the PTAX-203, with the price rounded to the nearest thousand. Exempt deeds still need a $0 stamp and a $25 administrative fee.

How early should I schedule the final water reading in Wheaton?

Call 5 to 7 days before closing. The city's Finance Department takes requests at 630-260-2000 or waterbilling@wheaton.il.us, and the final bill must be paid before the stamp is issued.

Did Wheaton stop refunding transfer tax?

Yes, as of October 1, 2025. Buyers who would have qualified for a refund, such as a Wheaton homeowner moving to another Wheaton home or a child buying from a parent, now claim Exemption 13 or 14 when they apply for the stamp.

Which county handles property tax for Wheaton?

DuPage County. Its treasurer mails one bill with two installment coupons, and the county bills a year in arrears. Call the treasurer for the current due dates.

Selling in Normal

Normal is a town in McLean County, central Illinois, and forms the Bloomington-Normal pair with its neighbor Bloomington. Population is 53,275 (July 1, 2025 estimate). Illinois State University and Heartland Community College shape the market: only 54.8% of homes are owner-occupied, the median owner-occupied value is $213,600, median gross rent is $965, and 75.5% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Rentals are a normal part of the market, so the town's rules for rental licenses and short-term stays come up in many sales.

Uptown Normal, built around a roundabout, holds the town hall, the Amtrak station and the restored Normal Theater. The average trip to work takes 16.5 minutes.

Rental occupancy licenses

Multi-family rentals need a license. Section 11.8-1 of the Town code says no one may operate an apartment, rooming house, multiple-use dwelling, hotel, motel, bed and breakfast or duplex (except the owner-occupied side) without a rental occupancy license issued by the Building Commissioner.

  • Licenses run January 1 through December 31 of a year.
  • A license belongs to one owner and one property and cannot be transferred without a transfer fee and a completed application from the new owner.
  • A change of owner is one reason a license may be revoked.
  • An inspection takes place before any license is issued, and the owner must give the Town access to the units. A tenant or owner who refuses can face a search warrant request.
  • Appeals of a refusal or revocation go to the Building Commissioner within 30 days.
  • Penalties run from $25 to $200 for a first offense and $50 to $500 for later ones, with each day counted as a separate offense.

If you are selling a duplex or small apartment building, tell the buyer that the license does not move with the deed. The Inspections Department is at 1 Uptown Circle, phone 309-454-9581.

Short-term rental rules

Short-term rentals in Normal need a Town business license, under Ordinance 6028 passed on June 16, 2025. They are prohibited in R-1 and R-2 zoning unless the property is the owner-occupant's primary residence.

  • In R-1 zoning, no more than 2 unrelated people, or 1 family plus 1 unrelated person, may stay.
  • In R-2 and R-3 zoning, the limit is 4 unrelated people.
  • Parking is allowed only on hard surfaces, and street parking is capped at 24 hours unless a sign says otherwise.
  • Parties, meetings and other events are not allowed.
  • The Short-Term Rental Tax form and payment are due by the 25th of the month after collection.

The business license carries no fee, but the Town issues it only after taxes and debts owed to the Town are paid. If the house has been used as a short-term rental, ask the Town how the license and any tax account will be handled so the buyer does not inherit a balance.

Recording a deed in McLean County

The McLean County Clerk's Recording Division records deeds at 115 E. Washington Street, Room M104, in Bloomington. The phone is 309-888-5170 and the office is open Monday through Friday, 8 am to 4:30 pm.

Every deed must include:

  • A statement of exemption or a transfer tax declaration.
  • The name of the person who prepared it.
  • Where future tax statements are to be sent.
  • A notary seal, date and signature, with original signatures. Photocopies and digital signatures are not accepted.
  • A complete legal description with the permanent index number.
  • A complete return address.

Staff cannot give legal advice or legal descriptions, so have the deed prepared by an attorney or title company.

Jobs and commuting

Rivian builds all-electric vehicles at the former Diamond-Star Motors plant in Normal, its largest in the United States, which has changed the local job picture. Interstates 55, 74 and 39 serve the town, and U.S. 51, U.S. 150, Illinois Route 9 and historic Route 66 pass through. The Amtrak station at 11 Uptown Circle has four Lincoln Service trains a day in each direction between Chicago and St. Louis, and Connect Transit runs 16 fixed routes.

Schools

The town sits inside McLean County Unit District No. 5, which runs Normal Community High School, Normal Community West High School and Kingsley Junior High School. Illinois State University operates University High School and Thomas Metcalf Elementary. Private options include Epiphany Catholic School, Calvary Christian Academy, Cornerstone Christian Academy and Bloom Community School.

Weather and older houses

Normal gets about 39.4 inches of precipitation and 20.1 inches of snow a year. July highs average 86 degrees Fahrenheit and January lows about 16. That range is hard on roofs, gutters, window seals and furnaces. If your house is older, a recent roof receipt or a furnace service record answers some of the first questions a buyer's inspector will ask.

From listing to closing

Work through the sale in this order. First decide how to sell: an agent for a house that shows well, or a cash buyer if repairs, tenants or a license problem would slow a normal listing. Second, if the property is a rental, call the Inspections Department at 309-454-9581 about the license and the transfer fee the buyer will face. Third, have an attorney or title company prepare the deed to the county's list, with original notarized signatures and the permanent index number.

Finally, record the deed with the McLean County Clerk and keep the recorded copy. Before closing, ask the Town whether any short-term rental tax account or other balance is open, since the Town issues licenses only after debts are paid.

A cash sale skips showings, appraisal and lender timelines, but the license, tax and recording steps above stay the same.

If neither applies, because the house is owner-occupied or rented only under normal long-term arrangements outside these categories, the license questions drop away and the sale is mostly deed, title and closing paperwork. When you are unsure which category your property falls in, phone the Inspections Department at 309-454-9581 before listing. A clear answer in writing helps a buyer's lender and attorney, and it keeps a surprise from appearing in the last week before closing.

Yes. The rental occupancy license is specific to one owner and one property, so the buyer applies in their own name, pays a transfer fee and passes an inspection. Ask the Inspections Department at 309-454-9581 how that will be handled before closing.

Where do I record a deed for a Normal house?

At the McLean County Clerk's Recording Division, 115 E. Washington Street, Room M104, Bloomington, phone 309-888-5170. The deed needs a transfer tax declaration or exemption statement, original notarized signatures and a full legal description with the permanent index number.

Are short-term rentals allowed in Normal?

They are allowed with a Town business license, but not in R-1 or R-2 zoning unless the property is the owner's primary residence. Guest limits depend on the zoning district.

What are typical home values in Normal?

The median value of an owner-occupied home is $213,600. The town has a 54.8% owner-occupied rate, a $965 median gross rent and a median household income of $64,785.

How long is the commute from Normal to work?

The mean trip to work is 16.5 minutes. Interstates 55, 74 and 39 serve the town, and Connect Transit runs 16 fixed routes.

Ways to sell a house in Oak Park

Oak Park owners can list with an agent, sell on their own, or take an offer from a buyer who pays cash and accepts the building as it stands. The choice depends mostly on the condition of the building and how soon the money is needed.

Oak Park is a village on the west edge of Chicago, so buyers here compare it with city neighborhoods as much as with other suburbs. Population is 52,823, down from 54,583 in 2020.

  • An agent listing suits a house that shows well, with updated systems and a seller who can stay out of the way during showings.
  • Selling it yourself suits someone who knows the block, can price the house, and is comfortable reading a contract.
  • A cash sale suits a house with deferred work, a tenant in place, or an estate where the heirs live elsewhere. Set any cash figure beside what a repaired, listed house would net after commission and carrying costs.

A cash sale also skips showings, buyer financing contingencies and most repair requests, which is why it tends to close on the seller's calendar instead of the buyer's lender's.

Whichever route you pick, a few documents save time later: the latest tax bill, any lease for a rented unit, the water account information, and anything you know about whether the house sits in a historic district. Having these in one folder makes it easier to compare offers and to answer a buyer's questions quickly.

Older housing and historic districts

Most Oak Park houses were built before 1950, and some sit inside a historic district. That shapes both what repairs you can make and what buyers ask about.

The village has about 2,400 historic sites, mostly Queen Anne, Prairie School and Craftsman homes, and three historic districts: Frank Lloyd Wright, Ridgeland-Oak Park, and Seward Gunderson. A preservation ordinance has been in force since 1972. Frank Lloyd Wright built homes and Unity Temple here, so the village has the largest collection of Wright-designed residences in the world, and that draws a particular kind of buyer.

Before you plan exterior work, a window swap or a porch repair ahead of a sale, ask the village's historic preservation staff whether your address falls inside a district. A buyer's inspector will also look closely at original wood windows, plaster, wiring and older masonry, so expect those items to come up in negotiation. If you would rather not fund that work, a buyer who purchases as is removes the repair negotiation altogether.

Transfer stamps and the final water bill

The seller must buy real estate transfer stamps from the village Finance Department before the transfer can be completed. Stamps cost $8 per thousand, or fraction thereof, of the full actual contract price, and an exempt transfer costs $30.

The steps run in a set order, and skipping one delays the closing.

  1. Order a final water reading by calling 708.358.5478 at least 72 hours before you plan to buy the stamps.
  2. Email the paperwork to waterbilling@oak-park.us for review before you go in, including the completed Real Estate Transfer Tax Declaration Form.
  3. Pay every village utility charge. No stamp is issued until the account is clear.
  4. Buy the stamps. The village takes a cashier's check, certified check, money order, MasterCard, Visa or Discover. Personal checks are not accepted.

An exempt stamp, for a transfer with no sale, needs the original signed and notarized deed plus the statement by grantor and grantee. Photocopies are refused. For a condominium whose water meter is billed to the association, file the Condominium Association Water and Sewer Charges Affidavit or a paid-assessment letter.

Your title company or attorney usually handles this, but confirm who is doing it so the stamp is not forgotten on closing day. Oak Park also numbers its streets differently from Chicago: east-west numbers begin at Austin Boulevard and north-south numbers start at the elevated tracks just south of Lake Street, so check the address on a bill against the one on your contract.

How do Cook County property taxes affect an Oak Park sale?

Oak Park is in Cook County, which reassesses homes on a three-year cycle. Oak Park Township is in the group reassessed in 2023 and 2026. The township assessor is at 105 S. Oak Park Ave., phone (708) 383-8005, and can help you read a notice.

Tax bills come in two installments, and the due dates shift in years when bills are delayed. Ask the Cook County Treasurer for the current dates and for a copy of your bill. Then ask your closing agent how the current year's tax will be split between you and the buyer, since the bill that arrives after closing usually covers a period you owned the house.

The tax bill for an Oak Park parcel includes several separate taxing bodies: the township, the high school district, the elementary district, the library district and the park district. All of them show up on the same bill.

Selling a house with tenants

Roughly half of Oak Park's approximately 26,000 residential addresses are in multifamily buildings, so a sale with renters in place is common. The leases already signed will matter to any buyer, so gather them before you list or accept an offer.

  • Apartments in buildings of four or more units need a written lease.
  • A landlord must hold at least one month's rent as a security deposit, and deposits in buildings with four or more apartments earn interest when held more than six months.
  • After a tenant moves out the deposit is due back within 45 days, or 60 days if a repair estimate is sent within 30 days.
  • For unpaid rent the landlord gives a written five-day notice before filing in court.

The village's guidance also sets minimum heat of 68 degrees from 6:30 a.m. to 11 p.m. and 65 degrees overnight. The Community Relations Division at 708.358.5405 answers questions about local landlord and tenant rules.

Owners live in 60.0% of Oak Park homes, which leaves a large renter share.

The seller buys the village stamps. Oak Park charges $8 per thousand, or fraction thereof, of the full actual contract price, and exempt transfers cost $30. The final water bill must be paid first.

Can I sell an Oak Park house that is inside a historic district?

Yes. A historic district does not stop a sale. It affects exterior changes, so ask the village's historic preservation staff before you plan repairs, and tell your buyer which of the three districts, if any, covers the property.

How soon should I order the final water reading?

Call 708.358.5478 at least 72 hours before you intend to buy the transfer stamps. The stamps are withheld until all utility charges are settled.

Does Oak Park reassess homes every year?

No. Cook County reassesses on a three-year cycle, and Oak Park Township falls in the 2023 and 2026 group. Between those years the assessment can still change through appeals or exemptions, so read each bill.

What if my Oak Park house has a tenant on a lease?

The lease and the security deposit stay important to the sale. Oak Park requires a written lease in buildings of four or more units and sets deposit return at 45 days after move-out, so gather those documents before you accept an offer.

Hoffman Estates at a glance

Hoffman Estates is a village in the northwest suburbs, mostly in Cook County with a very small part in Kane County. Mail is delivered under ZIP codes 60169, 60010 and 60192. Population was 52,530 in the 2020 census and is estimated at 50,858 in mid-2025.

Sam and Jack Hoffman, a father and son who ran a construction company, bought 160 acres in 1954 and began building homes. The village incorporated on September 23, 1959. The count rose from 8,296 in 1960 to 46,363 in 1990, so many houses are several decades old, and a buyer will ask how old the roof, furnace and windows are.

The 2020 to 2024 survey counts 18,537 households. Of the homes, 74.2 percent are owned, with a median value of $351,900. Renters pay a median gross rent of $1,734. Just over a quarter of homes have renters, so investor-owned and tenant-occupied houses come up in sales. About 46.4 percent of residents age 5 and older use a non-English language at home, so translated showing instructions and listing documents can help.

Employers and commuting

The Prairie Stone Business Park, a 750-acre planned district bounded by Illinois Route 59, Interstate 90, Illinois Route 72 and Beverly Road, anchors employment in the village. It took shape after Sears relocated its headquarters there in 1993. St. Alexius Medical Center is the largest local employer at 2,500 workers. Commutes average 28.5 minutes, and Woodfield Mall in neighboring Schaumburg is close by.

A transfer or job change can force a quick sale, and proximity to this much employment is a fair point to make in a listing.

School districts by address

Several districts overlap here, so the assigned school follows the street address.

  • North of Interstate 90, Township High School District 211 serves high school students.
  • In that northern area, Community Consolidated School District 15 (K to 8) serves addresses east of Huntington Boulevard.
  • Barrington School District 220 (K to 12) serves addresses west of Huntington Boulevard in the same area.
  • Residents west of Barrington Road primarily attend Elgin Area U46.

Most of the village is in Harper College Community College District 512. Confirm the district for your exact address before you name any school in a listing.

Village Hall requirements before closing

The Village's transfer tax dates to 1987 and falls on the seller of any real estate sold or transferred inside Village limits. Payment and the stamp come before closing and recording, and the Village prints the cost as $3 per $1,000 of the selling price.

  • Allow 48 hours of notice so staff can process the stamp, and send applications or questions to transferstamps@vohe.org.

  • An exempt stamp costs a $10.00 administrative fee, needs the fully executed deed carrying the exempt language and signature, and calls for a final water reading if ownership changes.

Stamps are sold at the Village Hall front counter at 1900 Hassell Road on weekdays during business hours, or by mail with a self-addressed stamped return envelope. Settle with your closing agent who will buy the stamp and on what day.

Deed filing and transfer taxes

Most of the village sits in Cook County, so deeds go to the Cook County Clerk's recordings division at 118 N. Clark Street. A deed costs $107, which bundles the county recording fee, a GIS fee, a document storage fee, the State Rental Housing Support Fee and a non-government filer fee. Mail-in recording with return adds $5 per document.

The seller is liable for two more charges: .50 per $500.00 for the State of Illinois and .25 per $500.00 for Cook County. The statute behind the state tax is 35 ILCS 200/31-10.

Count backward from closing day, because each step waits on the one before it.

Most delays come from paperwork nobody collected until the week of closing. Pull these together once you have a signed contract, or earlier if you can.

  • Any permit paperwork for work done on the house, since a buyer's inspector may ask about a finished basement, a new roof or replaced windows.

Stamp questions go to 847-882-9100, and the stamp email address is transferstamps@vohe.org. If you live out of the area, ask about the mail-in option so you do not need to stand at the front counter on a weekday. Keep a copy of every receipt and stamped document for your records after closing, in case a title question comes up later.

The Village asks for 48 hours of notice. Request the final water bill at 847-843-4824 at least five days before you buy the stamp.

That follows the street. In the north, east of Huntington Boulevard is CCSD 15 for grades K to 8 and west of it is Barrington 220, while addresses west of Barrington Road mostly go to Elgin Area U46.

Fastest ways to sell in Downers Grove

Speed points to a direct cash sale in Downers Grove, while a top price points to a broker listing and a house staged for showings. Handling the sale yourself falls in between.

  • A broker suits a house in good shape that can wait through showings and a buyer's loan.

Downers Grove homes and teardowns

Downers Grove is a DuPage County village roughly 20 miles from the Chicago Loop, between I-88 and I-55. It has 50,365 residents. Metra's BNSF Line stops three times in the village, at Belmont Road, Main Street and Fairview Avenue, which keeps commuter demand strong. Grade School District 58 runs most of the elementary and middle schools, and Community High School District 99 covers Downers Grove North and South.

Mid-19th-century houses cluster near the center, and every later decade is represented around them. The village has had one of the Chicago area's highest teardown rates, with small older houses replaced by much larger ones. If your house is dated, tell buyers it may suit a rebuild as well as a move-in purchase.

Buyers here often ask about the train, the schools and the age of the mechanicals, so have the answers ready. If the roof, furnace or water heater is near the end of its life, say so plainly and show what you have spent on maintenance. A buyer who plans to tear the house down cares less about finishes and more about the lot, the drainage and the zoning, so tell each type of buyer what matters to them.

Teardowns and stormwater rules

Teardowns have been contentious because larger new houses cover more of each lot and push rainwater into neighboring yards and streets. The village's permit page carries its stormwater and tree protection ordinance summaries plus site-management forms such as a construction checklist and a notice to adjacent property owners.

Three practical effects follow for a seller:

  • A buyer planning to rebuild must follow the village's demolition, stormwater and tree rules, so ask Community Development which apply to your lot.
  • Drainage history on your lot matters, so disclose known water problems.
  • Open permits or unfinished work should be closed out before listing.

The permit page also carries residential re-roofing requirements, a contractor list, an encroachment license, a pool information sheet and a form for homeowners acting as their own plumbing contractor. Sellers who made such changes should have their permit paperwork on hand.

The village runs a permit portal through its Customer Self Service system, and its Stormwater Utility and Utility Bill services are separate accounts to settle at sale.

If a buyer wants to demolish, ask them to confirm in the contract that they, not you, will handle any demolition permit and stormwater plan. That keeps village paperwork from landing on your side of the table after closing.

DuPage County property tax

DuPage County collects in arrears, so each year's bill pays for the prior tax year. The Treasurer mails one bill in the spring with two coupons, due around June 1 and September 1.

The general homestead and senior exemptions are each $8,000, and owners should confirm that every exemption they qualify for appears on the bill. A yellow box means a mortgage company is paying, so a second check would be a duplicate. The Treasurer does not set values; the assessor named on your bill answers those questions. Call 630-407-5900 for payment issues.

At closing, your title company can explain how the year's tax is divided. The state's rate under 35 ILCS 200/31-10 is 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction, and the same company can say whether a county or local stamp also applies. For current recording fees, ask the DuPage County Clerk's recording division.

If the bill is paid by your mortgage company, the escrow account may hold a refund after closing, so ask the lender how and when it will be returned. If you pay the bill yourself, keep the receipts for both installments and hand copies to the title company. Missing exemptions are worth checking before you list, because a corrected bill leaves a cleaner proration for both sides.

Before an offer arrives

Preparation prevents surprises at the table.

  1. Find the deed and confirm every name on it will sign.
  2. Print the newest tax bill and see which exemptions it shows.
  3. Ask the village about open permits and finish any unfinished work.
  4. Settle the village utility account before the house changes hands.
  5. Obtain a written payoff from each lender or lienholder.

If you inherited the house, gather the paperwork that shows who may sign early, since a title company will ask for it. List or sell directly, but judge each offer by the net after payoffs, taxes and closing costs, and get terms in writing.

Tell the title company early if the house is held in a trust or by an estate, since extra signatures or documents may be required.

What a cash closing involves

With a cash buyer, the title company searches the record, prepares the deed and collects the transfer tax, and you sign at the closing table. No lender appraisal is needed, so the timeline depends on clean title and how fast payoffs arrive. Ask the buyer in writing who pays title and recording fees, whether the closing date can move if you need extra time to pack, and how the tax bill will be split. Compare the final figure with a listing's net after commission, repairs and carrying costs, not with its asking price.

Frequently asked questions

Which county is Downers Grove in?

DuPage County. Property tax bills come from the DuPage County Treasurer and deeds are recorded with the county.

When do DuPage property taxes fall due?

They are billed a year behind, on one bill with two coupons due around June 1 and September 1.

Can I sell a Downers Grove house to a builder who will tear it down?

Yes. Teardown buyers are common in the village. Share what you know about drainage or trees on the lot, and point them to the village's stormwater, tree protection and demolition requirements.

Which school districts serve Downers Grove?

Most of the village is in Grade School District 58, some areas are in Center Cass District 66, and the two high schools are in Community High School District 99. Check your tax bill to see which districts your parcel pays.

How can I avoid paying my tax bill twice?

Check for the yellow box on your bill. It shows when a mortgage company is paying, and in that case you should not send another payment.

Selling in Plainfield?

Which sale route suits you?

A Plainfield owner can list through an agent, handle the sale personally, or hand the house to a buyer paying cash who accepts it unrepaired. Price, effort and speed pull in different directions, so start from the shape the house is in and the date you must be out.

Plainfield has grown quickly, from about 4,500 residents in 1990 to 50,043 now, so a newer subdivision house competes against many near-identical neighbors, while a home near the old downtown draws a different crowd. Rank these goals before you pick:

  • Getting the highest possible price, which usually means repairs, staging and showings.
  • Closing on your own schedule, which often favors a direct sale with no financing contingency.
  • Avoiding repairs on a house with deferred maintenance, storm damage or a failing system.
  • Handling an inherited house, a divorce sale or a move that cannot wait for a long listing period.

Because a cash purchase skips the lender's appraisal, one common cause of failed contracts disappears. Even so, set any offer next to what a listing might realistically bring, and have the terms put in writing before you sign anything.

Plainfield housing numbers

Owners live in 88.0 percent of Plainfield homes, and much of the housing is under thirty years old, so buyers will ask about roof age, HVAC replacement dates and any homeowner association rules.

Plainfield housing and income, 2020-2024 estimates

A median hides a wide spread. A downtown cottage and a newer four-bedroom on a cul-de-sac sit in different price brackets, so treat these numbers as background and not as an offer on your own address.

Will or Kendall County?

Plainfield sits in northwestern Will County, and the village limits reach west into Kendall County. Some addresses are recorded, assessed and taxed through Kendall County offices even though the mailing address says Plainfield. Check the parcel record before you assume which county handles your deed.

Whichever county contains the parcel handles the recording: Will County for most of the village, Kendall County for the western part. Each county sets its own fees and document standards, so ask that recorder's office for the current schedule.

The land here is flat, and the DuPage River runs through the village center. Ask your title company whether any part of your lot touches a mapped flood area, because that affects insurance and a buyer's lender.

Which school district is your house in?

Most of the village falls inside Plainfield Community Consolidated School District 202, but not every Plainfield address does. Parts of the village are served by Oswego Community Unit School District 308 and Indian Prairie Community Unit School District 204, and in Kendall County most of the Plainfield land lies in the Oswego district.

Buyers often search by district first, so confirm yours before you write a listing. If you have children in school and need to move quickly, say so up front to whoever you sell to. A buyer who knows your timeline can often accommodate a rent-back period, which lets you finish a school year before handing over keys.

Village rules and older homes

The Village of Plainfield runs its building permit process through an online permitting and licensing portal, and its Building and Code Enforcement department takes complaints by phone, email or an online form. If you have open work, an unfinished deck or a basement finished without a permit, resolve it before a buyer's inspector finds it.

The village also has a Preservation Commission and a historic preservation ordinance. If your house is in the older core around Lockport Street, ask the village planning staff whether exterior changes need review.

A boom of new subdivisions followed the 1990 tornado, which damaged or destroyed more than 1,100 homes, so many Plainfield houses share a similar age and construction era. Buyers of those homes often ask about roof age, siding and the sump pump.

The Illinois transfer declaration and stamps

Illinois law requires a transfer declaration. Under 35 ILCS 200/31-25, it must be presented with the deed, or within three business days after the transfer, whichever is earlier, and signed by at least one seller and one buyer or their attorneys or agents. The form asks for the property's value, parcel number, legal description, deed date and type, street address, type of improvement, lot size, any homestead exemptions on the latest tax bill, and whether the transfer is between related parties.

A deed will not be accepted for recording without that declaration, unless an exemption applies under section 31-45. The county collects state transfer tax through revenue stamps at 50¢ for each $500 of value, rounding up for any fraction, under section 31-15. Whoever runs your closing normally prepares both the declaration and the stamps.

What must a Plainfield seller disclose?

A short list of papers makes a Plainfield closing smoother: the deed, the latest tax bill showing any homestead exemption, the parcel number, repair invoices, and a signed disclosure report. Your title company will ask for the parcel number first, since it decides which county handles recording. If the house is an inherited one, add the estate paperwork to that pile, and tell your closing agent early who has the authority to sign for the sellers, so the signature page is not a surprise at the table.

Illinois sellers of residential property must fill in every item of the state disclosure report and hand it to the buyer before a contract is signed (765 ILCS 77/20).

Section 25 of the same act says a seller must disclose material defects the seller actually knows about, and is not required to hire anyone to investigate. A seller is not liable for an error if the seller did not know of it, believed a defect had been fixed, or relied on information from a public agency or a qualified professional. Take your time filling out the report, and keep copies, including any repair invoices that support what you wrote.

  • List known roof, foundation, basement water and drainage problems.
  • Note any past repairs and who did them.
  • Describe what you know about nearby issues such as construction, traffic or highway noise.

Frequently asked questions

Must a Plainfield seller fix things before selling?

No. An as-is sale is allowed, whether to a cash buyer or on the open market, but the Illinois disclosure report still has to list defects you know about. A buyer will price the unrepaired items into the offer.

Which county records my Plainfield deed, Will or Kendall?

It depends on where the parcel sits. Most of the village is in Will County and the western edge is in Kendall County. Look at the parcel number on your tax bill or ask your title company, then contact that county's recorder for fees and format rules.

Does Plainfield have a historic district that limits what I can change?

The village has a Preservation Commission and a historic preservation ordinance. Whether your house is covered depends on its location and designation, so ask village planning staff before you list a house in the older downtown area.

What paperwork do I sign at a Plainfield closing besides the deed?

You will sign the Illinois transfer declaration along with the deed, plus a closing statement and the title company's affidavits. The disclosure report should already have gone to the buyer before the contract was signed.

How is the state transfer tax collected in Plainfield?

The county collects it through revenue stamps at 50¢ for each $500 of value, rounding up for any fraction. Whoever runs your closing normally prepares the stamps along with the declaration.

Listing or quick sale in Glenview

A quick as-is sale suits a Glenview house that needs work or an owner on a short clock, while a listing suits a house that shows well and can wait for the strongest bid. The choice comes down to condition, calendar and how much of the process you want to run yourself.

  • Listing: expect photos, showings, a buyer's inspection and possibly a repair list, with a closing date that follows the buyer's lender.
  • Do-it-yourself sale: you price the house, field inquiries and hire an attorney to review the contract.
  • Direct cash sale: no lender, no appraisal gap, and the house changes hands in its present state.

Inherited homes, houses with deferred upkeep and properties with a tenant you want to move on from tend to fit the third path best.

About Glenview

Glenview is a Cook County village about 15 miles northwest of downtown Chicago, with roughly 14 square miles of land. Much of the land stayed in farming until after World War II, when builders laid out the suburban streets that dominate today.

A large share of the modern village comes from the former Naval Air Station Glenview. The base closed in 1995 and became The Glen, a 1,121 acre mixed-use district that makes up about 15 percent of Glenview, with homes, offices, a town center, a lake, trails and the North Glenview Metra station. Metra's Milwaukee District North Line stops at Glenview and North Glenview, with trains to Chicago Union Station, and Amtrak also calls at Glenview station.

Which school district is your address in?

  • The southeast and east parts of the village are served by Wilmette District 39 and Avoca District 37.

For high school, most addresses attend Glenbrook South in District 225. Anyone on or east of Harms Road is in New Trier District 203. Buyers often ask for this detail first, so confirm it for your street before the first showing.

Parks and landmarks near Glenview homes

The Glenview Park District runs the Park Center on the shore of Lake Glenview, a prairie-style community center with an indoor pool, fitness rooms, a preschool and a senior center. The Grove, a 123 acre prairie with an interpretive center, nature trails and the 1856 Kennicott House, is a National Historic Landmark. Wagner Farm, an 18.6 acre working farm, shows farm life as it was in the 1920s. Portions of the Forest Preserves of Cook County also lie within the village, with Harms Woods among them.

Mention whichever of these sits closest to your house. Buyers comparing suburbs often ask what is within walking or biking distance.

What the Village asks of a seller at closing

The Village asks sellers to arrange a final water meter reading, and that is the only local task. Glenview has no transfer stamp, so nothing has to be purchased from Village Hall before the deed goes to the county.

  • Water Billing takes the request at (847) 724-1700.
  • The Village suggests booking 7 to 10 business days ahead so a crew is free.
  • The person leaving pays the last bill, and the account itself stays with the address.
  • Bills arrive quarterly, dated the first of the billing month and due on the 25th, and a late balance picks up a 10 percent penalty.

Water comes from Lake Michigan by way of Wilmette, and the Village resets its fixed and usage rates each year. Request the current rate sheet from Water Billing if you want the figures for your own closing statement.

Glenview is a light-touch village for sellers, so the order is short. Book the final water reading with Water Billing 7 to 10 business days ahead. Ask your title company to prepare the deed with the Property Index Number, the legal description and return-mail details. Have the MyDec declaration filed so the county can collect the transfer tax at the recorder. Finally, review the closing statement with your attorney or title officer to see how the tax bill is split. An as-is cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal, and the same few steps still apply, which is why a Glenview closing can move quickly once a contract is signed.

Property taxes and your sale

Cook County prepares the bill, and the Village gets a thin slice. Out of a typical bill for the 2024 tax year, about 5.5 percent went to the Village. School districts, the library, the community college and other bodies took the rest.

Questions about a valuation start with the township: Maine at (847) 297-2510, New Trier at (847) 446-8202, Niles at (847) 673-9300 or Northfield at (847) 724-8300. The Cook County Assessor's Office is at (312) 443-7550. How the year's bill is divided between you and the buyer is settled on the closing statement, so ask your attorney or title officer to walk through it before you sign.

What goes on a deed recorded in Cook County

The Cook County Clerk's recordings office accepts Glenview deeds and publishes a checklist of required items. Missing any one of them gets a deed turned away.

  • Names and addresses of both the person conveying and the person receiving title.
  • The street address, the Property Index Number and the full legal description.
  • Return-mail and preparer details.
  • A finished MyDec filing for the state and county tax stamp.
  • An exemption line or affidavit, only if the transfer qualifies as exempt.

The state statute puts collection of the transfer tax with the county recorder, at 50 cents per $500 of value. Your closing agent will work out the exact total for your sale.

Weather and what buyers inspect

Glenview has a continental climate, with January lows near 17 degrees and yearly precipitation of roughly 38 inches, with August the wettest month at almost 5 inches. Roofs, gutters, grading and basements therefore get close attention from inspectors.

Receipts for a new roof, a working sump pump or drainage repairs are worth gathering. If the house needs those jobs and you would rather skip managing contractors, a buyer who takes the property in its current state removes that burden from you.

Is there a Glenview transfer stamp to buy before I close?

No. The Village of Glenview has no transfer stamp. The state and county declaration is still filed through MyDec when the Cook County Clerk records the deed.

Call (847) 724-1700 about 7 to 10 business days before the closing date. The seller covers the final bill, and the new owner opens a fresh account on the same property.

Who records the deed for a house in Glenview?

The Cook County Clerk's recordings office. Its checklist asks for a Property Index Number, a legal description, return-mail and preparer details, and the MyDec declaration.

Will anyone buy a Glenview house that needs big repairs?

Yes. Buyers who purchase as-is accept the present condition, though they factor the repair work into what they offer.

What share of a Glenview tax bill funds the Village?

About 5.5 percent for tax year 2024. Schools, the library, the community college and other districts receive the rest.
