Inherited house and the seller disclosure

An inherited Urbana house may not need the usual seller disclosure. Illinois expects residential sellers to give the buyer a disclosure report ahead of signing (765 ILCS 77/20), but Section 15 exempts several kinds of seller, including a fiduciary administering a decedent's estate, a transfer from a decedent by will or intestate succession, and transfers made under court order.

Who signs the deed decides whether an exemption applies, so check with the closing attorney. The Champaign County Recorder can tell you the current deed requirements and fees before you schedule a signing.

What a cash sale skips

Selling to a cash buyer drops several steps that drag out a regular listing. Nobody needs a mortgage approved, so there is no lender appraisal and no repair list from an underwriter. Staging, open houses and weeks of showings squeezed around a class schedule fall away too.

Disclosure of known problems, clearing taxes owed and recording the deed in Champaign County all still happen. For a rental, tenants keep their lease rights through a sale, so tell the buyer about every lease up front. Get the offer in writing, ask who covers closing costs, and read the contract through before you sign.

Steps from offer to closing

After you accept an offer, the title company digs through the records on the parcel and writes up every claim against it. Payoff letters come from any lender, you dig out the latest tax bill, and you and the buyer settle on a closing day.

For a rental, bring the current registration and any inspection results, and give tenants proper notice under their lease. A buyer paying cash has no lender appraisal to wait on, so the timeline comes down to the title work and when the deed reaches the Champaign County Recorder. Bring photo ID to the signing, plus any keys, garage openers and warranty papers you have for the house.

Does the city of Urbana inspect a house before it sells?

The city's permit and rental pages describe permits and a rental inspection cycle. Call the Building Safety Division at 217-384-2443 to ask whether anything applies to a sale at your address.

What dates apply to Urbana property tax installments?

There are two installments, with bills going out May 1. The first is due in early June and the second in early September, and the pattern repeats yearly.

What should the owner of an Urbana rental do before listing?

Confirm that registration is current, because the program year runs October 15 to October 14 and fees are annual. The Building Safety Division can explain the inspection history, which also appears in the city's open data.

Where can an Urbana owner pay property tax in person?

Pay at the Champaign County Treasurer's Office, 102 E. Main Street in Urbana. A 24-hour drop box sits in front of the guard shack in the parking area, and cash, checks, money orders and cards are accepted, with cards and checks only through September 30.

How fast can a cash sale of an Urbana house close?

It moves as fast as the title work, payoff letters and deed are ready. A cash closing depends on the buyer's funds, the title company and the county's recording of the deed.

Carol Stream in brief

Carol Stream sits in DuPage County, west of Chicago. The village incorporated on January 5, 1959, covers 9.44 square miles and had 39,854 residents in the 2020 census. Deeds go to the DuPage County Recorder.

Population grew from 836 in 1960 to 31,716 in 1990, peaked near 40,438 in 2000 and has been nearly flat since. Most neighbors bought within the same few decades, so comparable sales tend to be houses of similar age, and the stock is young by Chicago-area standards.

What Carol Stream requires before closing

On top of the state levy, Carol Stream collects a transfer tax of its own, and the stamp must be in hand before the closing papers go to the recorder. Finance sets the rate at $3.00 for each $1,000 of the selling price or fraction thereof.

You may email the contract to Finance, as long as the file is under 25MB and is not zipped. To set the meter reading, call Water Billing at 630-871-6222. Radio readings are the norm, so staff rarely need to go inside.

Who pays the village tax, and can it be refunded?

The seller, or grantor, normally owes the village tax. When a property passes through a sheriff's sale or a tax deed, the buyer owes it instead.

The village allows a refund only when every one of four conditions is met. The seller must have lived in the house for a year within the last three, must not have rented out any part of it, must have bought and now occupy a replacement home inside the village, and must apply within one year of paying the tax. A seller who moves out of Carol Stream will not qualify.

Permits and past work

A permit that was never closed can draw questions from a buyer's agent or the closing attorney. Community Development takes permit applications online or at its counter, and a card fee of 2.9 percent applies online and 3.5 percent in person.

  • Inspections need about 24 hours of advance notice and are scheduled at 630-871-6230 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.
  • Plumbing inspections are done by a consultant on Monday, Wednesday and Friday afternoons, 1:30 to 3:30 p.m.
  • A re-inspection fee can apply if work fails or is not ready, and it must be paid before the next visit.

Think back to a finished basement, a deck or a water heater swap by an earlier owner, and ask Community Development if that permit was closed. An as-is cash buyer takes on the risk, while a retail buyer's lender may insist on a fix.

Illinois levies a title transfer tax of half a dollar for each $500 of declared value under 35 ILCS 200/31-10. You file the declaration through MyDec, and Carol Stream wants a copy of it when you buy the stamp.

The DuPage County Recorder files your deed, and its land records go back to 1839. Phone 630-407-5400 with questions. The office also supplies deed copies, handy for a tax appeal or an exemption.

School boundaries cut across village lines, so your street address decides the district. Buyers ask early, and having the answer ready spares you a question at the door.

  • Some southern and southeastern blocks: Community Unit School District 200 in Wheaton, or Glen Ellyn School District 41 with Glenbard North for high school.

Check the boundary with the district before you mention schools in an ad.

The Great Western Trail crosses town, and the Steve Ravanesi Trail links it to Red Hawk Park, the dog park and Glenbard North High School. The Carol Stream Park District runs 36 parks. A house within a short walk of the trail or a park is an easy item to put in a listing description. North Avenue is the main east-west corridor, and Pace Route 711 runs between Carol Stream and Wheaton.

An agent listing reaches the most buyers. It works best for a house in good shape when you can sit through showings, repair requests and a buyer's loan approval. If you sell on your own, you keep the agent's fee and take on the contract, disclosures and the village stamp errands yourself.

A cash sale as-is makes sense for a house with repair needs, a tenant, an estate behind it or a deadline. Expect the offer to come in under what a repaired house could fetch on the open market. Set it beside your repair estimate, your monthly carrying costs and your calendar.

Step by step to closing

Carol Stream is one of the villages where the seller handles several errands before the deed is recorded. Keep a folder with the contract, the two declarations, water receipts and permit papers, and hand a copy to your title company. If anything is missing, the Finance Department can tell you before you make the trip, and Community Development can confirm permit status over the phone. Doing those calls first keeps the stamp visit short and the closing date steady.

Once you have a signed contract, email a copy to the Finance Department. Book the final meter reading with Water Billing at least two working days before closing, and pay the final bill. Complete the village declaration and the state declaration. Pick up the stamp, pay the village tax, and bring the deed to the DuPage County Recorder.

If you plan to claim the refund, check the four conditions first. A seller who leaves the village will not qualify, so count the tax in your net before you accept a price.

Do I pay the Carol Stream transfer tax as the seller?

Usually yes. The tax generally falls on the grantor, the seller, with an exception for sheriff's sales and tax deeds, where the buyer pays. The rate is $3.00 per $1,000 of the price or fraction thereof.

How soon before closing should I book the water meter reading?

At least two working days before closing. Call the Water Billing division at 630-871-6222. The final bill, and anything else owed to the village, must be paid before the stamp is issued.

Which school district is my Carol Stream house in?

It depends on the address. Most homes are in District 93 and Glenbard North, while parts of the village fall in U46, District 25, District 200 or District 41. Check the boundary with the district before you advertise the house.

Can I sell if a past owner skipped a permit?

Yes, though the issue may come up in an inspection or title review. Ask the Community Development Department at 630-871-6230 about the permit history. An as-is cash buyer may take the risk on, while a financed buyer may ask you to resolve it first.

Where is the deed recorded after the sale?

With the DuPage County Recorder. The state transfer declaration and the village stamp are completed before recording. Call 630-407-5400 with questions about recording.

Which way of selling fits a Quincy homeowner?

Quincy owners usually choose between a standard listing, a private sale, and a direct offer from someone paying cash for the house exactly as it stands. Age of the structure, the work it needs and your calendar decide which of those makes sense.

Quincy has several historic districts, and many of its brick homes date to the German immigrant building boom of the late 1800s. Those houses charm some buyers and put off others who dread the cost of updating them. Think through which of these describes your situation:

  • The condition is sound and months of waiting for the right buyer would not hurt, which favors a listing.
  • A roof, furnace or foundation needs money you would prefer not to spend.
  • A parent who lived there for decades has died and you are settling the estate.
  • A tenant, a code complaint or a lien is getting in the way of a conventional sale.

In the last three situations a direct sale can shorten the process, since no lender appraisal has to be passed. With any route, get the price, the closing date and the split of costs written down before you commit.

Quincy housing numbers

Prices sit low and renters make up a sizable share of households. Only 63.6 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, which gives landlords and investors a real presence among buyers. Population is 38,918, down from 39,463 in 2020 and 40,633 in 2010, so plenty of sellers are longtime owners downsizing or heirs clearing out a parent's place.

Housing built for a larger population now serves a smaller one, with 10.4 percent of the 19,028 housing units vacant in 2020. Buyers compare your house with others on the market, including the many older brick homes nearby, and ask pointed questions about condition, so a clear repair history and recent utility bills help.

Bluffs, the river and neighborhoods

The city rises on bluffs above the Mississippi River at Quincy Bay. Houses on sloping lots near the river deserve a close look at drainage, retaining walls and basement moisture before you list.

Buyers tend to think in terms of areas. Downtown is a historic district, and the South Side German Historic District holds the brick homes built by German immigrants in the late 1800s. North Quincy lies beyond a rail line and a large creek, and Hickory Grove sits to the east along Interstate 172. Commutes average about 14 minutes, which is a point to mention to buyers.

A house inside or beside a historic district should be described in terms of its architecture. Brickwork, original trim and period details are what shoppers in those areas tend to look for.

What city rules should a Quincy seller check?

Quincy's Office of Inspection, on the second floor of City Hall at 730 Maine Street, handles building permits and minimum housing complaints. The city runs a complaint-driven system for rentals, where a tenant files a Minimum Housing Complaint Form and an inspector visits. If you are selling a rental, ask the Office of Inspection whether any registration or inspection requirement applies to your address.

The complaint form's checklist shows what inspectors measure against the International Property Maintenance Code:

  • Working smoke detectors in each bedroom and hallway.
  • Carbon monoxide alarms in homes with fuel-burning appliances or an attached garage.
  • Handrails on stairs with more than four risers.
  • A watertight roof.
  • A heating system that holds 68 degrees.

A buyer's home inspector will likely check the same points, so repair them before you list, or sell as is to a buyer who will handle them.

Recording a deed in Adams County

Adams County files deeds through its Clerk and Recorder office at 507 Vermont Street in Quincy. A deed or trust document has to arrive with an Illinois Department of Revenue Real Estate Transfer Declaration or a Statement of Exemption.

Posted fees start at $80.00 for land records under 50 pages on standard paper, rise to $92.00 for documents that miss the 55 ILCS 5/3-5018 format standards, and add $80.00 per extra book and page reference. The schedule includes the Rental Housing Support Fee. Fees move over time, so confirm the amount with the office before closing.

A Quincy sale from start to finish

Selling an older Quincy house goes more smoothly when you take the steps in a sensible order.

  1. Decide how much repair work you are willing to fund, and whether an as-is sale to a cash buyer would leave you better off than a listing.
  2. Walk through the house with the city's checklist in mind: smoke detectors, carbon monoxide alarms, stair handrails, the roof and the heat.
  3. Gather invoices for any past work, and recent utility bills that show what the house costs to run.
  4. If the house is a rental, call the Office of Inspection at City Hall to ask whether anything applies to your address.
  5. Have your closing attorney prepare the transfer declaration and the deed for the Adams County Clerk and Recorder, and confirm the fees before closing.

Quincy's older brick homes can be sound and still need work, and buyers who finance with a mortgage often ask for repairs after the inspection. A direct buyer who pays cash and takes the house as it stands removes that step. That helps most with an inherited property, a vacant house or a rental with a tenant in place, where the owner would rather not manage repairs from a distance, and it lets you pick a closing date that fits the estate or the move.

What a Quincy seller must disclose

State law requires a completed residential disclosure report to go to the buyer before a contract is signed (765 ILCS 77/20). The next section of the act limits that duty to material defects the seller actually knows about, with no obligation to investigate. Keep the invoices for any work done on the house. They back up what you wrote on the report if a question comes up later.

For an estate sale, the heirs should fill in the report from what they actually know, and say so plainly where they have never lived in the house. A cash buyer who purchases as is still receives the report, but the repair negotiation that normally follows it largely disappears.

Frequently asked questions

Does an older brick house take longer to sell in Quincy?

Often, because buyers want evidence that the wiring, plumbing and foundation are sound. A listing can reach people who prize historic detail, and a direct sale suits an owner who wants to skip the repairs.

What are the recording fees for a Quincy deed?

Adams County posts $80.00 as the minimum for land records under 50 pages that meet the paper standards, and $92.00 for those that do not. Call the office to confirm the schedule before closing.

Does Quincy require a rental registration for landlords selling a house?

The city's housing complaint process is tenant-driven, and an inspector visits after a complaint. Ask the Office of Inspection at City Hall whether any registration applies to your property before you list a rental.

Who inspects Quincy houses for code problems?

The city's Office of Inspection, at 730 Maine Street, reviews minimum housing complaints and building permits. A tenant files the complaint form and an inspector schedules a visit.

What does a Quincy seller have to disclose?

A completed Illinois residential disclosure report must reach the buyer before a contract is signed. It covers material defects you actually know about, and you do not have to hire anyone to investigate.

Selling quickly in Park Ridge

With a median owner-occupied value of $551,200 and owners who tend to stay put, a standard listing is the usual route when a house is in good shape. A cash buyer is more useful when the house needs work that would take months to finish, when a probate or move deadline is close, or when you want to avoid showings.

Park Ridge is a city in Cook County about 15 miles north of downtown Chicago, close to O'Hare International Airport. Population is 38,463, and much of the housing dates to the mid-century boom, so a buyer's inspector will look closely at the age of the wiring, plumbing, roof and foundation.

With 84.8 percent of homes owner-occupied, most buyers are families who plan to live in the house and who usually rely on a mortgage. A house that cannot pass a lender's appraisal or an inspection can lose that kind of buyer, which is where a cash sale enters the picture.

Houses here sell at prices where small defects matter to a lender. If the roof is near the end of its life or the electrical panel is original, a mortgage buyer may ask for credits or walk away, while an investor will simply lower the offer and close without a financing step. Decide which of those outcomes you can live with before you set your asking price.

The Park Ridge transfer tax and who files it

The city charges its own real estate transfer tax, and the seller pays it. The rate is $2.00 per $1,000 of value or fraction thereof, and the fee for an exempt transfer is $25.00.

To get the transfer tax certificate, send the Finance Department:

  • The PTAX-203 or MyDec form.
  • A photo of the water meter for the final reading.
  • The closing date.
  • A contact name, phone number and email address.

Documents go to transferstamp@parkridge.us or to the Finance Department at 505 Butler Place. Questions go to 847-318-5222, option 4. The certificate is issued once the tax and any other amounts owed to the city, including the final water bill, are paid, and it is attached to the deed at recording. On top of the city's tax, recording adds the state's 50 cents per $500 and the county's 25 cents per $500.

Closing cannot be completed without the certificate and the final water reading, so ask your closing attorney or title company to start these steps as soon as the contract is signed.

Water bills and closing dates

Water is billed every other month, issued on the last day of the month and due by the 20th. Email the meter photo no earlier than five days before closing, with the service address and closing date. Water is not shut off during a transfer, and the account moves automatically into the buyer's name.

Final payment is accepted as cash, credit or debit card, certified check, money order or attorney's check. Homeowners are responsible for repairs to the water service pipe between the buffalo box and the house, so a leak that turns up in a buyer's inspection is yours to fix or to credit.

Assessment is a Cook County function, so property tax appeals and exemptions go to the county assessor, not City Hall.

Do you need a permit for repairs on a Park Ridge house?

A permit is required for most construction. The city lists new buildings, additions, garages, driveways, HVAC, electrical and plumbing work, pools, fences, patios, decks, sheds and siding. No permit is needed for window replacement unless the opening is enlarged, or for residential roof replacement, although roofing contractors must hold a city license. Routine maintenance that leaves existing systems and structural walls alone also needs none.

Timing matters if you plan fixes before a sale:

  • Reviews usually take up to two weeks, and the standard time is two weeks for every permit during the May to September busy season.
  • Residential permits stay valid for one year, and a renewal after expiration costs 50 percent of the original permit fee.
  • Applications go through the Civic Access online portal, and inspections are booked by morning or afternoon block with a one to two business day lead time.

Questions go to the Community Preservation and Development department at 847-318-5291. A separate tree removal permit is required for trees larger than 10 inches in diameter, so check before clearing a lot.

Landmark and preservation rules

Park Ridge has a Historic Preservation Commission. A house becomes a local landmark only with the owner's consent, and a designation can be rescinded, though the Commission encourages owners to look at alternatives first. If your house is already landmarked, tell buyers early.

Park Ridge also sits close to O'Hare, and buyers sometimes ask about the neighborhood as a result. Be ready to talk about the block, the two Metra stops (Park Ridge and Dee Road, on the Union Pacific Northwest Line) and which school your street feeds, since families make up most of the buyers here. Park Ridge-Niles School District 64 runs the elementary schools and Maine Township High School District 207 serves high school students.

If you are unsure whether your address carries a designation, ask the Community Preservation and Development department before you list, so the answer is ready when a buyer asks.

A simple order of steps for a Park Ridge sale

Whichever way you sell, the same few tasks set the closing date. If you do them early, nothing stalls at the last minute, and the buyer's side has less to chase.

  1. Decide between a listing and a cash offer by comparing what each would net after repairs and carrying costs.
  2. Check for open permits and tell your buyer about any past work that needed one.
  3. Once the contract is signed, have your attorney or title company send the transfer tax paperwork to the Finance Department.
  4. Email the water meter photo within five days of closing.
  5. Pay the transfer tax and any remaining city amounts so the certificate can be issued and attached to the deed.

A cash buyer who accepts the house as is makes the repair step disappear, so the city paperwork becomes the main work left before closing. Keep copies of everything you file, since the title company will ask for the certificate number on closing day.

Frequently asked questions

How much is the Park Ridge transfer tax?

The city charges $2.00 per $1,000 of value or fraction thereof, paid by the seller. The state adds 50 cents per $500 and the county adds 25 cents per $500.

Do I need to pay my final water bill before closing in Park Ridge?

Yes. The transfer tax certificate is issued after the tax and any other amounts owed to the city, including the final water bill, are paid. Email a photo of the meter to the Finance Department no earlier than five days before closing.

Can I replace my roof or windows in Park Ridge without a permit?

Usually yes. Residential roof replacement and window replacement do not need a permit unless the window opening is enlarged. Roofing contractors must hold a city license, and decks, fences and electrical work still require permits.

Who handles Park Ridge property tax appeals?

The county does, not the city. Assessment is a county function, so owners go to the Cook County Assessor's office for appeals, exemptions and the required forms.

Does the water account transfer when a Park Ridge house sells?

Yes. The city places the account in the buyer's name automatically, does not shut off service during the transfer, and bills every other month afterward. Sellers settle the final reading through the transfer tax process.

Is there a transfer tax in Wheeling?

Not from the village. Wheeling has no real estate transfer tax of its own. It does require every seller to obtain a Real Estate Transfer Stamp on the original deed, and the stamp carries no fee. The catch is that the stamp is only issued after the final water, sewer and garbage charges, plus any outstanding tickets and penalties, are paid in full.

The state tax still applies. Under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, Illinois taxes the privilege of transferring title at 50 cents per $500 of value stated in the declaration, and the county where the parcel sits can add its own.

How the Wheeling transfer stamp works

The rule sits in Section 15.10 of the Wheeling Municipal Code. The seller presents the original deed at the Finance Department counter in Village Hall, or mails it in, and the stamp is placed on that deed. The village asks for 10 business days of notice before closing so it can schedule a final meter reading and prepare the stamp.

Give the village a forwarding address and the final reading date. Buyers then supply new resident registration information, and if registration is incomplete the village may discontinue water service.

Condominium sellers

Condo owners pay for water, sewer and garbage through monthly assessments, but the village still treats them as owners who need a stamp. A condo seller therefore has two sets of paperwork: the association's payoff and resale documents, and the village's stamp. Ask the management company early for its timeline, because the association's letter and the village's 10 business day notice both feed the closing date.

  • Order the association paperwork as soon as a contract exists.
  • Submit the village's transfer stamp application at the same time.
  • Keep a copy of the original deed, since the village stamps the original.

Wheeling housing at a glance

Owners occupy 62.7% of Wheeling homes, which leaves a large share of rentals. The typical owner-occupied value is $266,200, rent is $1,663 a month and household income is $85,205, across 15,171 households. Population is estimated at 38,391 for July 2025, 2.0% below the 2020 base.

Monthly owner costs are $1,909 with a mortgage and $892 without. Because so many homes are rented, investors and landlords are an active part of the buyer pool, and a seller with tenants in place should expect questions about lease terms.

Property taxes and reassessment

Most of Wheeling lies in Cook County, in Wheeling Township, with a smaller part in Lake County. Cook County reassesses one-third of the county each year, and the north suburbs, Wheeling Township included, were reassessed in 2025. Wheeling Township takes in all or part of Wheeling, Arlington Heights, Des Plaines, Glenview, Mount Prospect, Northbrook, Palatine, Prospect Heights, Rolling Meadows and Buffalo Grove, so neighbors across a municipal line share the same assessment cycle. Owners in the Lake County portion should ask the Lake County treasurer and assessor for their schedule.

The Cook County Assessor put the township's median 2024 single-family sale price at $457,000 against a median market value estimate of $429,000. Your closing agent prorates the unpaid tax, so request a copy of the most recent bill before you list.

Selling with tenants in place

Many Wheeling houses and condos are rented, and a sale does not end a lease. Tell every prospective buyer what the lease says: the rent, the end date and any deposit you hold. A cash buyer who wants the unit empty should say so before the contract is signed, so you can plan notice to the tenant.

Keep rent and utility records handy. The village stamp depends on the final water, sewer and garbage charges being paid, and a tenant who runs up a balance can delay the stamp. Check the account a few weeks ahead and clear anything outstanding, including tickets and penalties.

Closing is also the moment to hand over keys, garage openers and any warranty papers, and to pass the buyer the tenant's contact details and the lease itself.

Getting around and schools

Wheeling is a village in Cook and Lake counties about 23 miles northwest of downtown Chicago, in Wheeling and Vernon townships. Metra's North Central Service stops in Wheeling on weekdays only, and Pace buses connect to Des Plaines and Buffalo Grove. Public schools are run by Wheeling Community Consolidated School District 21 and Township High School District 214, which operates Wheeling High School.

Winters are usually very cold and snowy and summers are hot and humid, so buyers look closely at roofs, gutters and furnaces when they walk a house. Drainage and basement moisture are on most inspection lists, so fix or disclose them early.

Getting ready for a quick sale

Start with the village paperwork, because it has the longest lead time. Then gather the Illinois disclosure report required for one to four unit homes before a contract is signed under 765 ILCS 77/20, and a recent tax bill. An investor who pays cash and takes the house as-is still needs the stamp, the final water reading and the paid utility balance, so those steps do not shorten with a faster closing.

  • Call Water Billing at (847) 459-2607 about 10 business days before the closing date.
  • Pay any outstanding tickets and penalties with the village.
  • Have the original deed available, since a copy will not be stamped.
  • Have the closing agent confirm the county's recording charges.

What happens at the closing table

You sign the deed, the title company pays off any mortgage from your proceeds, and the stamped original goes to the county for recording. If the final water bill is not paid, the stamp is not issued and the recording waits, so settle it a few days ahead. Ask the title company for a closing statement that lists every charge, and keep it with your tax records.

If the house sits in the Lake County portion of the village, the recording happens at the Lake County Clerk instead of Cook County, so ask the title company which office applies. Either way, the stamp comes first and the recording follows, and a clear paper trail of paid utility bills makes both steps quick.

Does the Village of Wheeling charge a transfer tax?

No. The village has no real estate transfer tax, but it requires a transfer stamp on the original deed. The stamp has no fee, and all water, sewer, garbage charges, tickets and penalties must be paid first.

How much notice does Wheeling need before closing?

The village asks for 10 business days of notice. The electronic final water reading happens 2 business days before closing, so the longer notice gives staff time to prepare the stamp.

Do condo owners in Wheeling need a transfer stamp?

Yes. The requirement applies to condominium owners even though they pay water, sewer and garbage indirectly through monthly assessments. It also covers refinances, quit claim deeds and transfers into a trust.

Which agency assesses a Wheeling house for tax?

The Cook County Assessor handles most of Wheeling, since the village lies mainly in Cook County. Wheeling Township was reassessed in 2025. Owners in the Lake County portion deal with Lake County offices instead.

What is the median home value in Wheeling?

Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $266,200 for 2020 to 2024. The July 2025 population estimate is 38,391, and median gross rent is $1,663.

A Streamwood owner's options for selling

Three doors are open to a Streamwood seller: a broker's listing, a sale you manage alone, or a buyer who pays cash and takes the house untouched. Repairs, renters and the date you need funds usually settle the question.

  • Broker's listing: rewards a house in good order, provided you can sit through inspections and a lender's schedule.
  • Going alone: saves the commission and hands you the pricing, advertising and contract review.
  • Cash, untouched: no buyer repair demands, which suits a worn, inherited or tenant-occupied house.

Rented houses carry a Streamwood-specific wrinkle. The village licenses every rental property, single-family homes and condominium units included, so a landlord who sells should ask what happens to the license at transfer.

Streamwood prices and who lives here

Streamwood has an estimated 38,277 residents in 13,057 households averaging 2.97 people. Owners live in 89.0% of homes, the middle value is $271,200, and middle gross rent is $1,809. Owner cost per month runs $1,907 with a mortgage and $880 without one, and the middle household income is $101,218.

Inspectors for a buyer will focus on roofs, gutters and basements. Elgin Area School District U-46 serves most of the village, but boundaries split near Barrington Road and Route 59 for schools, libraries and park districts. Tell buyers which district, library and park district apply to your address. The nearest Metra station is in Bartlett, on the Milwaukee District West Line to Chicago Union Station.

Village transfer stamp

Streamwood has its own real estate transfer stamp, issued by the Finance Department. Three items must reach the village before a stamp is issued:

  • A copy of the deed.
  • A copy of the state's Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration.
  • Payment of all outstanding water and sewer charges, including any assessments or penalties owed to the village.

Rental license and inspection

A single-family or condo rental license costs $155 per building per year, includes the required inspection, and expires December 31. Landlords must finish a free online Crime Free Housing seminar of about an hour before applying. Each rental needs an interior and exterior inspection before the one-year license is issued, and the license must be renewed and paid for every year.

  • The tenant, or the landlord acting for the tenant, signs an inspection consent form before the village schedules the visit.
  • Landlords must show a certificate from the Crime Free Housing seminar. The village accepts one issued within the last five years by a community in Cook, DuPage, Kane, McHenry or Will County.
  • A sample Crime Free addendum for leases is posted on the village page.

Selling a rented Streamwood house

Treat the license as part of the house's paperwork. A buyer who plans to keep the tenants should ask for the license record and the latest inspection result. A buyer who wants the house empty will want to know the lease end date before closing. A cash buyer can take a rented house, but the lease still has to be read first. Keep the license in force while the house is rented, and ask your attorney how a tenant's lease passes to the buyer.

Who assesses and bills Streamwood property taxes?

The village does not provide property tax services. Hanover Township handles assessment through the Cook County Assessor, and the Cook County Treasurer collects the tax. Ask the Treasurer about current bills at (312) 443-5100, and take past years or delinquent taxes to the Cook County Clerk at (312) 603-5645.

Cook County reassesses each property once every three years, on a township schedule, and north suburban townships such as Hanover are reassessed only where something about a property has changed. The last day to file an appeal with the Assessor for Hanover this cycle is December 7, 2026.

  • Look up your parcel number and notice on the Assessor's website.
  • Find out from the Assessor which exemptions are attached to your parcel.
  • Have your closing attorney explain how the year's bill is divided with the buyer.

What the Cook County deed needs

Deeds for Streamwood property are recorded by the Cook County Clerk. Its checklist includes the common address, the Property Index Number, a legal description, mail-to and prepared-by names, grantor and grantee details and a completed MyDec form for the state and county stamps. It also lists the municipality's real estate transfer tax, which is where the Streamwood stamp comes in.

For an exempt transfer, the deed needs exemption language citing 35 ILCS 200/31-45 and Cook County Ordinance 93-O-27, or a grantor and grantee affidavit. Section 31-15 of the Property Tax Code sets the state rate at 50 cents per $500 of value, and your title company can confirm the county amount.

A cash sale in Streamwood, start to finish

A cash buyer skips showings, a lender's appraisal and the repair list, but the village steps still apply. Pay the water and sewer balance, send the deed and transfer declaration to Finance, and receive the stamp. Then the Cook County Clerk records the deed. If the house is a rental, have the license record and last inspection result ready for the buyer. Put the price, the closing date and the lease terms in writing before you sign. Ask the buyer to confirm who pays for the village stamp, since the contract decides it, and keep copies of the stamped deed and the closing statement for your own files once everything records. If a question arises, the Finance Department can usually answer it in one call.

Papers to gather before you list

A short folder prevents delays. Collect your deed, the latest tax bill and the parcel number, the water and sewer account details, and receipts for roof or gutter work. For a rental, add the license, the latest inspection result, the lease and any Crime Free addendum. Give the closing attorney or title company a copy right away so the transfer declaration and the village stamp request can be prepared while you line up a buyer. If you live elsewhere, name one contact who can answer the village if a question comes up.

Does Streamwood charge its own transfer tax?

Yes. The village's Finance Department prints a rate of $3.00 per $1,000 of value, and it issues the stamp after receiving the deed, the state transfer declaration and proof that water and sewer charges are paid.

Should a landlord keep the Streamwood rental license while selling?

Streamwood requires a license for every rental, at $155 per building per year with an inspection. Keep it in force while the house is rented, and ask your attorney how a tenant's lease passes to the buyer.

Which office assesses a Streamwood home?

Hanover Township does the local assessing through the Cook County Assessor, and the Cook County Treasurer collects the tax. The village itself does not handle assessments or bills.

What happens to water and sewer balances at closing?

Pay them first. The village will not issue the transfer stamp until all outstanding charges, assessments and penalties are cleared.

What does an exempt Streamwood transfer cost?

A transfer that changes the deed with no money exchanged needs a $10 exempt stamp. The application requires a signed, notarized deed.

Carpentersville at a glance

Carpentersville is a village in northern Kane County on the Fox River. The 2020 census counted 37,983 residents in 8.09 square miles, up 0.8 percent from 37,691 in 2010. Carpentersville handles its own permits, water billing and rental licensing, so most of the paperwork stays at Village Hall instead of moving to a county office.

The 2020 census recorded 11,777 housing units, 2.9 percent of them vacant, with a homeowner vacancy rate of 0.9 percent and a rental vacancy rate of 5.0 percent. A rate that low suggests few for-sale houses sit empty, which helps a seller who prices sensibly. Median household income is $73,105, so many buyers will need a mortgage. That is one reason some owners prefer a cash buyer who does not depend on lender approval.

Older river blocks and newer subdivisions

The village has two kinds of housing. The older street grid along the river centers on Main Street, and the population jumped from 1,523 in 1950 to 17,424 in 1960 as subdivisions arrived. Newer subdivisions and shopping centers have gone up west along Randall Road since the 1990s.

Know which type you own before you price. Younger families make up much of the village, with a median age of 32.5 in 2020, so house size and layout matter to the likely buyer pool. If your house is in the older river-side grid, ask Village Hall whether any local review applies before you plan exterior changes.

No transfer stamp in Carpentersville

Carpentersville has no transfer stamp requirement for real estate transactions, which makes it one of the simpler closings in the northwest suburbs.

The seller still has one task. Call the Water Billing Department at 847-551-3476 to schedule a final reading on the water meter. The new owner then opens service in person at Village Hall with a settlement statement or deed, a completed water application and picture identification.

State tax still applies. Illinois taxes the transfer of title at 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction thereof under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, based on the declaration filed for the sale.

Permits and inspections

The Community Development Department issues permits for construction, and even a new water heater or a shed needs some kind of permit or approval. The village links a list of work that does and does not need one.

  • Past work: if the previous owner added a deck, finished a basement or replaced a furnace, confirm the permit was closed.
  • Open work: a buyer who takes the house as-is takes the open permit with it.
  • Rental houses: the village runs a rental licensing program with an initial inspection and an annual license.

The rental licensing steps start with a temporary certificate after an application, then an inspection, then a follow-up inspection if violations are found, and a Crime Free Housing seminar the owner must attend. Ask Community Development for the current version of the checklist before you rely on it.

If you plan to sell a tenant-occupied house, remember that the owner is responsible for getting tenant consent for inspection visits.

Recording the deed in Kane County

The Kane County Recorder in Geneva keeps the land records for the village. The recorder's website offers a records search, and the office provides recording, copying, scanning and a tract department.

The recorder also runs a free Property Watch service aimed at deed fraud, which targets homeowners at risk of foreclosure. An owner of a vacant or inherited house may want to look at it.

The water account at closing

Water is the only village item that every Carpentersville seller must schedule. Call Water Billing as soon as you have a closing date, and ask for the final reading to match that date. Keep the final bill with your closing papers so the title company can see it was settled.

The new owner has to show up in person at Village Hall, so tell your buyer about it early. They bring the settlement statement or deed, a completed water application and picture identification. A buyer who learns this the day of closing may lose a day or two before service is in their name.

What happens at closing

With no village stamp, closing in Carpentersville comes down to the title company, the state declaration and the deed. The declaration sets the state tax at 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction thereof. After signing, the deed goes to the Kane County Recorder in Geneva, which records it and adds it to the land records.

Ask your title company for a settlement statement before the closing date and read each line. A cash purchase usually closes faster because no lender has to approve the buyer, though the same paperwork applies. Keep a copy of the deed and the statement for your own records.

Listing or cash sale?

A listing makes sense when the house is move-in ready and you can wait out showings and a buyer's financing. A cash sale as-is makes sense when repairs, a tenant, an inherited estate or a deadline would make a listing slow or costly.

Either way the village side is light: no municipal stamp, a final water reading and the permit review above. That leaves your time and repair costs as the real variables, so compare the net result of each route and not just the headline price.

Steps to take before you list

Start with the permit question, because it can take the longest to answer. Ask Community Development about any deck, basement, furnace or water heater work done since the house was built. Next, call Water Billing and set the final meter reading. Then gather the deed or settlement statement for the new owner's water application, and tell your title company which county recorder will file the deed.

If the house is a rental, ask about the license status and the inspection history, and tell the tenant about any inspection visit. A buyer who plans to keep the tenant will want to see the lease and the license together.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What a cash buyer will ask

Expect questions about the roof, the furnace, the basement and any open permits. A cash buyer pricing a house as-is counts those items against the offer, so having permit papers and repair receipts on hand can lift the number. Ask the buyer to confirm in writing who pays for the water reading, any open permit work and the recording step.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a village transfer stamp to sell in Carpentersville?

No. The village has no transfer stamp requirement for real estate sales. You should still schedule a final water meter reading by calling Water Billing at 847-551-3476.

What does the buyer need to start water service?

The new owner brings a settlement statement or deed to Village Hall in person, fills out the water application and shows picture identification.

Is a permit needed for a water heater or shed in Carpentersville?

In general, yes. Work from a new water heater or shed up to a full building requires some type of permit or approval. Check the village's list of work that does and does not need a permit before you start.

Which county records the deed?

Kane County. The Kane County Recorder in Geneva records deeds and offers an online records search.

How much did Carpentersville grow in the last census decade?

Slightly. The population rose from 37,691 in 2010 to 37,983 in 2020, a gain of 0.8 percent.

Before selling in Hanover Park

The biggest local step is the Village transfer stamp, which every Hanover Park seller has to buy before closing. The second is working out which county records your deed, since the village straddles Cook and DuPage counties. Everything else follows the usual path of listing, selling on your own, or accepting an as-is cash offer.

  • Listing with an agent: the most exposure, with showings and buyer repair requests.
  • Selling on your own: you manage the marketing and the paperwork, often with an attorney reviewing the contract.
  • As-is cash purchase: fewer contingencies and a closing date you can usually choose, with the buyer accepting the house's condition.

Start the stamp request early, because the Village needs notice and every balance owed to it has to be settled first.

If you are unsure whether anything is owed, ask Finance for a balance check before you accept an offer. A forgotten parking ticket or code invoice is the most common reason a stamp is held up.

A simple order of steps

Delays in Hanover Park usually come from the Village side of the sale, so work through it in order.

  1. Check your tax bill or title commitment for the county and the parcel number.
  2. Pay anything owed to the Village, including tickets, invoices, liens, judgments and the water balance, and ask Water Billing for the closing read.
  3. Fill out the MyDec or PTAX-203 form and the Village's Real Estate Transfer Tax Declaration form, and attach the deed.
  4. Call Finance at least three business days before closing, or email the set, and ask for the current stamp rate.
  5. Hand the stamp to your title company so the deed can be recorded with the right county office.

An as-is cash buyer removes the lender's appraisal and repair requests from the timeline, but the stamp, the water account and the county filing are still required. If the house is a rental, ask Code Enforcement about the license and any open violations at the same time, so nothing owed to the Village surfaces on closing week.

How the transfer stamp works

All residents selling a home in Hanover Park must buy a Transfer Tax Stamp from the Village before the closing. The homeowner, realtor or lawyer calls the Finance Department at 630-823-5790 at least three business days before closing, and walk-in requests are not honored.

  • Have the MyDec or PTAX-203 form ready.
  • Complete the Village of Hanover Park Real Estate Transfer Tax Declaration form.
  • Include the deed, and email the set to financedepartment@hpil.org if you prefer.
  • Pay everything owed to the Village first: tickets, invoices, liens, judgments and the final water bill.

A quitclaim deed also needs a stamp. In that case the Village asks for a copy of the signed, notarized deed plus its own declaration form. Ask Finance for the current stamp rate, since the amount depends on the value of the sale.

Do not wait for the last week. If the balance is clear and the reading is booked, the Finance Department can issue the stamp on the day you call, and your title company will not be chasing the Village for paperwork at the closing table.

Closing the water account

Water bills go out on the first of each month and are due by the 21st, whatever day of the week that falls on. A payment that is not received by then draws a 10 percent penalty, and a termination notice is mailed on the 22nd.

Because an unpaid final water bill blocks the transfer stamp, arrange the closing read with Water Billing early. You can email waterbilling@hpil.org with your property address in the subject line, and a representative replies with forms or instructions, so there is no need for a trip to Village Hall. Log in to your water account on the Village website to check the balance before you call.

Which county records the deed?

Hanover Park lies in both Cook and DuPage counties, so the recorder depends on where your parcel is. Your tax bill or title commitment shows the county and the parcel number.

For Cook County parcels, the Cook County Clerk's recordings office requires the preparer's and mail-to names and addresses, the common address, the Property Index Number and a legal description. A deed also needs grantor and grantee names and addresses, a completed MyDec declaration and any municipal transfer tax, which in Hanover Park is the stamp described above. An exemption statement is added where one applies.

For DuPage parcels, the DuPage County Recorder asks for a completed deed, the PTAX form or an exemption statement, municipal transfer stamps if applicable, the grantee's name and address for tax bills, the permanent parcel number, the legal description and the preparer's name and address. The DuPage office accepts PTAX-203 forms completed in MyDec and supports eRecording through several vendors. Title companies usually take care of these filings.

Hanover Park housing snapshot

Hanover Park is a dense suburb of about 6.5 square miles with 36,568 residents and large households. About 91.5 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which points to long tenure in many homes. Many sellers speak a language other than English at home, so plain-language or translated paperwork helps.

Of the 11,732 housing units counted in 2020, 2.8 percent were vacant. Metra's Hanover Park station on the Milwaukee District West Line is in fare zone 4, and Pace Route 554 reaches Elgin and Schaumburg.

School districts

Several districts overlap here, and six different public high schools serve the village. Elgin Area School District U-46 is the largest, covering about 90 square miles across Cook, DuPage and Kane counties.

  • Schaumburg Township Elementary District 54
  • Township High School District 211
  • Community Consolidated School District 93
  • Glenbard Township High School District 87
  • Keeneyville School District 20
  • Lake Park High School District 108

Your address determines the district, and buyers who have children check this first. Library service comes from the Poplar Creek Public Library District or the Schaumburg Township District Library depending on the part of town.

Selling a rental house

The Village licenses all residential rental properties, and the Code Enforcement Unit inspects them. An owner needs to pass an inspection and attend a landlord training seminar before getting a rental license. The Crime Free Multi-Housing Program requires landlords to attend training and use a crime free lease addendum.

If you are selling a rented house, ask Code Enforcement at 630-823-5570 about the license and any open violations before you list. You can report a problem on the 24 hour hotline at 630-823-5572, and an officer usually investigates within 24 to 48 hours. Building permits for work on the property come from the Community Development Department, not Code Enforcement.

Frequently asked questions

Do I have to buy a transfer stamp to sell my Hanover Park house?

Yes. The Village requires all home sellers to buy a Transfer Tax Stamp before closing. Call Finance at 630-823-5790 at least three business days ahead.

What blocks the stamp in Hanover Park?

Unpaid money owed to the Village. Tickets, invoices, liens, judgments and the final water bill must all be paid before the stamp is issued.

Does a quitclaim deed need the stamp?

Yes. A quitclaim deed requires a stamp, and the Village asks for a copy of the signed, notarized deed with its transfer tax declaration form.

Which county records my Hanover Park deed?

Cook County or DuPage County, depending on where the parcel sits. The village spans both, so check your tax bill or title paperwork.

When are Hanover Park water bills due?

On or before the 21st of each month. A balance unpaid by then gets a 10 percent penalty, so clear it before you request the transfer stamp.

Sell My House Fast in Rock Island, IL: Options, Costs and Cash Offers

Cash Home Buyers in Illinois

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Rock Island, IL sale

Sell Your Rock Island House for Cash

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Rock Island?
We buy Rock Island houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Which sale method fits a Rock Island owner?

You can hire an agent to list the house, market it yourself, or accept an offer from a buyer paying cash who will take the property as it is. Repairs, timing and whether the building is a home or a rental usually decide it.

Rock Island is one of the Quad Cities, alongside Moline and East Moline in Illinois and Davenport and Bettendorf in Iowa, so buyers come from both sides of the river. A tidy house can do well on the open market. A house that needs work, has a tenant, or sits on a rental-heavy block often fits a direct sale better. The trade-offs:

  • A listing reaches the most shoppers, though repairs and open-house hours usually come with it.
  • A private sale skips the agent's commission and leaves marketing, paperwork and negotiation to you.
  • A cash buyer needs no lender appraisal, so you can often pick the closing day.
  • For a rental, the city's license and inspection rules come first.

Get the price, the closing date and who pays which costs on paper before you shake hands on anything.

Home values and renters

Rock Island has about 36,225 residents, down from 37,108 at the 2020 census. Prices run modest: the middle value of an owner-occupied house is $125,900, and about 64.8% of occupied units are owned by the people living in them. The rest are rented, at a middle gross rent of $842.

That mix shapes who buys. Many sellers are landlords or heirs, and many buyers are local investors. An investor works backward from what tenants pay, so price a rental with area rents in mind. With values this modest, a repair bill can swallow a large share of the sale price, which is why owners of tired houses often look at as-is offers.

Older houses and what buyers ask about

Much of the city dates from the 1800s and early 1900s, especially downtown, around the Broadway Historic District, on Watch Hill and in the blocks near Augustana College. Houses from that era can carry original wiring, plaster walls and stone foundations. A buyer will want to know what has been updated, so gather receipts, permits and any inspection reports before you show the place.

If your address sits near a school district line, call the district before you advertise it. Rock Island-Milan School District 41 covers most of the city, while some southwest addresses belong to Rockridge. Plenty of shoppers narrow their search by district before they look at streets, so a wrong guess in a listing costs you credibility.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Rock Island house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Rental license and inspection rules

City ordinance requires a rental license for every residential rental, and each unit must pass an inspection against a minimum code standard before it is offered to tenants. Landlords apply through the city's self-service portal, and the Inspection Division emails to schedule the inspection after the rental fee is paid.

The owner or a designated agent has to be present. A $50 cancellation fee applies if nobody shows up or the visit is not canceled 24 hours ahead. A Notice of Violation lists items that fail life safety requirements. The first re-inspection is free, and each additional compliance inspection costs $50. The city can fine owners and revoke the license if repairs are not made in a reasonable time.

A license does not excuse unfixed violations. If you plan to sell a rental, clear any open violations or disclose them to the buyer in writing. The Inspection Division is at 1528 Third Avenue, and its staff can tell you where your license stands before you list.

Selling a rented house, step by step

You do not need a rental license to sell. The license covers renting a unit, not transferring it. Open violations on the file can still slow a deal, since a buyer's lender, inspector or title company may ask about them. A sensible order of work looks like this:

  • Call the Inspection Division and ask whether any notices are open on the address.
  • Fix life safety items first, because those are what trigger a Notice of Violation.
  • Pull together leases, deposit records and a list of repairs made.
  • Tell tenants in writing that the house is for sale, and agree on how showings will work.
  • Decide whether the buyer takes the house with the tenant in place or with the unit empty.

A cash buyer will often take a rental as it stands, tenants and open repair items included. That can save you the cost of bringing every unit up to standard before the sale, though you should still ask for the offer in writing with the closing date and any repair terms spelled out.

How a Rock Island deed is recorded

Deeds for Rock Island parcels are recorded with the Rock Island County Recorder. The fee schedule, set by county ordinance effective February 1, 2025, is below. Any document with a legal description also needs the 10-digit PIN.

Rock Island County Recorder fees
Document typeRecording fee
Conforming document$83
Certain exempt document types$64
Non-conforming document, or more than five references$104

Your title company normally handles the filing, but ask the Recorder's office to confirm the current fee before closing.

Transfers that are exempt from state transfer tax

The state transfer tax statute exempts a list of transfers, and some of them still require the declaration to be filed. Section 31-45 of the Property Tax Code lists these among the exempt items:

  • Deeds where the actual consideration is less than $100.
  • Tax deeds and deeds of partition.
  • Deeds that only correct or confirm an earlier deed.
  • Deeds to or from government bodies and charities.
  • Deeds given to a mortgage holder after foreclosure or as a substitute for it.

A normal sale to a buyer does not fall in these categories, so expect the tax to apply. Rock Island County also offers a no-cost Property Fraud Alert subscription that sends a notice whenever a filing mentions you. If you will leave the house empty for a while, enroll before you go.

What a cash sale lets you skip

A straight cash sale cuts out the slow parts of a listing: staging, open houses, haggling over inspection repairs, and the wait for a buyer's loan and appraisal. Title still has to be clean, the contract signed and the deed recorded at the county. A rental's license and inspection history will still interest the buyer.

Check the written offer for the price, the closing-cost split, the closing date and whether the house goes as is. Keep a copy of everything you sign.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a city rental license to sell a rented Rock Island house?

The license applies to renting a unit, so selling does not require one. Open inspection violations can still slow a sale, so ask the Inspection Division where your file stands.

How much do Rock Island houses cost?

The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $125,900. An individual house can land far above or below that, depending on size, condition and block.

Where is a Rock Island deed recorded?

With the Rock Island County Recorder. The fee schedule effective February 1, 2025 lists $83 for a conforming document and $104 for a non-conforming one. Confirm the current figure before closing.

What school district is my Rock Island house in?

Rock Island-Milan School District 41 covers most addresses. A few in the southwest belong to Rockridge, so verify yours with the district.

What happens if my rental has an open violation?

The city can fine owners and revoke the license if repairs are not made in a reasonable time. Fix the items or disclose them to the buyer, and ask the Inspection Division about the file.

Addison housing in brief

Addison is a DuPage County village where most sales involve a suburban house or condo that has to clear a short list of village steps before the deed can move. The July 1, 2025 population estimate is 35,758, a hair above the 35,702 recorded in 2020, so the housing stock is stable and fully built out.

Most houses date from after 1960, when farmland became subdivisions and the population jumped from 6,741 in 1960 to 24,482 in 1970. Owners value their homes at a typical $341,300, and 67.0% of homes are owner-occupied. Typical gross rent is $1,245. Expect buyers of these postwar houses to ask about roofs, furnaces and basements.

Village steps before an Addison sale can close

Addison will not issue a real estate transfer stamp until the sewer, permit, water and paperwork items on the Community Development and Finance pages are cleared. The deed cannot be transferred before the stamp is issued, so a missed item can push back the closing date.

  • Sewer compliance: the certificate cannot be older than six months on closing day, and the village wants the inspection booked two weeks early through Community Development at (630) 693-7530.
  • Permit release: confirms there are no open building permits or unpaid inspection fees. A release stays valid for two months only.
  • Water: the seller books a final meter reading 24 hours before closing and pays the final bill by noon the business day before closing. The buyer pre-registers for the water and sewer account.
  • Paperwork: the seller's attorney sends the village a copy of the PTAX-203 or PTAX-203A and a copy of the drafted deed.

Condominiums skip the water account and the sewer or sump inspection. A condo needs only the permit release.

Transfer stamp amounts

Addison transfer stamp amounts on the village real estate transfers page
Stamp typeAmountWho pays
Standard transfer stamp$2.50 for each $1,000 of purchase priceBuyer
Exempt transfer stamp (quitclaim, trust, foreclosure, sheriff sale)$50 administrative feeParty requesting the stamp
Transfer of beneficial interest$1.25 per $500 block, rounded upParty transferring

Separately, Section 31-10 of the Property Tax Code puts a state tax of 50 cents on every $500 block of value stated on the transfer declaration. When the deed says the property passes subject to a mortgage, the outstanding mortgage balance is left out of the basis. File the declaration on Form PTAX-203 or through the Department of Revenue's free MyDec system, and have the seller's attorney send the village its own copy at the water billing email on the village page.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Addison house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Quitclaim deeds, trusts and foreclosures

The village issues a zero-dollar exempt stamp for quitclaim deeds, deeds into a trust, foreclosures and sheriff sales, and it still charges the $50 processing fee. A lost stamp has to be repurchased in full, so keep the original in the closing file.

The exempt stamp needs the same sewer inspection, permit release and final water bill as a sale. The village also asks for its own Certificate of Exemption form and a copy of the signed and notarized deed. When the owner name on the deed is changing, the new owner opens a water and sewer account with two forms of identification. When the name is not changing, the water balance simply has to be paid before the stamp is released.

Heirs deeding an inherited Addison house should plan on the same items, even though no sale tax is due. Starting the sewer appointment early is the best way to protect the closing date.

Rules for an Addison house that is rented out

Every Addison dwelling that is not owner-occupied and charges rent needs an annual Residential Rental License. The license year runs May 1 to April 30, renewal notices arrive by mail in March, and renewals are due by April 30.

The village counts more than 1,000 rental properties and nearly 4,000 rental units, and it grades each property after an annual inspection. In a single-family house, condo or townhouse the inspector walks the interior. In a multi-family building the village inspects 20 percent of the units plus the common areas. Owners must also attend an 8-hour Crime Free Multi-Housing class within 90 days of getting a license.

Addison bans short-term rentals outright and classes them as a nuisance, so a buyer hoping to use a booking site is out of luck. A landlord selling a rental can email Rentals@addison-il.org or call the Rental Housing Supervisor line at (630) 693-7544 to ask how an open license year is handled at closing.

DuPage County property tax bills

DuPage County sends one bill with two installment coupons, and the tax covers the prior year. For 2025 taxes, bills went out on April 29, 2026, with payments due on the first of June and the first of September. The DuPage County Treasurer at 630-407-5900 can confirm the dates for the next cycle.

Addison spans Addison and Bloomingdale townships, so the township assessor named on the bill is the first contact for valuation questions. The treasurer's office does not set values. A yellow box on the bill means a mortgage servicer is already paying, and a second payment would later have to be refunded.

  • The general homestead exemption and the senior exemption are each $8,000.
  • Preliminary county figures for the 2025 levy showed assessed value up 8.2%, the average tax rate down 4.37% and the overall bill up 3.83%.
  • Individual bills differ by parcel because each one falls in a different mix of school, park and fire districts.

Because the bill arrives a year behind, ask the title officer how the current year's tax and any unpaid installment will be split between buyer and seller.

Appealing an assessment before you list

An owner can file with the DuPage County Board of Review, but only inside the 30-day window that opens when the township roll is published. Section 16-55 of the Property Tax Code sets the deadline at 30 calendar days after publication, and talking with the township assessor does not extend it.

The county asks for three or more comparable properties, with recent sales as the strongest evidence. Assessed values rest on the three prior years of sales, so the 2025 value drew on sales from 2022 through 2024. Written decisions usually arrive the following March. An owner who disagrees can go on to the state Property Tax Appeal Board or to court. An appeal challenges the assessed value only, and the tax rate stays with the local taxing districts.

Which sale route fits an Addison house?

Addison owners can hire an agent, sell on their own, or sell to a buyer who accepts the house in its current condition. A cash buyer still needs the same sewer certificate, permit release and final water bill, so the village timetable applies on every route. Inherited, tenant-occupied or heavily worn houses often go the as-is route because repairs would otherwise be negotiated after the buyer's inspection.

Whichever way you go, call Community Development first, ask what is open on your address and book the sewer inspection. Then line up the water readings and have your attorney prepare the declaration and deed copies so the stamp can be released on time.

Frequently asked questions

How far ahead should I book the Addison sewer inspection?

Call Community Development at (630) 693-7530 and set the appointment at least two weeks ahead. The certificate must be dated within six months of closing.

Who pays the Addison real estate transfer stamp?

The buyer. The standard rate is $2.50 for each $1,000 of purchase price.

Do condos in Addison need a sewer inspection?

No. Condos skip the water and sewer account and the sewer and sump pump inspection. A permit release is the only requirement.

Can a buyer run an Addison house as a short-term rental?

No. Addison prohibits short-term rentals and treats them as a nuisance. Long-term rentals need the annual Residential Rental License and an inspection.

What were the DuPage County property tax installment dates?

The 2025 taxes came due on the first of June and the first of September 2026. The DuPage County Treasurer can confirm the next dates, and you should check whether a mortgage servicer already pays your taxes before sending money.

Selling in Calumet City?

Who sells in Calumet City, and how

Sellers in Calumet City include longtime owners, landlords, heirs and people holding houses that sat empty. The 2020 census found about one in ten housing units vacant, and owners live in 55.7 percent of units, a lower share than in most nearby suburbs.

That mix produces three common routes: a listing handled by an agent, a sale you manage yourself, and a direct sale to a cash buyer who accepts repairs and tenants as they come. A listing suits an updated house, and a cash buyer suits a house a lender would balk at. Each route needs the city's transfer stamp and a paid final water bill.

Home values and what they mean for costs

A typical Calumet City home is worth $145,200 for 2020 through 2024, and typical gross rent is $1,177. Middle household income is $55,369, there are 14,332 households, and the one-way commute is 34.4 minutes. The 2020 count was 36,033 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 34,798, which is 3.5 percent below the 2020 base.

At these prices, flat costs such as the transfer stamp and the final water bill take a bigger bite out of proceeds than they would on a costlier house. Price against closed sales within a few blocks of yours instead of a metro-wide number. Higher vacancy means your house competes with empty units on the same blocks, and a clean, inspected house stands out most in that kind of market.

Transfer stamp cost

The clerk's Real Estate Transfer Declaration prints $4.00 per $1,000 or part thereof for the buyer and the same for the seller, which totals $8.00 per $1,000 or part thereof. The form is written for transfers up to and including $2 million.

  • Collect the stamps at least 48 hours ahead and leave about half an hour for processing.
  • Only certified checks, money orders or cash are taken.
  • Whoever requests the stamp must be the owner of record, an attorney or a broker, and an agent writes a bar or license number on the form.
  • An exempt transfer cites a paragraph of Sec. 82-323 of the municipal code and submits a copy of the deed.

The City Clerk's office answers at (708) 891-8110, Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The form lists Thornton Township and ZIP code 60409 for the property.

Every outstanding water bill has to be paid before a property is sold. The seller or the seller's representative orders a final meter reading at least 48 hours before the stamp is bought. Call Water Billing at (708) 891-8121 to schedule it.

Rentals and vacant houses

The city's Forms and Applications page lists a rental application, an annual rental code compliance letter, an owner-occupied form, a Crime Free Housing licensing application and a vacant and foreclosed property registration. A landlord selling a rental should confirm that the application and the compliance letter are current, because a buyer's attorney tends to ask for them.

Ask Building and Zoning, (708) 891-8120, whether the vacant and foreclosed registration applies to your house and whether any permit or violation is open on the address. The same page offers permit forms for building, electrical, plumbing, HVAC and fences, and an overhead sewer rebate program form. A quick call before you accept an offer avoids surprises after the inspection.

Where the deed is recorded

Cook County's Clerk runs the Recordings Division, which keeps office hours from 9 to 5 and accepts its last customer at 4:45. Buyer and seller also complete the PTAX-203 Illinois declaration.

The state levies its own tax of 50 cents per $500. Home rule municipalities may add theirs, and Calumet City's stamp falls into that category. For the property tax proration, exemptions appear as deductions on the second installment bill, so ask the County Treasurer for the amounts and due dates on your parcel.

Whom to call first

Three city numbers cover most of a handover: the clerk at (708) 891-8110, Water Billing at (708) 891-8121 and Public Works at (708) 891-8161. Call them in that order if you want the stamp price, the meter reading and any street or utility question settled before the closing date.

Buyers often compare Calumet City with houses in Hammond, Lansing, Dolton and South Holland, so state commute and highway access in a listing. A cash buyer comfortable with tenants in place, an older furnace or an overhead sewer can often close faster than a buyer who needs a loan, while a retail buyer pays more for a house that has been updated.

Order of steps at the city

Start with the final meter reading, since it has the longest lead time. Once the water account is closed out and paid, bring the signed declaration and the payment to the clerk at least 48 hours before you need the stamps. Allow about half an hour at the counter. If the transfer is exempt, cite the paragraph of Sec. 82-323 and bring a copy of the deed.

If an agent handles the stamp for you, make sure the form shows the agent's bar or license number. A form that comes back incomplete can cost you the extra days you did not budget for.

Selling an inherited or empty house

Heirs often inherit a house that has sat empty. Start by confirming who is the owner of record, because only the owner, an attorney or a broker can request the stamp. Then ask Building and Zoning about the vacant and foreclosed registration and any open violation, order the final meter reading, and collect any permit records. A buyer who pays cash and takes the house as-is can close without waiting on a lender's inspection list.

Keep copies of everything you submit to the city, along with the receipts, so the title company can match each payment on the settlement statement. If a buyer asks about the rental or vacancy forms, tell them what you filed and when, and hand over the paperwork right away, in writing if possible.

How is a final water reading ordered in Calumet City?

Call Water Billing at (708) 891-8121. The city asks for the order at least 48 hours before the stamp is bought, and all water bills must be paid before the sale.

What payment does the stamp office accept?

Certified check, money order or cash only. Plan to pick the stamps up at least 48 hours ahead.

Which office records a Calumet City deed?

The Cook County Clerk's Recordings Division, because the city is in Cook County. It takes customers until 4:45 p.m.

Can a rental house in Calumet City be sold?

Yes. The city has a rental application and an annual compliance letter, so confirm both are in order and ask Building and Zoning at (708) 891-8120 about open permits before signing a contract.

Selling in Northbrook

Northbrook is one of the simpler Cook County villages to sell in on paper, because it charges no municipal transfer tax and issues no transfer stamps. The one local step is closing out the water account with a final meter reading.

The village sits on the North Shore and has 34,744 residents (July 2025 estimate). Housing is mostly owner-occupied (87.2%) and high in value, with a median owner-occupied value of $652,300, so most of a seller's effort goes into pricing and condition. About 91.9% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which means few homes change hands in a given year and comparable sales can be thin on a specific block. Ask an agent or appraiser for nearby sales, since the village median hides block-by-block differences.

Transfer tax and stamps

Northbrook does not levy a real estate transfer tax or issue transfer stamps, and the Cook County Clerk's municipal transfer tax list has no entry for the village.

The state and county taxes still apply, with the seller as the liable party. The state rate comes from 35 ILCS 200/31-10. A sale also needs the PTAX-203 transfer declaration.

Closing out the water account

Northbrook Municipal Code Section 27-63 requires everyone in a property transaction to confirm with the village that a final meter reading was taken and that no unpaid water balance remains. Call the water billing office at 847-664-4171 to set that up.

  • Water is billed quarterly, and sewer and stormwater charges ride on the same bill.
  • If the seller leaves a balance, the code ties it to the property, and it moves to the new owner's account after thirty days.
  • Close any utility accounts and schedule final reads as part of the sale.

Settling the final bill at the closing table avoids a dispute with the buyer later. For liens and other debts, search the Cook County Property Tax Portal. Its records may not be complete, so a FOIA request to the village for building permits and other outstanding items on a parcel is a sensible extra check.
