Assessments and property tax

Most of Northbrook lies in Northfield Township, and a northwest corner lies in Wheeling Township. Both are north suburb townships on the Cook County Assessor's triennial reassessment cycle.

Look up your parcel's township and 14-digit PIN on the Assessor's site. The township assessor for Northfield can answer questions about an appeal. For installment dates and the balance on a parcel, ask the Cook County Treasurer, because the closing statement usually prorates the bill.

Schools and neighborhood

Several elementary districts, numbered 27, 28, 30 and 31, serve the village, and High School District 225 feeds Glenbrook North High School. A small northwest corner falls in Wheeling's District 21, and a southeast sliver is in Sunset Ridge District 29. Because district boundaries cross house by house, a listing should name the exact elementary and junior high district for the address. The village's Know Your Neighborhood tool shows zoning and school districts by property.

Metra's Milwaukee District North Line stops at Northbrook station on Shermer Road downtown, and shopping runs along Sanders Road, Skokie Boulevard and Lake Cook Road. Mean travel time to work is 26.8 minutes, so name the train and the main roads in a listing.

Recording the deed in Cook County

Northbrook deeds are recorded through the Cook County Clerk's recordings office at 118 N. Clark St., phone 312.603.5050, which also lists the state and county stamp amounts. A rubber stamp is the proof of payment.

Because Northbrook has no municipal stamp, the closing package is lighter than in many neighboring suburbs. You still need a signed deed, the PTAX-203 declaration, clear title and a final water read. If a trust or estate holds the title, the title company will tell you which exemption language applies.

Listing or direct sale?

At these prices, most Northbrook houses sell through a standard listing, since buyers usually arrive with a mortgage. A direct sale makes sense when the house needs more work than a listing can absorb or a family needs a quick, quiet close.

  • Choose a listing when the house is updated and you can wait for showings.
  • Choose a direct cash sale when the property is dated, a tenant or estate issue slows a listing, or you need a firm closing date.
  • Either way, arrange the final water read, confirm liens through the Cook County portal, and order the PTAX-203.

With no village stamp to wait on, the Northbrook side of a quick sale can move fast: book the water read, gather the deed and declaration, and let the title company handle recording.

A short checklist for sellers

Put four items in one folder: the latest Cook County tax bill with your PIN, your loan payoff statement if you have a mortgage, the water account details, and any permit records for additions or major work. A buyer's attorney will ask for most of these, and the title company needs them to prorate the tax bill.

Call 847-664-4171 as soon as you have a closing date so the final reading lands on or near it. If the title is in a trust or estate, send the trust certificate or letters of office to the title company early so the deed language is settled before the closing table.

How a quick Northbrook sale unfolds

A direct sale here has few moving parts. You agree on a price and a closing date, and the title company opens the file. You schedule the final water read, the title company checks for liens, and you sign the deed and the PTAX-203 declaration. The deed is then recorded with the Cook County Clerk, and the state and county stamps are paid, with the seller liable for both.

What can slow it down is an unpaid water balance, an open lien that turns up in the portal search, or a trust or estate that needs extra paperwork. Ask about each early. If the house needs work, a cash buyer can take it as it stands, and you skip repair negotiations and the wait for a lender's appraisal.

If you plan to list instead, expect showings and a mortgage-driven timeline, and have the water read and lien check done before the first offer.

Frequently asked questions

No. The village does not levy a transfer tax or issue transfer stamps. State and Cook County transfer taxes still apply on the deed.

What must I do about the water bill when I sell?

Call 847-664-4171 to schedule a final meter reading and pay the balance. Section 27-63 of the municipal code requires the final read, and any unpaid amount moves to the new owner after thirty days.

Which school districts serve Northbrook houses?

Elementary districts 27, 28, 30 and 31 serve most of the village, and District 225's Glenbrook North High School serves most of it. Small areas fall in Wheeling's District 21 or Sunset Ridge District 29, so check the exact address.

Which township assessor handles my Northbrook property?

Most of the village is in Northfield Township and a corner is in Wheeling Township. Look up your PIN on the Cook County Assessor's site to confirm the township.

How do I check for liens before listing?

Use Cook County's Property Tax Portal to search for liens or debts on the parcel. Its records may not be complete, so a FOIA request to the village for building permits and other debts is a good second check.

How a North Chicago sale works

A North Chicago sale runs through two layers of paperwork: the city's own transfer stamp and sale inspection, then the Lake County Clerk's recording desk. An owner can hire an agent, sell alone, or take a direct offer from a buyer willing to accept the property as it is.

North Chicago is a Lake County city on the Lake Michigan shore, directly south of Waukegan. Population is 34,050 (July 2025 estimate). Only 32.6% of homes are owner-held, the middle value of owned homes is $159,600, and typical rent is $1,426. Those are citywide medians, so a closed sale on your own street is a better guide than the citywide number.

A sale cannot close with a stamped deed until the city has checked for unpaid bills and, for any building, completed a sales inspection. Starting early keeps a closing date from slipping.

Steps the city requires before you sell

The city requires a transfer stamp on every sale inside its limits. It is released only after debts are cleared and the sale inspection is done. The order is:

  1. Call the Comptroller's Office at 847-596-8600 and the Department of Economic and Community Development at 847-596-8650 to request an outstanding payment and lien check.
  2. Pay anything the check turns up. The stamp is not issued until those payments are made.
  3. If the property has a building on it, schedule the sales inspection with Economic and Community Development.
  4. After the inspection, the buyers sign a Buyer's Acknowledgement form and give it to the Comptroller's office, which issues the stamp.
  5. The stamp goes on the deed, and the buyer or seller records the deed with the Lake County Recorder.

A Zoning Verification Letter before a sale states whether a use or structure is legal nonconforming, which can answer a buyer's questions about an old garage, an extra unit or a converted basement. The request form goes to the Economic and Community Development office at City Hall.

Permit questions go to permits@northchicago.org or 847-596-8650. Permit reviews take about 10 business days when volume is normal, so ask about timing if the inspection turns up work that needs a permit.

State and Lake County transfer tax

Section 31-10 of 35 ILCS 200 sets the state tax at 50¢ for each $500 or fraction of $500. Lake County adds 25¢ per $500, and the county issues one stamp covering both. The Lake County Clerk collects the tax at recording, and the contract decides whether buyer or seller pays it.

North Chicago is one of the municipalities the county names as requiring its own stamp or exemption letter before the deed is submitted. Get that from the city first.

  • Only the stamped deed is recorded. The PTAX-203 goes to the county assessment office.
  • Recordings are filed at the Lake County Clerk's Recording Division, 18 N County St, 6th Floor, Waukegan, 847-377-2575.

Ask the Clerk's office for the exact figure that applies to your deed.

Landlord and short-term rental rules

These matter if the house has ever been rented. Any dwelling not occupied by its owner falls under the landlord license rules in City Code Title 5, Chapter 14, whether or not rent is charged. The license runs January 1 to December 31, and inspections must be passed every two years for the certificate of compliance.

  • Short-term rentals need an endorsement on top of the landlord license, and only 25 endorsements are available per year, first come, first served.
  • Short-term rentals also owe the city's 9.5% hotel and motel tax, remitted monthly.
  • Rental properties with four or more units must have a Knox Box key box for Fire Department access under City Code Title 3, Chapter 2, Section 14.
  • Vacant and foreclosed properties must be registered through the HERA Property Registry, with a fee.
  • The city enforces the 2021 International Building, Residential, Mechanical, Fuel Gas, Fire, Property Maintenance and Existing Building codes, along with the 2020 National Electric Code.

An inherited house with a former tenant, or a house left empty, is where these rules most often trip up a sale. Ask the building department whether the address is registered, ideally before an offer arrives.

Lake County property taxes at closing

Lake County sends one bill with two installment coupons, and penalty interest is added the day after each due date. The county publishes a new calendar each year, and the Treasurer's office can tell you which installments are paid on your parcel.

At closing, the title company usually splits the year's tax between buyer and seller. Bring the latest bill to the closing table and phone the Lake County Treasurer if any installment shows as open. An unpaid installment stays attached to the parcel and becomes the next owner's problem unless it is settled in the closing statement.

Local setting

North Chicago Community Unit School District 187 runs the public schools. Two Metra stations, North Chicago and Great Lakes, serve the Union Pacific North Line, with trains south to Chicago and north to Kenosha, and Pace buses link the city to Waukegan. Main roads include Sheridan Road, Green Bay Road, Waukegan Road, Skokie Highway, Buckley Road and the Tri-State Tollway.

Most of the city drains toward the lake, while the western edge drains to the North Branch of the Chicago River. Ask the building department about any past drainage or basement water complaints on your street before you list.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy North Chicago houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Agent, as-is sale or cash buyer

The choice depends on condition, timing and what the sales inspection might find. A public listing reaches the most buyers but adds showings, repair requests and a longer timeline. A direct cash sale moves faster and accepts the house with its flaws, and it still goes through the same stamp, inspection and recording steps.

  • Hire an agent and list publicly if the house shows well and you can wait for a financed buyer.
  • Sell as-is when repairs, a code violation, a former tenant or probate paperwork makes a normal listing hard.
  • Get the lien check and sales inspection started first in either case, because both can reveal debts or defects that change the price.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a city transfer stamp to sell in North Chicago?

Yes. The city requires a transfer stamp on any sale inside its limits, and it will not issue one until outstanding payments and liens are cleared and, for a building, the sales inspection is done. The stamp goes on the deed before it is recorded.

Which office handles the sales inspection?

Call the Department of Economic and Community Development at 847-596-8650 or write to permits@northchicago.org. The Comptroller's Office at 847-596-8600 handles the lien and payment check and issues the stamp after the buyers sign the Buyer's Acknowledgement.

What is the Illinois and Lake County transfer tax rate?

Illinois takes 50¢ per $500 and Lake County takes 25¢ per $500, both collected by the Lake County Clerk when the deed is filed. The city stamp is separate, so confirm its amount with the Comptroller's Office.

Can I sell a North Chicago rental house with tenants in it?

Yes, but the unit must be covered by a landlord license, since any dwelling not occupied by its owner falls under City Code 5-14. Ask the building department for the certificate of compliance status, because a buyer or lender may want to see it.

Where does the deed get filed after closing?

At the Lake County Clerk's Recording Division, 18 N County St, 6th Floor, Waukegan, phone 847-377-2575. The stamped deed is the document filed, while the PTAX-203 declaration goes to the assessment office.

Selling a house in Woodridge

Woodridge is a DuPage County village southwest of Chicago, with small pieces reaching into Will and Cook counties. A seller here is usually dealing with a post-war suburban house, townhome or condo. The 1960 census counted 542 people, the 1970 census 11,028, and the 2020 census 34,158, and most homes went up after the 1950s, so many houses are now old enough to need a new roof, windows, furnace or a rebuilt basement. School districts by address

It depends on the street. Woodridge has no high school of its own, and the village is split among several districts, so the district for your house can change the buyer pool. The village lists six: Center Cass 66, Community High School District 99, Lemont-Bromberek 113A, Lemont Township High School District 210, Naperville 203 and Woodridge School District 68.

  • Woodridge School District 68 runs six elementary schools for grades K-6, plus Jefferson Junior High for grades 7 and 8.
  • Most high school students go to Downers Grove North or South in District 99.

Say the district name in your listing or when you talk to a cash buyer. It shapes price expectations more than a dated kitchen does.

The Woodridge transfer stamp

Anyone selling property in Woodridge has to buy a Real Estate Transfer Stamp from the village before the deed is recorded. Stamps can take 60 minutes or longer to process and sometimes 24 hours or more, so allow time, or drop the paperwork off with a phone number and wait for a call.

Village Hall is at 5 Plaza Drive. The village does not accept stamp paperwork by email or fax, and original documents must be brought in or mailed with a self-addressed, postage-paid envelope. Questions go to 630-719-4909 or epay@woodridgeil.gov. Ask Village Hall for the current stamp amount before closing day, because it is a village charge and the closing agent will need the figure.

  • An exempt stamp is available when the transfer qualifies for an exemption under the state Transfer Tax Law.
  • A refund of the village transfer tax is available to someone who sold a primary residence in Woodridge and bought another residence in Woodridge.
  • Payment by check is converted to an electronic transfer, so the bank account can be debited the same day.
  • Mortgage lenders starting a foreclosure on a Woodridge home send a copy of the foreclosure notice to the Village Clerk at Village Hall.

Recording happens at the county, and a signed transfer declaration goes in with the deed or within three business days of the transfer, whichever is sooner (35 ILCS 200/31-25). Woodridge parcels can lie in DuPage, Will or Cook County, so confirm which recorder handles yours.

Work must begin within three months and finish within one year of the permit.

If a house has an unfinished basement or addition, call Building Permits and Inspections at 630-719-4750 before you list, so a buyer does not inherit an open permit. Construction hours are limited: between September 1 and May 31 the village bars work after 7:00 p.m. Monday through Saturday, and on Sundays allows it only from 10:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m. Summer evenings run later, to 9:00 p.m.

The village also runs a Residential Rental Program. Owners of three or more multi-family units need an annual license by January 1 and take part in a yearly inspection. Owners of single-family rentals, or two or fewer multi-family units, register at no fee. Both groups complete a four-hour crime free housing seminar once, and the certificate goes with the registration. An investor who buys your house to rent it will need to complete the same steps.

Storms, flooding and disclosure

Inspectors and buyers look closely at roofs, basements and drainage. On June 20, 2021, an EF-3 tornado struck just after 11 p.m. and damaged 225 homes in Woodridge and neighboring suburbs. Storm repairs are one reason a roof or siding permit shows up in a house history.

Stormwater is another: the village enforces the 2019 DuPage County Countywide Stormwater and Floodplain Ordinance as part of its building codes. If a basement has had water, say so on the disclosure form and keep the repair records. A large limb over the roof is also a fair item for a buyer to raise.

Selling without repairs

Three routes exist: an agent listing, a sale by the owner, and a purchase by someone paying cash who takes the house as it sits. Each ends with a village stamp, a recorded deed and a closing statement, so what changes is the timeline and who pays for repairs.

  • Agent listing: works when the house shows well and you can sit through showings, inspection demands and a buyer's loan approval.
  • Owner sale: avoids a commission, but disclosure forms, the contract and the village stamp become your job.
  • Cash purchase: no loan underwriting and no repair haggling, which helps with inherited houses, open permits, tenant trouble or a firm move date.

Compare what each route leaves in your pocket after repairs, carrying costs, the stamp and the months of waiting.

Property tax collection

The tax bill comes from the county where the parcel sits, so a Woodridge owner may deal with DuPage, Will or Cook County. Your bill lists the taxing districts, including the school district, park district and the fire protection district. Woodridge has no fire department of its own and is covered by the Lisle-Woodridge, Darien-Woodridge and Lemont fire districts, which each levy their own tax.

Before you sign a contract, ask the county treasurer where every installment on your parcel stands, and ask who is handling the proration at the table. The village website has a Property and Tax Information section with pages on buying or selling a home and on municipal taxes.

Frequently asked questions

Does the seller or the buyer deal with the Woodridge transfer stamp?

The seller needs to buy it, since anyone selling property in Woodridge must purchase a Real Estate Transfer Stamp. Your closing agent or attorney usually brings the paperwork to Village Hall at 5 Plaza Drive, because the village does not take stamp paperwork by email or fax.

Can I get my village transfer tax back if I stay in Woodridge?

Yes, in one situation. The village offers a refund when you sold your primary residence in Woodridge and then purchased another residence in Woodridge. Contact the Finance Department at 630-719-4909 to learn what documents it wants.

Which county records the deed for a Woodridge house?

Most of the village is in DuPage County, but small portions lie in Will and Cook counties. The county of your parcel decides which recorder takes the deed and which treasurer sends the tax bill, so check your parcel number with the closing agent.

Does a recent roof or water heater replacement need village paperwork?

Yes, both jobs need a village permit, and Community Development can issue permits for roofs and water heaters the same day. If the work is already done without one, call 630-719-4750 and ask how to close it out before the buyer's inspection.

Does Woodridge regulate rental houses that I might sell to an investor?

Yes. Single-family rental owners register at no fee, and owners of three or more multi-family units hold an annual license with village inspections. Every owner or manager attends a crime free housing seminar once, so an investor buyer should plan for that step.

How homeowners in St. Charles usually sell

Most use one of three paths: a listing through a broker, a sale they run themselves, or a cash purchase with no repairs requested. Repair needs and how rigid your timeline is usually decide it.

  • Broker listing: suits an updated house and an owner who can host showings for several weeks.
  • Owner-run sale: saves the agent's commission but puts pricing, marketing and negotiation on you.
  • Cash buyer: closes without loan approval, which helps with inherited houses, tenants in place or a pending relocation.

St. Charles homes tend to sell on location and condition. If yours has an open permit, an unfinished project or deferred maintenance, sort that out first, because open permits can hold up a sale.

St. Charles prices and long-time owners

St. Charles has an estimated 33,594 residents and 13,161 households. About 70.3% of homes are lived in by their owners, and the median home value is $377,400. Median gross rent is $1,819 and median household income is $114,300. Owner cost runs $2,381 a month with a mortgage and $1,102 without one.

Long tenure and an older age profile mean estate sales are a regular part of the local market. Buyers often compare a house near the river or the downtown grid with nearby Geneva and Batavia, so be ready to explain what sets your block apart. Families ask about schools early. St. Charles Community Unit School District 303 runs the public schools, so get your attendance zone from the district, not from a neighbor.

Permits and open permits

Take permit questions to the Building Division on the ground floor of City Hall, 2 E. Main Street, or call (630) 377-4406. The city says open permits can hold up the sale of a home, and that a disapproved final inspection means the work must be corrected before the sale.

Which projects need a St. Charles permit
ProjectPermit needed?

The city runs its own electric utility, which is why electrical permits include a service application. Work done without a permit can be charged double fees once you apply, and a citation with an adjudication hearing is possible if you wait too long.

Plat of survey and city limits

A plat of survey submitted with a permit application must be 11 by 17 inches. If you lost yours, the Building Division can check its files.

Many homes carry a St. Charles mailing address but sit outside city limits. A letter in the numeric address, such as 12N123, signals unincorporated Kane County, where permits come from the county. St. Charles lies in both Kane and DuPage counties, so confirm which county holds your parcel number.

Why a St. Charles tax bill can rise

For a Kane County parcel, a township assessor sets the first value and the Supervisor of Assessments equalizes it. A DuPage County parcel goes through DuPage offices instead.

A bill can rise even when a value does not. Your exemptions may be incomplete, neighbors may qualify for exemptions you lack, taxing bodies may have raised levies, or your value may have moved faster than the neighborhood average. The largest share of a bill goes to schools, and the county cannot set another government's levy. The Property Tax Extension Limitation Law applies in Kane and generally caps levy increases at 5 percent or the rate of inflation, whichever is lower. New construction, bonded debt and voter-approved increases fall outside that cap.

Appealing an assessment

Complaints for a given year go to the Kane County Board of Review within 30 days of the township roll being published, and a bill that has already arrived is too late unless a complaint was filed. You can look at the township assessor's records for any parcel, including your own, to see how neighbors are valued. Your parcel number appears on your tax bill and your assessment notice. If your parcel's taxes were sold, redeem them at the County Clerk's tax extension office, 630-232-5964.

What is filed and taxed at closing

Your deed is filed in whichever county contains the parcel, and the title company usually handles the filing. State law prices the transfer tax at 50 cents per $500 of value, paid with revenue stamps from the recorder, and a MyDec report goes to the Department of Revenue.

The county's share, the recording fee and any city requirement are separate questions. Ask the Kane County Recorder, or the DuPage County Recorder for a DuPage parcel, and ask City Hall whether a final read is needed on a water or electric account. The settlement statement will show every charge.

A cash sale in St. Charles without surprises

A cash buyer takes the house without asking for repairs and without waiting on loan approval, so the work left is mostly paper. Close out open permits, confirm the county, locate your survey, and ask the city about the electric and water accounts. Then agree the price, the closing date and who pays each recording cost in the contract. Keep a copy of the signed contract and the closing statement. A listing may bring more on a well-kept house, but a cash sale gives you a firm date and fewer showings.

Selling an inherited St. Charles house

Estate sales are common here, and they follow the same local steps as any other. Find the deed and the latest tax bill, then ask the Building Division whether any permit is still open on the address. Old work on a deck, water heater or air conditioner is the usual culprit. If a permit was never closed, ask the division what inspection the city needs so the file can be cleared before a buyer's title company finds it. Keep the electric and water accounts active until the deed records, since the buyer's walkthrough often happens in the last days.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Papers to have ready

Before you accept an offer, set out your deed, a recent tax bill, your plat of survey, any permit records and receipts for major repairs. If tenants live in the house, add the lease. Share them with the title company at the start, so the stamps, the MyDec report and the recording are prepared together and nobody waits on a missing page. If your house is in DuPage County, ask that county's recorder for its own requirements early, since they can differ from Kane's.

Frequently asked questions

Will an open permit delay my St. Charles closing?

It can. The city states that open permits can hold up the sale of a home, and unfinished or failed work must be corrected before the transfer.

Is my St. Charles address inside city limits?

Not always. If the numeric address contains a letter, such as 12N123, the property is in unincorporated Kane County and permits come from the county.

Can I protest my St. Charles assessment after the tax bill arrives?

Generally no. Complaints for a given year must go to the Board of Review within 30 days of the township roll being published, and a bill that has already arrived is too late unless a complaint was filed.

Who handles electric service when a St. Charles house changes hands?

The city operates its own electric utility. Ask the city about the account transfer for your address.

What do I need for a fence permit?

A permit is required for a new or replacement fence, and the plat of survey must show where it sits. Submitted surveys must be 11 by 17 inches.

Selling a house in Mundelein

Population is 32,680 (July 2025 estimate), the typical owner-occupied home is worth $309,700, and 71.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Owners generally compare an agent listing, a self-managed sale and a cash purchase of the house in its present state.

Housing reflects the village's growth: ranches and tri-levels were built in the center of town in the 1950s and 1960s, and larger two-story houses followed on the edges from the 1970s. A tri-level near the old center and a newer two-story near the village edge attract different buyers, and their repair needs differ too. Households average 2.72 people, so buyers may look hard at bedroom count and basement space. Bilingual listing materials can reach more buyers.

Recording a deed in Lake County

Deeds are filed with the Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk, on the sixth floor at 18 N County Street in Waukegan (847-377-2575). Fees are $70 for a standard document and $82 for a non-standard one, and the only extra charges at recording are the state and county transfer taxes.

State tax under 35 ILCS 200/31-15 is fifty cents for every $500 of value. The clerk names six municipalities whose deeds need local stamps or a signed exemption certificate: Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa and North Chicago. Mundelein is not one of them. Most deeds qualify for eRecording, but a deed with a paper PTAX-203 cannot be submitted that way.

Five elementary districts divide the village, so the one for your street varies: Diamond Lake School District 76, Fremont School District 79, Hawthorn Community Consolidated School District 73, Libertyville School District 70 and Mundelein Elementary School District 75. Mundelein High School serves the village.

  • Bus: Pace Route 574 links Mundelein with Grayslake, Vernon Hills and other stops.
  • Streets: Lake Street, Illinois Route 60, Illinois Route 83, Maple Avenue, Midlothian Road and Hawley Street carry most traffic.
  • Interstate: Interstate 94 is five miles east.

The village hall sits on a 10-acre site next to the Metra station, so homes within walking distance of that area are easy to market on convenience. A typical commute lasts 27.9 minutes.

Diamond Lake, flooding and new construction

Diamond Lake is a 153-acre glacial lake in south Mundelein, used for fishing, swimming and boating. Homes near it may appeal to buyers who want water access, and a lakefront or creekside lot should prompt you to confirm flood zone status before you list. Disclose any water events at your own address on the seller report.

Inspectors test the roof, furnace and sump pump here, since winters are cold and summers can run hot.

New construction is also worth watching. In 2022 the village annexed more than 700 acres of land owned by the Wirtz family, where the plan was to build 1,200 houses and 600 townhomes. Price against what buyers can find new as well as resale houses.

A cash buyer may close within a short window and buy without repairs. A listing may bring more money but takes more time. Let your deadline choose.

The order of steps is simple, and most of the work is gathering paper early.

  2. Pull permit records for additions, decks, roofs, furnaces and finished basements. Call the village at 847-949-3283 if a record is missing.
  3. Ask the village about final water billing so the account closes on the sale date.
  4. Prepare the deed and the transfer declaration. Mundelein does not need a local stamp, so the clerk's recording fee and the state and county transfer taxes are the charges to plan for.
  5. File the deed with the Lake County Clerk in Waukegan or through eRecording, unless it carries a paper PTAX-203, which has to go in person.

A seller who wants speed can ask a cash buyer for a short closing and no repair requests. A seller who wants the highest price can list with an agent and plan for showings, inspections and a lender's timeline.

Whichever route you take, keep the parcel number, tax bill and payoff statement together so the closing does not wait on a missing page.

What to bring when you record

Bring or upload the signed deed, the transfer declaration and the parcel number. If you plan to use eRecording, check first that the deed qualifies, since a deed with a paper PTAX-203 cannot be submitted that way. If you go in person, the Recording Division is on the sixth floor at 18 N County Street in Waukegan, and the staff at 847-377-2575 can confirm which fee applies to your document.

Ask your title company or attorney who handles recording. In many sales they file the deed for you, but you still need to supply the permit records, tax bill and water account details that go into the closing file.

No. The Lake County Clerk lists six municipalities needing local stamps or an exemption certificate: Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa and North Chicago. The state tax of fifty cents per $500 still applies.

Which office takes a Mundelein deed for recording?

The Lake County Clerk's Recording Division, 18 N County Street, 6th Floor, Waukegan, in person or by eRecording through an approved vendor. Call 847-377-2575.

How much does Lake County charge to file a deed?

$70 for a standard document and $82 for a non-standard one, with state and county transfer taxes as the only additions at recording.

One of five: Diamond Lake 76, Fremont 79, Hawthorn CCSD 73, Libertyville 70 or Mundelein Elementary 75. Confirm by address. Mundelein High School handles the older grades.

Use the Permit Application and Homeowner Project Guide posted by the Village, and call customer service at 847-949-3283 or email building@mundelein.org with questions.

Ways to sell in O'Fallon, Illinois

O'Fallon owners can go with an agent, run the sale themselves, or accept an offer from a company that buys for cash. The right pick turns on the house's condition, the lender's timeline and how much repair work you are willing to manage.

This O'Fallon is in St. Clair County, east of St. Louis, and it is not the O'Fallon in St. Charles County, Missouri, so make sure any records or tax searches use the Illinois city. Population is 32,656, up from 32,289 in 2020. Much of the housing stands in subdivisions built since the 1980s and again after Interstate 64 was widened in the 1990s, with names such as Thornbury Hill, Nolin Creek Estates, Fairwood Hills, Deer Creek and Forest Hills.

  • An agent listing makes sense when the house is ready to occupy and similar sales nearby are easy to find.
  • A sale by owner works when you have the time to show the house and handle paperwork with a title company.
  • A cash purchase works for deferred maintenance, a leased rental, or an inherited property. Get any offer in writing and set it beside a listing price minus commission and repairs.

Scott Air Force Base and buyers on orders

O'Fallon is about 5 miles from Scott Air Force Base and roughly 17 miles from downtown St. Louis, which puts a major employer within a short drive. Many residents work at the base, both military and civil service.

If you deal with a buyer who is moving on orders, expect a firm closing date, and keep repair receipts, appliance manuals and a recent utility history ready so the paperwork moves quickly. Which school district the house is in is the next question such buyers ask. Three districts overlap in O'Fallon: Community Consolidated School District 90, Central School District 104 and O'Fallon Township High School District 203. Print the correct one on your listing sheet.

Is an occupancy permit needed when ownership changes?

Yes. The city requires an occupancy permit when the ownership or occupancy of a home changes and no current permit is on file. A residential permit costs $75 as of May 1, 2025 and stays valid for two years.

The city treats the permit as a property maintenance inspection. After you apply, the schedule runs like this:

  • Call to book the inspection appointment within 7 days of applying.
  • Plan on the inspection taking place inside a month of the application.
  • Any violations must be fixed, and the permit follows within a second 30-day window after that first inspection.
  • Water and electricity must be on during the inspection.

The house may be occupied before the inspection as long as no life safety problems exist. Ameren Illinois and the city's utility billing office ask for the occupancy permit number before they open service. The city offers a seller's and a buyer's "as is" letter, and you should ask your lender whether the permit is a condition of closing.

You can apply online, by mail, through the white drop box in the parking lot, or at Community Development inside City Hall. Paying by card adds a 2.35% convenience fee. Landlords are also pointed to the city's Crime-Free Rental Housing Program.

Stopping or transferring water service

Fill out the city's start or stop service request form, and call Utility Billing at 618-624-4500 extension 1 if you need help. The office is at 255 S Lincoln Avenue and keeps weekday hours, 7 a.m. to 5:15 p.m.

The city bills water and sewer for most O'Fallon addresses and for most of Fairview Heights. A new account is charged a $50 non-refundable new service fee on its first bill. Sewer charges follow an averaging rule: June, July and August sewer use is billed from the average of the October through April water consumption, with 10,000 gallons assumed for a new residence that has no history. A bill that looks too high can mean a leak, and the city will re-read a meter and run a leak check on request.

When are St. Clair County property taxes due?

Property tax in St. Clair County comes due twice a year, in July and September in recent years, and the Treasurer posts a tax sale for unpaid bills later in the fall. The Treasurer's office opens at half past eight and closes at half past four.

Call the Treasurer for the schedule on your next bill, since posted dates carry a tentative label until they are final. Ask your closing agent how the seller's portion of the year's tax is credited at closing, and pay anything past due before the sale so no lien follows the house.

Step by step for an O'Fallon seller

The city handles most of what a sale needs, so it helps to take things in order.

  1. Decide whether to list, sell it yourself or take a cash offer, and compare what each would put in your pocket after repairs and fees.
  2. Look up whether a current occupancy permit is on file. If not, apply online, by mail, in the white drop box or at Community Development.
  3. Book the inspection within 7 days of applying, make sure the water and electricity are on, and fix any violations the inspector lists.
  4. Submit the start or stop service form to Utility Billing so the water account moves on the closing date.
  5. Call the Treasurer about the tax bill and pay anything past due.

A listing gives you time to find the best price, but the occupancy permit and the inspection apply to a listed sale as much as to a cash sale. A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands saves you from a long list of repairs and lets you choose a closing date that works.

Landlords who are selling a rental should also look at the city's Crime-Free Rental Housing Program and tell the buyer where the property stands.

Closing checklist for an O'Fallon seller

A few tasks decide how smoothly an O'Fallon sale closes. Apply for the occupancy permit as soon as you have a contract, because the inspection and any repairs take more than a month. Have the water and electricity on for the inspector. Tell Utility Billing the closing date, and ask the Treasurer about the tax bill. A cash buyer who takes the house as is can still need the permit, so ask the buyer who will arrange the inspection.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need an occupancy permit to sell my O'Fallon house?

Usually yes, because the city requires one when ownership changes and no current permit is on file. A residential permit costs $75 and lasts two years, and your lender can tell you if closing depends on it.

How long does the O'Fallon occupancy inspection take to schedule?

Contact the city within 7 days of applying, and the inspection must occur within 30 days of the application. The permit itself follows within another 30 days after the first inspection.

Can a buyer move in before the occupancy inspection is done?

Yes, provided there are no life safety issues. The inspection still has to happen and any violations still have to be corrected.

Which county collects property tax on an O'Fallon house?

St. Clair County. The Treasurer bills in two installments, in July and September in recent years. Call the Treasurer for the next bill's dates.

Is O'Fallon, Illinois the same place as O'Fallon, Missouri?

No. They are separate cities in the same metro area. Illinois's O'Fallon is in St. Clair County, so make sure any records or tax searches use the Illinois city.

Selling fast in Glendale Heights

The first move for a fast Glendale Heights sale is the village's transfer inspection application, filed at least 21 days before closing, since that step sets the earliest realistic closing date for any buyer. After that, the choice is between listing, selling privately, or accepting an as-is cash purchase.

  • A listing can reach the most buyers, but the house has to pass the village's inspection process like any other.
  • A private sale saves the commission and leaves the contract, disclosures and scheduling to you.
  • An as-is cash sale is common for houses with code problems, tenants or an estate, and the buyer can sign the village's guarantee of compliance for many checklist items.

Glendale Heights is a village in DuPage County and a far west suburb of Chicago. It is almost entirely residential, so most sales here are of single-family houses, townhouses, duplexes and condominiums, and the village's rules are written around those property types.

Whichever route you pick, gather three things first: a plat of survey dated within one year, the deed, and a list of anything you owe the village. Those cover the inspection application and the Finance Department visit, and having them ready is what keeps the 21 day lead time from stretching.

Glendale Heights housing snapshot

Glendale Heights is a compact suburb of 32,655 residents on roughly 5.4 square miles of land, with 11,196 households averaging 2.93 people.

Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $261,700, and owners hold 64.4 percent of the housing. Median gross rent is $1,590 and median household income is $86,545.

Builders began putting up houses here in 1958 on former farmland, and the village incorporated in 1959. Houses from the first building decades are now well past 50 years old, so roofs, furnaces and electrical panels deserve a look before you list.

School districts and transit

Three K to 8 districts serve the village, and all feed into Glenbard Township High School District 87. Marquardt School District 15 covers the eastern part and feeds mainly into Glenbard East. Queen Bee District 16 sends students to Glenbard North and Glenbard West. Glen Ellyn School District 41 covers a portion of the village, and its students attend Abraham Lincoln School, then Hadley Junior High, and later Glenbard West.

Pace routes 711 and 715 connect the village to Wheaton and other destinations. Because the district lines cut across the village, check the district for your street before you describe a school in a listing or offer letter.

Transfer inspection and stamp

Glendale Heights requires a real estate transfer inspection for most sales, and the owner must file for a certificate of compliance at least 21 days before the proposed transfer, along with a plat of survey dated within one year. The inspection is visual only and does not replace a private home inspection.

Transfer inspection application fees
Property typeApplication fee
Single-family residential$100
Multi-family building, up to 6 units$200, plus $10 for each unit over 6
Commercial or industrial, up to 10,000 square feet$300

The sequence for sellers runs like this:

  • Community Development inspects the property and gives you a report of items to correct. You can fix them and request a re-inspection, or the purchaser can sign a Guarantee of Compliance for items authorized on the checklist.
  • Pay any money you owe the village, such as unpaid building or code invoices, lien filing fees, parking tickets and rental fees.
  • Then go to Finance. There you pay the final water bill, hand in the stamp form with the deed copy and the state's PTAX-203 declaration, and pay the village's transfer tax of $3 on each $1,000 of value, rounding up any fraction.

What the inspector looks at

The sample checklist gives a sense of the inspector's eye: ground-fault outlets near water, smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, doors and windows that lock, a covered electrical panel, flues in good order, a sump pump that empties into the yard, and a self-closing fire-rated door from the garage into the house.

A re-inspection can turn up items missed the first time, and the village may require an escrow to secure corrections. Walk the house with that list before you apply, and fix the cheap items first. Call Community Development at 630-260-6030 and Finance at 630-260-6000 with questions.

Rental licensing and a sale

All residential rentals in the village must hold an annual license and be inspected each year, so a rental house or condo has an extra layer of paperwork at sale time. The transfer form asks whether the property was or will be used as a rental, and the checklist warns that a rental inspection is more stringent than the transfer inspection.

License fees depend on property type: $200 for a single-family condominium, $300 for a single-family rental house, townhouse or duplex, and for apartment complexes $100 per building plus $50 per unit. Applications and fees are due by February 1 each year, and licenses expire January 31. A late renewal adds $25 per month, and a re-inspection fee of $75 can apply when an inspection is missed or cancelled late. Owners schedule inspections with their tenants by calling 630-260-6030.

If you own a rental here, clear any unpaid license or inspection fees before you apply for the transfer stamp, because the village will not issue it while rental fees remain owed.

DuPage County property taxes

DuPage County sends bills each spring with installments due June 1 and September 1. After a due date the county adds 1.5 percent a month, and delinquent notices follow a pre-delinquent bill in the fall.

Exemptions include a homestead improvement exemption that shelters up to $25,000 of added assessment for four years, plus senior and disability programs. The assessor for your township, named on the tax bill, handles valuation questions and the residential exemption, and appeals go to the county Board of Review within 30 days after the township roll is published, supported by three or more comparable properties.

Selling or refinancing sometimes leads to a double payment, because a title company or lender and the owner each pay the same bill. The county refunds a duplicate payment only to the person who made it, using a notarized affidavit and proof of payment, so tell your lender and title company which of you is paying. For bills, call the Treasurer at 630-407-5900. For exemptions, call the Supervisor of Assessments at 630-407-5858.

Frequently asked questions

How early should I start the Glendale Heights transfer inspection?

At least 21 days before the proposed closing. The village requires the application and a plat of survey dated within one year, and the application fee for a single-family home is $100.

Who pays the Glendale Heights transfer stamp?

The seller completes the stamp steps at the Finance Department. The tax is $3 for every $1,000 of value or fraction thereof, and the deed, PTAX-203 and final water bill are part of the packet.

What happens if the inspection finds problems?

You receive a report of items to correct, and you may fix them and ask for a re-inspection. A purchaser may instead sign a Guarantee of Compliance for authorized checklist items, and the village may require an escrow.

Does a rented Glendale Heights house need its license before I sell?

A rental house needs its annual license while it is rented, with renewals due February 1. Pay any unpaid rental fees first, since amounts owed to the village must be settled before the stamp.

Where do Glendale Heights owners ask about taxes or exemptions?

Use the DuPage County Treasurer at 630-407-5900 for bills and payments and the Supervisor of Assessments at 630-407-5858 for exemptions and appeals. The township assessor on your bill covers the residential exemption.

Before closing: what Elk Grove Village requires

The village wants a transfer stamp, a settled water account and a few forms before a sale can close, so a fast sale here comes down to lining those items up early. Population is 31,885, and the village sits next to O'Hare International Airport and runs its own transfer tax.

Elk Grove Village lies in both Cook and DuPage counties, and the county of your parcel decides where the deed is recorded. A title company or attorney usually files the paperwork, yet you should know what they will ask you for.

  • Your parcel number and the county on your tax bill.
  • The names on the deed, spelled exactly as recorded, including middle initials and trust numbers.
  • A final water meter reading booked ahead of closing.
  • A mortgage payoff statement and a list of any liens.
  • For homes north of Elk Grove Boulevard, the underground fuel tank disclosure form.

A simple order of steps for the sale

Most delays come from doing things out of order. A workable sequence looks like this.

  1. Confirm which county your parcel sits in and whether your house is north of Elk Grove Boulevard.
  2. Get a payoff statement from your lender and ask the title company to look for liens.
  3. Set the closing date, then book the final water reading for at least two days earlier.
  4. Gather the declaration form, the deed copy, the water and sewer affidavit and the state form, and sign where two signatures are required.
  5. Buy the stamp at the Finance Department or send the forms by email, and keep the receipt.
  6. After closing, make sure a copy of the signed deed reaches the Finance Department within 10 days.

A cash buyer who takes the house as-is skips lender appraisal and repair negotiation, but the village paperwork stays the same. The stamp, the water account and the disclosure apply to every sale.

How the transfer stamp works

Elk Grove Village levies its own tax when title to local real estate changes hands: $3 for every $1,000 of value, counting any fraction, with the seller carrying primary liability. To buy the stamp you submit a village Real Estate Tax Declaration Form with two signatures, a copy of the new deed, a water and sewer affidavit, and either the state PTAX-203 or an EZ Dec form. An unsigned copy of the deed is accepted for purchase, but a copy of the signed deed must reach the Finance Department within 10 days after closing.

Acceptable payment is cash, a cashier's check, a money order, or an attorney's or title company's check made out to Elk Grove Village. Credit cards and personal or company checks are turned away. The finance counter in the Municipal Building, 901 Wellington Avenue, sells stamps on weekdays between 8:30 and 4:30, and finished forms can be emailed to fc@elkgrove.org. Mailed requests take about one week, so leave extra time if your closing is close.

The Finance Department's number is (847) 439-3900.

What to do about the water bill before closing

The final water bill has to be paid when you buy the transfer stamp, and the village asks that a final meter reading be scheduled at least two days before the closing date. All other utility bills and debts owed to the village must also be settled before the stamp is issued. The water and sewer affidavit asks for the top three lines, the seller's forwarding address and the buyer's name.

The stamp, the final reading and the payoff all need to land near the closing date, so put the reading on the calendar as soon as the closing is set. A seller who forgets the reading can delay the stamp, and a delayed stamp can delay the closing. Ask your title company to confirm that the village has the reading scheduled.

Underground fuel tank disclosure

The village requires a Real Estate Disclosure Form for underground fuel heating storage tanks on all properties located north of Elk Grove Boulevard. Sellers give it to the buyers, and it covers the possible presence of those tanks. Questions about underground heating fuel tanks go to the Fire Department at (847) 734-8020.

It is easy to overlook because it applies by location inside the village. Check where your street sits relative to Elk Grove Boulevard, and fill the form out before the contract date rather than at the closing table. A house with a known tank history can still sell, but the buyer should receive the information up front.

Exemptions and refunds on the transfer tax

Certain transfers are exempt. Village Code 3-2-5-F and the back of the declaration form carry the complete list, and anyone claiming an exemption must supply proof of every fact needed to establish it. The exempt stamp carries a $10 handling fee, and all utility bills and village debts must be paid before it is issued.

Some taxpayers can claim a refund on a portion of the tax. Applications for re-investment or senior refunds must reach the village within one year of payment, so keep your receipt and closing documents. The village's Real Estate Transfer Stamp Refund and Exemption pages describe who qualifies. If you are transferring a house into a trust or between family members, ask the Finance Department whether the exempt route fits before you purchase a regular stamp.

  • Exemption claims need proof of each fact behind the exemption.
  • The exempt stamp carries a $10 handling fee.
  • Re-investment and senior refund requests must arrive within one year of payment.

Elk Grove Village was incorporated in 1956 as a planned suburb about 22 miles northwest of Chicago. The housing is mostly early suburban stock, kept separate from a large industrial park on the eastern edge. Buyers here include commuters who value the access to O'Hare and the expressways.

About 90 percent of residents stay at the same address from one year to the next, so turnover is modest.

School boundaries, roads and recording

Interstate 290 splits the school boundaries. East of I-290, students attend Elk Grove High School in Illinois High School District 214 and Community Consolidated School District 59. West of I-290, students go to James B. Conant High School in Township High School District 211 and Mead Junior High in District 54. Name the right district in your listing, since buyers with children search by it.

The village is reached by I-90, I-290, I-355, Route 53 and IL-390, and Pace Route 223 links to the Rosemont station. Its position directly beside O'Hare along the Golden Corridor is a selling point for commuters.

Deeds are recorded by the Cook County Clerk or the DuPage County Recorder. Cook lists state transfer tax at .50 per $500, county tax at .25 per $500 and a $107 deed recording fee under its April 2024 schedule. DuPage's Recorder can be reached at 630-407-5400.

Frequently asked questions

How much is the transfer tax in Elk Grove Village?

The village rate is $3 per $1,000 of value, or fraction thereof, with the primary liability on the seller. State and county transfer taxes are separate charges set by the recording county. Ask your title company to list each one on the settlement statement.

Can I pay for an Elk Grove Village transfer stamp with a credit card?

No. Cash, a cashier's check, a money order, or an attorney's or title company's check to the village will work. Credit cards and personal or company checks are not taken.

How early must I schedule the final water reading?

At least two days before the closing date. Book the reading as soon as your closing date is set, and confirm the timing with the Finance Department.

Do I need an underground fuel tank disclosure?

Yes, if the house is north of Elk Grove Boulevard. Sellers there must give buyers a disclosure form about possible underground fuel heating storage tanks. Fire Department staff answer questions about the tanks.

Which county records my Elk Grove Village deed?

Either Cook County or DuPage County, depending on where your parcel sits. Look at the tax bill for the county, and the title company files the deed there.

The median value of owner-occupied homes in Pekin is $120,700, so repair costs can take a large share of the price. A new roof or furnace is a bigger decision when the house is worth that little, and for that reason many sellers weigh a cash purchase against listing and fixing the house first.

Pekin is the county seat of Tazewell County, on the Illinois River in central Illinois. Population was 31,731 in 2020 and is estimated at 31,277 now. A small part of the city lies in Peoria County, so some Pekin addresses are recorded and taxed in a different county than most of the city.

Flood zones and the river

The city takes part in the National Flood Insurance Program, and properties below the 1 percent annual chance flood level may be required by law to carry flood insurance. An owner who thinks the flood designation is wrong can ask FEMA for a Letter of Map Amendment, and lenders may still require insurance. Properties along the Illinois River are often subject to floodway rules.

For a sale, find out your flood zone early, since it affects a buyer's mortgage and insurance. New construction in a flood hazard area must set the lowest floor two feet above base flood elevation.

Permits and yard rules before a sale

Pekin's Inspections Department requires permits for electrical, plumbing, sewer, heating, ventilation and air conditioning work, and also for fences, sheds, new homes, additions, decks, signs and pools. A roofing permit applies to a complete tear-off or a second layer of shingles. Siding, windows, doors and interior remodeling need none unless the work changes structural walls, plumbing or electrical.

Other rules a buyer's agent may bring up:

  • A homeowner may do their own work but must still get a permit. The city defines a homeowner as the person who owns and lives at the residence.
  • Pools deeper than 24 inches need a permit and may sit only in the rear yard.
  • Chain link fences are not allowed in any front yard, and corner lots must keep sight lines clear.
  • Vehicles may not be parked in yards or the right of way, and must stand on a hard surface such as concrete or asphalt.

The Inspections Department takes questions at 309.478.5364. If you built a deck or finished a basement without a permit, ask whether it can be inspected before you list.

Which county records a Pekin deed?

Most Pekin parcels are in Tazewell County, where the County Clerk and Recorder keeps real estate records. Everything in the Recorder's files is public record, anyone may look through it free of charge, and some forms are supplied at no cost. Ask the office for current recording fees and transfer stamp amounts before closing, since they change.

Parcels in the Peoria County portion go through Peoria County instead. Its land records office takes part in the state's MyDec system, which lets filers submit the PTAX-203 transfer declaration electronically before a deed is recorded. Check your tax bill or parcel number to see which county applies, and tell your closing attorney if the house straddles the line.

Old mines and your lot

Coal mining once left its mark under parts of Pekin, though it had ended by 1951. One mine, run by the Pekin Coal Mining Company until 1952, lay under what later became Broadmoor Junior High, Willow Elementary and Schramm School, and another crossed Broadway in the eastern part of town.

If a buyer asks whether your lot sits over old workings, the title company or the county recorder's records are the place to start. Do not guess at the answer in a listing.

Schools and commuting

Public schools depend on where the house sits. Most of the city is in Pekin Public School District 108. Parts of the Tazewell County side belong instead to North Pekin-Marquette Heights School District 102 or Rankin Community School District 98, and all of Pekin in Tazewell County feeds Pekin Community High School District 303. The Peoria County portion is in Hollis Consolidated School District 328 and Limestone Community High School District 310.

Ask the district for the boundary of your address before a buyer does. CityLink buses on Routes 17, 18 and 23 connect the city to downtown Peoria, which helps buyers who commute.

What a cash sale skips

A listed sale usually brings showings, a buyer's mortgage and appraisal, and a list of repairs after the inspection. A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands skips those steps, which suits an older house in a flood zone, a property with permit questions, or one that is vacant or inherited. Compare what you would keep from each route after repairs and fees, not just the price on the offer.

A sensible order of work: first find out which county and school district your parcel is in, then confirm the flood zone, then gather permit records for any roof, deck, fence or basement work. With those three answers in hand, you can price the house honestly and tell a buyer or a cash investor what they are getting. Sellers who skip these checks often lose time later, because a lender, an insurer or a buyer's inspector raises the question first, usually just before the closing date. Ask the title company early whether any liens or unpaid taxes are on file for the parcel.

If the permit record is incomplete, ask the Inspections Department at 309.478.5364 whether the work can be inspected now. An older house with a clean record is easier to sell to any kind of buyer, and one with open questions is easier to sell as is.

Frequently asked questions

Which county is Pekin in?

Pekin is the county seat of Tazewell County. A small part of the city extends into Peoria County, so parcels there are recorded and taxed through Peoria County. Check your parcel number to see which applies.

Do I need a permit to replace a roof in Pekin?

Yes, for a complete tear-off and replacement, or for adding a second layer of shingles. Siding, window and door replacement do not need a permit unless structural, plumbing or electrical changes are involved.

Does Pekin have flood rules that affect a sale?

Yes. The city takes part in the National Flood Insurance Program, and properties below the 1 percent annual chance flood level may be required by law to carry flood insurance. New construction in a flood hazard area must set the lowest floor two feet above base flood elevation.

Can I do my own repairs on my Pekin house?

Yes, if you own and live in it, but you still need the permit. Nobody may work on someone else's property unless they hold a license or are registered with the Inspections Department.

Where do I get recording information for a Pekin sale?

Ask the Tazewell County Clerk and Recorder, whose office keeps real estate records open to the public at no charge. For the Peoria County portion of the city, use the Peoria County land records office, which accepts the MyDec transfer declaration.

Algonquin and its two counties

Algonquin is a Fox River suburb about 40 miles northwest of the Chicago Loop, and a sale there can involve two counties because the village straddles the McHenry and Kane line. Roughly 78 percent of the village area is in McHenry County and the rest is in Kane County, so the county printed on your tax bill decides who records the deed and who collects the tax.

The population was 29,700 in 2020 and is estimated at 30,824 for July 1, 2025. Most of the housing is relatively young, since the count climbed from 5,684 in 1980 to 11,663 in 1990 and 23,276 in 2000. Owners occupy 88.2% of homes and value them at a typical $351,000. Gross rent runs a typical $1,723.

Neighborhoods and school boundaries

Location inside the village matters because Algonquin has distinct districts with different traffic and housing. Old Town sits along Main Street (Illinois Route 31) near the original village hall at 2 South Main Street, and exterior changes to any building in its historic district need a Certificate of Appropriateness from the village.

The Randall Road corridor on the western side is the retail spine. The manufacturing belt runs along Algonquin Road between Pyott Road and Route 31, west of Old Town. A buyer comparing a house near the industrial belt with one near the river will weigh noise and truck traffic differently, so an honest description saves time later.

Two school districts split the village, and the boundary often decides which houses draw the most interest from families. Community Unit School District 300 covers the area generally along and east of Randall Road. Consolidated School District 158, headquartered in Algonquin, serves the far western side. Confirm the assignment for your street before you put a school name in a listing.

Do I need a village permit before repairing or selling?

Algonquin requires a building permit before anyone erects, enlarges, alters, repairs, moves, improves, removes, converts or demolishes a building or structure. Small cosmetic jobs are exceptions. The Community Development Department says permit review can take up to five weeks, so repairs you want done before listing should start early.

Anyone moving into a newly built home needs a certificate of occupancy before move-in. The village uses the 2018 International Residential Code and the 2018 International Property Maintenance Code, among others. Questions go to Community Development at (847) 658-2700, option 3, or permits@algonquin.org. If a prior owner finished a basement or deck, ask that office whether the permit was closed before you list.

Roads, fire districts and transit

Out-of-town buyers check the road network first. Randall Road is the multi-lane north and south arterial and runs six lanes between Harnish Drive and Corporate Parkway. Route 31 is the two-lane Main Street through downtown, and its intersection with Algonquin Road backs up at peak times. Illinois Route 25 runs along the eastern edge, and Pace Route 550 follows Randall Road between Crystal Lake and Elgin.

Fire and rescue come from one of three districts depending on the address: the Algonquin-Lake in the Hills Fire Protection District, the Huntley Fire Protection District or the Carpentersville Countryside Fire Protection District. Your tax bill names the districts that serve the parcel.

Property tax bills in McHenry County

McHenry County mails one bill and collects two installments. For the 2026 collection year, bills went out in early May and the installments were due June 9 and September 9. The payment office at 2100 N. Seminary Ave. in Woodstock takes payment at the window or drive-thru lanes from 7:30 to 5 on weekdays.

  • eCheck payments online carry no fee. Credit cards, debit cards and digital wallets add a 2.4% convenience fee.
  • Two 24-hour drop boxes, one walk-up and one drive-up, take checks and money orders payable to the McHenry County Collector. No cash.
  • Write the parcel number (PIN) on any check, and ask the Post Office for a postmark when mailing close to a due date.
  • The VIP Taxpayer program sends email and text reminders and lets owners switch to e-billing.

Parcels in the Kane County part of the village are billed by Kane County, so check the county name on the bill before you pay. At closing, ask the title officer to settle the current year's tax and any open installment between buyer and seller.

Recording the deed

The County Recorder rejects documents that miss formatting or content rules, and a rejection can push back the date a buyer gets title. The Recorder wants a white 20-pound page with a half-inch clean margin on every side and a clear 3 by 5 inch box at the top right.

  • A deed needs the grantor's signature, the grantee's address and the full McHenry County legal description.
  • A Plat Act affidavit goes with the deed when the legal description is metes and bounds.
  • Either a completed exemption paragraph or the Illinois transfer declaration (PTAX-203 or MyDec) must accompany every deed. A MyDec filing must state "Closing Completed."
  • Every document needs "Prepared By" and "Mail To" lines with names and addresses.

Section 31-10 of the Property Tax Code sets the state transfer tax at 50 cents on each $500 block of value in the declaration. Ask the McHenry or Kane County Recorder, whichever holds your parcel, about any county stamp and the Rental Housing Support Program surcharge.

Choosing a sale route

Owners here usually weigh three paths: an agent listing, a private sale and a sale to a buyer who takes the house as it stands. A listing fits a house ready for move-in. Selling privately skips the agent but leaves the permit, deed and declaration work to the owner and the closing attorney. A sale as-is fits a vacant, inherited or tenant-occupied property that needs work.

Whichever route you pick, an open permit or a missing certificate of occupancy will still come up at closing. A call to Community Development early in the process keeps the schedule intact. Then confirm your county from the parcel number, get the current-year tax settled with the title officer, and have the deed prepared to the Recorder's format rules before the signing date.

Frequently asked questions

Which county handles my Algonquin deed and tax bill?

It depends on the parcel. About 78 percent of the village is in McHenry County and the rest is in Kane County. The county name on your tax bill tells you whom to ask.

Does Algonquin require a permit for a small roof repair?

Not for a repair of 200 square feet or less. Larger roof work, gutters and downspouts, and a garage service door do need permits.

When were McHenry County property tax installments due in 2026?

June 9 and September 9, 2026. Check the Treasurer's Office for the dates on the next bill, and pay online by eCheck to avoid the 2.4% fee charged on cards.

Does Algonquin Old Town have extra rules for exterior work?

Yes. A Certificate of Appropriateness is required for all exterior changes, additions and demolitions to buildings inside the historic district.

What must a MyDec filing say for McHenry County recording?

It must state "Closing Completed." The Recorder also needs the grantee's address, the legal description and a Plat Act affidavit if the description is metes and bounds.

Highland Park housing at a glance

Highland Park sits in Lake County on the North Shore, about 25 miles north of downtown Chicago. The city is split between Moraine Township and West Deerfield Township, and mail runs through ZIP codes 60035, 60036 and 60037. Population is 30,767 in the mid-2025 estimate.

Lake Michigan shapes the layout. A bluff about 100 feet high runs along 6 miles of shoreline, and wooded ravines cut up to a mile inland. A house beside a ravine or at the bluff edge sells differently from one on a flat street near a Metra stop, and buyers will ask about the lot as closely as the building.

The five-year survey figures for 2020 to 2024 show 11,787 households, 83.8 percent of them owner-occupied, with a median home value of $607,300 and a median gross rent of $1,925. About 87.5 percent of residents stayed at the same address through the previous year, which describes a city of long-time owners.

Older homes and what buyers ask for

The city was platted in 1856 after the Chicago and Milwaukee Railroad built a depot, and it became a city on March 11, 1869. That early start left a lot of older houses. The Willits House is on the federal historic register, and the register also lists work by Frank Lloyd Wright, John S. Van Bergen, Howard Van Doren Shaw, Robert E. Seyfarth and David Adler.

If you own an architect-designed house, you probably have the original plans, permits and drawings somewhere. Gather them before you talk to any buyer. Documented history is one of the few things that can set a house apart from its neighbors.

  • Most residents stay put, so your listing may be the first on the street in years. Pull recent sale records before you pick a price.
  • Older construction makes for a long inspection report, and a buyer may ask to see plans and permits.
  • Four Metra stations inside city limits make distance to the platform a selling point for downtown workers.

Commuting, schools and lakefront

North Shore School District 112 runs the elementary and middle schools. Township High School District 113 runs Highland Park High School and also Deerfield High School in nearby Deerfield.

US 41 is the main highway and connects Chicago to Milwaukee. The four Metra stations are Braeside, Ravinia Park, Ravinia and Highland Park, all on the Union Pacific North Line. Pace buses add local routes, O'Hare is about 20 miles southwest, and the Skokie Valley Trail runs through town. Three public beaches, Rosewood, Moraine and Park Avenue, line the shore. Buyers of every type, cash buyers included, weigh the stations, schools and beaches when they set a price.

What the city requires before closing

Chapter 97, Article X of the city code taxes real property transfers. The declaration form prints the rate as $5.00 per $1,000 or fraction thereof of full actual consideration, and it puts payment on the transferor when the sale contract says nothing different.

  • The declaration needs a signature from a transferor and a transferee.
  • A final water bill must be prepared and paid when the tax stamp is bought, and a final meter reading can be scheduled up to five business days before closing.
  • A copy of the deed headed for the Recorder of Deeds goes to the city, while an exempt transfer requires the original.
  • Consideration counts the mortgage amount and any liabilities the buyer assumes.
  • Section 97.1004 lists exempt deeds, such as tax deeds, partition deeds, deeds with consideration under $100, and foreclosure or in-lieu deeds to a mortgage holder.

Personal checks and credit cards are refused. Finance, at 1707 St. Johns Avenue, takes calls at 847.432.0800 and email at Finance@cityhpil.com. Ask for the final water reading early so closing does not wait on a meter.

Recording the deed with Lake County

The Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office handles deeds at 18 N County Street, 6th Floor, Waukegan, phone 847-377-2575. The fee is $70 for a standard document and $82 for a non-standard one, and state and county transfer taxes are the only added charges at recording.

The state levies its own tax under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, charged on the value stated in the declaration, and a mortgage the buyer takes over can be excluded when the deed says so. Your closing agent will give you the county rate and a final total.

A step-by-step order for the sale

Most Highland Park sales follow the same order, whichever route you pick. Knowing it ahead of time keeps a closing date from slipping over paperwork.

  1. Settle on a route and sign a contract that says who pays the transfer charges.
  2. Fill out the city declaration. Both a transferor and a transferee must sign it.
  3. Ask the city to schedule the final meter reading, which can happen up to five business days before closing.
  4. Pay the final water bill and buy the tax stamp at Finance. Bring a payment other than a personal check or a credit card.
  5. Have the closing agent prepare the deed and compute the state and county transfer taxes from the value stated in the declaration.
  6. File the deed with the Lake County Clerk's Recording Division in Waukegan and send the city its copy.

If your house is on a ravine lot or a bluff, or was designed by a known architect, hand the buyer the plans and permits early. A buyer with documents in hand tends to ask fewer questions at the end, and that helps a short closing hold together. Keep copies of everything you sign for your own files.

Which selling route fits a Highland Park owner in a hurry?

Three routes exist, and each trades price, certainty and effort differently.

  • Work with a listing agent. Exposure is widest, and a bluff, ravine or architect-designed property can justify a longer wait.
  • Sell on your own. You control the contract and carry the showings, disclosures and negotiation.
  • Accept a cash offer. The closing date can follow your calendar and the house stays as it is, which helps with an estate home, a tenant-occupied unit or a house that needs work.

The city stamp, the final water bill and the deed filing apply on every route. When a cash buyer makes an offer, get in writing who pays each transfer charge named above. The sale contract is where that split is settled, so read it before you sign.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and the loan approval wait, and you can usually choose a closing date that suits a move or an estate timeline.

The transferor does, unless the sale contract says otherwise.

Yes. It must be prepared and paid when the stamp is bought, and a final meter reading can be booked up to five business days ahead of closing.

Which office files the deed after a Highland Park closing?

The Lake County Clerk's Recording Division in Waukegan. The fee for a standard document is $70.

Which school districts serve Highland Park?

North Shore School District 112 runs the elementary and middle schools, and Township High School District 113 runs Highland Park High School and Deerfield High School.

About Gurnee

Gurnee sits on the Des Plaines River in Lake County, roughly 40 miles north of Chicago and 50 miles south of Milwaukee, next to Waukegan. Interstate 94 splits the village into an older east side and a newer west side. Pace buses link Gurnee with Waukegan and Grayslake, and a CPKC rail line between Chicago and Minneapolis runs through town.

Six Flags Great America, Gurnee Mills and the Great Wolf Lodge resort bring millions of visits a year. Buyers will want to know how close a house sits to the I-94 corridor and the attraction areas, so be ready to describe its location.

Timeline for a Gurnee sale

Gurnee closings move fastest when the paperwork starts before the contract is signed. A workable order looks like this.

  2. Confirm which elementary district your address falls in, and write it into the listing.

  4. Choose your route: listing, owner-handled sale or as-is cash offer. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and usually the repair requests that follow it.
  5. Ask your title company to line up the notary, the legal description, the PTAX-203 and the tax bill address for the deed.
  6. Use the Village's Start, Stop or Make Changes page to end your water service near the closing date.

None of these steps needs a trip to Village Hall, and most can be done online or by phone. An owner who tackles them in order can usually give a buyer a firm closing date.

If the house has had work done without a permit, say so early. A buyer who takes the house as-is can accept the open items, but the contract should state clearly who is responsible, and the Building Division can tell you what it would require to close the permit.

The May 2004 storm brought the worst flooding in a century, closed schools and damaged dozens of homes and businesses. The Village names the low ground along the Des Plaines River and its tributaries as the most dangerous flood hazard area.

  • Basements built more recently must have a sump pump ejection system, and the Village urges backups.
  • The Engineering Division, at 847-599-7550, keeps elevation certificates supplied by owners and historical flood records.
  • The Village's participation in the Community Rating System earns policyholders a 5 to 20 percent insurance discount.

A voluntary floodplain buyout program is also listed among the Village's flooding resources, along with a mailing list for flood updates.
