Deeds and transfer tax in Lake County

Deeds go to the Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office in Waukegan. The county's deed packet requires a notarized grantor signature, the grantee's address, a legal description, the preparer's name and a completed PTAX-203 form or an exemption statement. It also lists six municipalities that require a local transfer stamp before recording. Vernon Hills is not among them, but ask the village clerk if your deed has unusual features.

Under 35 ILCS 200/31-15, the state tax is collected through revenue stamps or an electronic indicator. Any sale also has to be reported to the Department of Revenue electronically. Your title company normally handles both, so ask for the figures before closing day.

Before you list or accept a cash offer

Gather your latest tax bill, any permit paperwork for decks, fences or basement finishes, and a payoff figure from your lender. Check with Community Development at (847) 367-3700 about any permit left open, since a buyer's title review can turn it up.

A cash purchase skips the buyer's loan approval and the appraisal that comes with it. The work that remains is the title search, payoff letters, the deed and the PTAX-203. If those are in order, closing can come quickly, and you choose the date together with the buyer. Compare any offer against what a listing would net after repairs, showings and the wait.

At closing you sign the deed, the lender is paid off from your proceeds, and the county records the transfer. Keep copies of everything you sign, and ask the title company to confirm in writing that the old mortgage is released.

Frequently asked questions

Does the village of Vernon Hills inspect a house before a sale?

The village's permit and Community Development pages cover permits, code enforcement and certificates of occupancy for newly occupied units, and none describes a seller inspection tied to a resale. Ask Community Development at (847) 367-3700 if you have open permits or an unusual use.

How long does a Vernon Hills permit review last?

Residential permit applications typically take 15 business days to process. Minor permits such as a water heater, HVAC, roof, siding or sewer repair are released immediately, subject to staff availability.

Does a Vernon Hills sale carry a village transfer tax?

The Lake County deed packet lists six municipalities that require a stamp, and Vernon Hills is not one of them. State and county transfer taxes are collected at recording, so ask your title company for the figures on your deed.

What dates apply to Vernon Hills property tax installments?

Lake County splits the bill in two, due in early June and early September. Bills are mailed at the start of May each year.

Can a cash buyer close fast on a Vernon Hills house?

Yes, when the title is clear and the deed and PTAX-203 are ready for Lake County recording. A cash closing then depends on the title search, payoff letters and the buyer's funds.

Selling a Granite City house quickly

The quickest routes are an as-is cash purchase or a competitively priced listing, and both run through the same Madison County recording steps. What changes is how many conditions stand between you and closing day.

  • As-is cash sale: no mortgage underwriting, and the buyer normally takes the house with its repairs.
  • Agent listing: wider exposure, but a buyer's lender may require an appraisal and repair requests.
  • For sale by owner: you keep control of price and showings and pay for a contract review yourself.

Granite City has a lot of older, modestly priced housing, so condition often drives the choice. If a roof, furnace or foundation is the sticking point, compare what repairs would cost against a sale to someone who will handle them.

Granite City housing market

Granite City is one of the lower-priced housing markets in the St. Louis area. Population is 26,807, down from 27,563 in 2020, and the city has 11,562 households.

If your house is one of the empty ones, keep the utilities connected, since the city requires them to be on for an occupancy inspection.

Neighborhoods and housing stock

Granite City was planned as a company town in 1896 by the Niedringhaus brothers, who made graniteware kitchen utensils and later steel. A street grid with lettered avenues and numbered streets was laid out, with Niedringhaus Avenue as the only exception.

The result is a city of neighborhood pockets: Downtown, East Granite, West Granite, North Granite, the Nameoki Strip, the Bellemore area and the Wilson Park area. Wilson Park is known for turn-of-the-20th-century homes, while East Granite is mostly newer residential subdivisions. Name the neighborhood in your listing, since buyers shop by area.

Roads, flood protection and jobs

Granite City sits in the American Bottom beside the Chain of Rocks Canal on the Mississippi, with Horseshoe Lake to the southeast. Interstate 270 crosses the northern edge, and Interstates 255, 70, 55 and 64 pass just south and east. Route 3 runs along the western side and reaches downtown St. Louis over the McKinley Bridge.

The city stayed dry in the Great Flood of 1993 because levees protect it along the river and the canal. Even so, a buyer in this area will usually ask about flood zone status and insurance, so have your elevation or insurance information ready if you have it.

Industry remains central, with steel and food manufacturers among the long-running employers, which keeps steady local demand for housing.

Schools and parks buyers ask about

Granite City Community Unit School District 9 serves the city. It runs five elementary schools (Frohardt, Mitchell, Wilson, Prather and Maryville), Grigsby Intermediate, Coolidge Junior High and Granite City High School. Families also have two Catholic kindergarten through eighth grade schools, Holy Family and St. Elizabeth, and Rivers of Life Christian School.

The Granite City Park District owns 13 parks, and its most notable, Wilson Park, includes a 1.4 mile paved trail, a pool and an ice rink. Horseshoe Lake State Park, retail along the Nameoki Strip and the Madison County Transit bikeways are also worth a line in the listing.

Order of steps for a Granite City sale

A simple sequence keeps the city and county pieces from colliding. Call the Building and Zoning Department first and ask whether an Occupancy Permit applies to your sale. If it does, file the application, pay the fee and book an inspection slot with the utilities still on. While that is moving, ask your title company to prepare the deed with the grantee's tax billing address, the parcel number and the PTAX form. A cash buyer can skip the lender's appraisal, but the permit and the recording steps stay the same, so start them as soon as you have a signed contract.

Occupancy permit when a house changes hands

The owner of a home must apply for an Occupancy Permit when occupancy or ownership changes. Call the Building and Zoning Department at (618) 452-6218 to confirm how the rule applies to your sale and your buyer before you set a closing date.

  • The permit must be obtained within 30 days of application.
  • The owner pays the fees and arranges access for the inspection.
  • Utilities must be on for the inspection.
  • Inspection slots run from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Monday through Friday, and you can book once the application is in and the fee is paid.

The same office enforces a property maintenance code, and grass on private property must be kept below eight inches.

Permits and upkeep rules

The Building and Zoning Department asks for 24 hours of advance notice for inspections and takes scheduling calls at (618) 452-6218. Get permits before any home improvement project, which matters if you are tempted to finish a repair before listing.

  • Inspections are required at set stages, such as before concrete is poured, before insulation and drywall, and after the structure is finished and before it is used.
  • New structures cannot be used or occupied until final inspections pass and a certificate of use and occupancy is issued.
  • Grass on private property must stay below eight inches, and below five inches in the right-of-way between the curb and sidewalk.
  • Trash and recycling go to the curb the evening before pickup, no earlier than 6:00 p.m.

Ask the department about permits for any addition, deck or finished basement before you accept an offer.

How the deed is recorded in Madison County

Granite City is in Madison County, so the deed goes to the Madison County Recorder. Every deed needs a grantee name and address for tax billing and a permanent parcel number, along with a return-to name and address and the name and address of the person who prepared it.

  • An Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration (PTAX) or a statement of exemption.
  • A Plat Act affidavit, which must accompany all deeds.
  • Transfer tax at the rates the office prints: $.50 per $500 or part thereof to the state and $.25 per $500 or part thereof to the county.

If you pay by check, the Recorder asks for the recording fee and the transfer tax on separate checks. Your title company usually handles all of this at the closing table.

Does Granite City require an inspection before I can sell?

An owner must apply for an Occupancy Permit when occupancy or ownership changes, so call (618) 452-6218 to see how it applies to your sale. When one is required, the owner pays and the utilities must be on for the inspection.

Where do I record a deed for a Granite City house?

At the Madison County Recorder, since Granite City is in Madison County. Bring the deed, a parcel number, the PTAX form or exemption statement and a Plat Act affidavit.

What transfer tax rates apply in Madison County?

The Recorder prints $.50 per $500 or part thereof of taxable consideration for the State of Illinois and $.25 per $500 or part thereof for the county. Your closing agent calculates the amount from the declaration.

Is Granite City in a flood area?

The city is on the Mississippi River plain and is protected by levees along the river and the Chain of Rocks Canal. It did not flood in 1993, but check the flood zone and insurance details for your own address.

Can I sell a Granite City house with tenants or code problems?

Yes. An as-is buyer can take a house with tenants in place or an open maintenance notice. Ask the Building and Zoning Department about any violation before closing so it does not surprise anyone.

Oak Forest sellers deal with Cook County recording and a handful of city programs for rentals, vacant buildings and code upkeep. The city's own rules are light for an owner-occupied house, but a former rental or empty property brings extra registration questions.

The city sits about 24 miles south-southwest of downtown Chicago in Bremen Township and has 26,792 residents (July 2025 estimate). Median owner-occupied value is $255,100, 82.4% of homes are owner-occupied, and 92.0% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Rental and vacancy rules

Oak Forest regulates rentals more closely than many suburbs, so a house that was ever leased may carry a registration trail.

  • All rental properties must be registered under the Crime Free Multi-Housing ordinance, with a license for each calendar year. The fee is $100 for one to five units, $150 for six to ten, and rises to $500 for 41 or more.
  • Landlords complete a seminar, a physical security inspection, background checks for new tenants age 18 and over, and a city lease addendum. Missing records can bring a fine of up to $750.
  • Apartment and condominium buildings are registered and inspected every year, with inspections from May 1 through September 30.
  • Vacant buildings must be registered, with a $700 fee and required inspections.
  • A short-term vacation rental license costs $50 a year, requires the owner to live in the home as a primary residence for nine of twelve months, and requires $1,000,000 per occurrence in liability insurance.

Foreclosure notices and confirmation orders go to the city's Property Maintenance Coordinator at 15440 S. Central Avenue, and code questions go to Property Maintenance at 708-444-4846. Ask the Crime Free Housing office at 708-687-4050 extension 1295 whether a rental license is current.

Property maintenance code

The city enforces the 2018 International Property Maintenance Code with local amendments. Violation notices cite the problem, set a correction date and schedule a re-inspection, and unresolved items can bring fines.

  • Typical violations include rubbish, tall grass, inoperable or unlicensed vehicles, roof and fence repair, and grading and drainage.
  • House numbers must be at least four inches high and plainly visible from the street.
  • Recreational vehicles of 26 feet or less may be stored anywhere on a lot, those between 26 and 40 feet only in a side or rear yard, and vehicles of 40 feet or more are not permitted.

Clear any open notice before listing. It is easier to settle before a buyer's inspector sees it.

Recording and closing in Cook County

An Oak Forest deed is recorded with the Cook County Clerk's recordings office at 118 N. Clark St., phone 312.603.5050. A rubber stamp is the proof of payment, and municipal amounts vary by location.

Ask the Cook County Treasurer for the balance and installment status on the parcel, and ask the title company how the closing statement will prorate that year's bill.

Public elementary districts include Forest Ridge District 142, Arbor Park District 145 and Tinley Park District 146. Oak Forest High School is part of Bremen District 228, and parts of the city feed Tinley Park, Victor J. Andrew or Carl Sandburg high schools, so confirm by address.

US Route 6 (159th Street) and Illinois Route 50 (Cicero Avenue) are the main crossing roads, and Interstate 57 clips the southeast corner. The Oak Forest Metra station at 159th and Cicero is on the Rock Island District line to LaSalle Street, and Pace routes 354, 364 and 383 serve the city. The mean commute is 31.8 minutes, so train access and quick reach to I-57 are worth stating in a listing.

Which route fits your house?

A traditional listing suits an updated house with no open notices. A direct sale to a cash buyer suits a house that needs work, a rental with a messy license history, or an inherited home where relatives live out of state. Both routes use the same Cook County recording steps.

Before you choose, check the three things buyers' attorneys ask about first: open code notices, any rental or vacancy registration, and the water account. A clean answer on each shortens the closing, and a problem on any of them is easier to solve before you sign a contract.

Paperwork to gather before you list

Collect the deed or trust documents, your latest Cook County tax bill, and any payoff statement. If the house was ever rented, pull the rental license record and ask the Crime Free Housing office whether your registration is current. If the building was ever empty, ask Property Maintenance whether a vacant building registration was filed and whether the $700 fee was paid.

Walk the exterior as an inspector would: house numbers, tall grass, vehicles, fences, roof and drainage. Fix or document anything that could draw a notice. Then call City Hall at 708-687-4050 to confirm there is no municipal transfer stamp for your address, and call the water office so the final bill is settled before closing.

What is the fee for vacant property registration?

The city charges a $700 registration fee for a vacant building and requires inspections. The owner or anyone with a legal or equitable interest must register it.

Oak Forest is in Bremen Township, on the south and west suburban reassessment cycle. Look up your PIN on the Cook County Assessor's site to confirm.

Selling a house in Yorkville

Yorkville is the Kendall County seat, on the Fox River about 4 miles southwest of Aurora, 13 miles southwest of Naperville and 39 miles west of Chicago. The city spreads across Bristol, Kendall and Fox townships, so one house may stand on a downtown lot near the river and the next in a large newer subdivision. Buyers weigh those two areas separately, and you should say which kind of house you are selling.

The oldest homes sit within walking distance of Bridge Street, the 1864 courthouse building and Union Hall. Until 1957 the place was two towns with separate governments, Bristol north of the river and Yorkville south of it. They merged that year as the United City of Yorkville.

Plenty of owners here have spent ten years or more in the same subdivision and want out without a long wait on the market. Others inherit an older river-town house that needs work. Both can sell by listing, by owner or for cash.

Housing and income in Yorkville

Yorkville leans toward owner-occupied family housing. Population is 26,730, up from 21,533 at the 2020 count, and about 26.8% of residents are under 18. Incomes run higher than in nearby towns, and the average one-way commute is 34.0 minutes, so a seller who knows the real drive time to Aurora, Naperville or the train can use it in the listing.

School districts

Yorkville Community Unit School District 115 covers the bulk of the city, and Oswego Community Unit School District 308 reaches a small part. Buyers ask about schools early, so confirm which district covers your street and which building your house feeds.

  • District 115 elementary and intermediate schools include Autumn Creek, Bristol Bay, Bristol Grade School, Circle Center, Grande Reserve, Yorkville Grade School and Yorkville Intermediate.
  • Yorkville Middle School and the Yorkville Freshman Academy lead to Yorkville High School.
  • A small part of the city sends students to Oswego District 308 instead.

If your house is near one of those buildings, name it in the listing, because buyers searching by school zone look for it.

Building permits and your sale

City staff say almost any improvement touching plumbing, structure, wiring or mechanical systems calls for a permit. Specific permits cover basements, concrete and paver patios, decks, fences, garages, pools, roofs and sheds. If you finished the basement or built a deck, locate the permit and the final sign-off before a buyer's inspector asks.

  • Apply at City Hall, 651 Prairie Pointe Drive, second floor (Community Development), or email bzpermits@yorkville.il.us. The permit line is 630-553-8545.
  • Most applications need a recent plat of survey and the property's PIN, as state law requires.
  • Review generally takes 7 to 14 days, and longer if changes are needed.
  • Permits lapse after six months without a start or without activity, and the longest life is two years.
  • Ask for inspections a working day or more in advance.

The city lists the 2018 International Codes and the 2017 National Electric Code as its adopted codes. If any permit paperwork is missing, call the department before you list, since an open permit can slow a financed buyer and a closing.

How deed recording works in Kendall County

Deeds for a Yorkville house are recorded by the Kendall County Recorder at 502 S Main St in Yorkville, phone 630-553-4112. Staff are in Monday through Friday. The Recorder takes plats until 3:00 p.m. and other documents until 4:00 p.m., and the research room closes at 4:00 p.m. as well.

Kendall County uses MyDec for online real property transfer tax declarations, a system that has handled PTAX-203 forms through the Illinois Department of Revenue since December 2, 2019. Under the state's transfer tax law, a declaration signed for the seller and the buyer must go with each deed (35 ILCS 200/31-25). The recorder's page also links a PTAX-203 exemptions sheet and forms for a quit claim deed and a warranty deed.

Whoever handles your closing can tell you whether a local transfer charge applies, and the recorder posts the current fee schedule. A free alert service run by the county notifies owners when a filing appears under their name, which is a handy way to catch a surprise lien or a bad filing before you list.

Ways to sell quickly

Speed comes from cutting steps. A buyer paying cash skips the lender's appraisal, so the closing date can follow your move rather than a loan schedule.

  • Agent listing: fits a house with updated systems, with a timeline set by showings and the buyer's loan.
  • Owner-handled sale: you set the price and run the showings, contract and disclosure forms.
  • Cash purchase: suits an estate house, an empty property or one with postponed repairs, because the buyer accepts the condition.

Before talking to anyone, pull together the plat of survey, permit records, your latest tax bill and a payoff statement from your lender.

A cash sale also skips repair requests that follow an inspection, staging and weeks of open houses. You still sign a contract, a title company still checks for liens, and the deed still goes to the Kendall County Recorder with its transfer declaration. What changes is how long the middle part takes and how many things can fall through before the closing date.

If the house is in an older part of town, expect questions about the roof, the furnace, the electrical panel and the foundation. In a newer subdivision, buyers ask about the age of the roof and the homeowners association. Have the answers written down before you start, so you can compare offers on the same facts.

On closing day, the title company pays off your lender, deducts any tax or lien owed, and sends the deed to the recorder. Bring a photo ID and the keys, and make sure your plat of survey and permit records are in the file the title company holds. Ask for the final settlement statement a day ahead so nothing surprises you at the table.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Kendall County Recorder for a Yorkville sale?

The recorder's office is at 502 S Main St in Yorkville, phone 630-553-4112. Documents must arrive by 4:00 p.m. on a weekday to be recorded that day, and plats by 3:00 p.m.

Which school district is Yorkville in?

Yorkville Community Unit School District 115 covers the bulk of the city, and Oswego District 308 reaches a small part. Check your address with the district before you list.

Does a roof replacement in Yorkville need a permit?

Yes. Yorkville lists roofs among the projects that need a specific building permit, along with decks, fences, garages, pools and sheds. Applications go to the Community Development Department at City Hall or to bzpermits@yorkville.il.us.

How long does a Yorkville building permit take?

Review generally takes 7 to 14 days, longer if changes are required. A permit expires if work has not started within six months, and no permit can run longer than two years.

When did Yorkville become one city?

In 1957. Bristol, on the north side of the Fox River, merged with Yorkville on the south side to form the United City of Yorkville, and residents of both agreed to a single school district.

The Windmill City and its oldest blocks

Settlers arrived in 1833, which makes Batavia the oldest city in Kane County, and incorporation followed on July 27, 1872. Six windmill manufacturers operated here before 1900. Many of the limestone factory buildings still stand and now serve as government and commercial offices and storefronts.

The river and the factory district shaped the oldest part of town, so a Batavia price starts with the block. If your house is within walking distance of the river paths or the old factory district, say so in the first line of the description. Schools and roads

Batavia Public School District 101 has six K-5 elementary schools, one 6-8 middle school and Batavia High School. Small pockets of the city belong to Geneva Community Unit School District 304 and to West Aurora District 129. The district line can follow a street instead of a city boundary, so confirm the school assignment for your address before you repeat a school claim in a listing.

Batavia Avenue is Illinois Route 31, Main Street is Route 10 and Washington and River streets carry Illinois Route 25 along the river. Randall Road and Wilson Street are also major streets. Pace runs some bus service, and the Geneva and Aurora Metra stations are nearby. Which county handles my deed and property record?

Most of the city is in Kane County, whose offices are at 719 Batavia Avenue, Building A, in Geneva, open weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30 with some offices keeping other hours. A portion of Batavia is in DuPage County, so check the parcel number on your tax bill to see which recorder and treasurer apply.

Illinois transfer tax is paid with stamps the recorder sells, and both parties sign Form PTAX-203 for the county. Home rule municipalities may levy extra, so ask the title company whether Batavia does. For recording charges, contact your county's recorder.

What happens at closing

Whichever way you sell, the paperwork looks the same. The deed has to name every owner, any lender must be paid off from the proceeds, and the recorder in the parcel's county files the transfer. A parcel in the DuPage portion follows a different office than one in the Kane portion.

Older houses near the river and the old factory district tend to raise inspection questions about wiring, roofs and basements. Because Batavia sits in two counties, line up the documents in the right office from the start. The county printed on your tax bill tells you where the deed gets recorded and who collects the tax. Then settle the current year's tax and any open installment through the title company so the closing statement shows a clear balance.

A step-by-step path for a Batavia seller

Selling goes faster when the steps are in order. Begin with the parcel number on your tax bill and learn whether the house is in the Kane or DuPage part of the city. Next, decide between a listing, a private sale and a cash buyer. Then collect the papers a buyer or title company will request: the tax bill, a payoff letter from any lender, and permit records.

When a contract is signed, the title company runs the search and prepares the closing statement. The deed has to name every owner, so if the house passed through an estate or a family transfer, tell the title company early and ask what extra documents the recorder needs. At closing, the lender is paid from the proceeds, the seller receives the balance, and the county recorder files the deed. Ask for the recorded copy and keep it with your closing papers.

What buyers want to know about a Batavia address

Buyers ask three things first: which county, which school district and how far the house is from the main roads or the train. Having those answers ready saves time. Write the district into the listing only after you have checked the street, since boundaries can follow a road. Say whether the river path or the old downtown is a short walk. For a house that needs work, state the condition plainly and let the price carry it.

If an inspector finds old wiring, a worn roof or a damp basement, the cash route keeps those items out of negotiation, while a listing may bring requests for credits or repairs. Neither route is wrong. Pick the one that fits your timeline and how much work you want to take on before closing.

Most likely Kane, though part of the city lies in DuPage. The parcel number on your tax bill settles it and tells you which recorder files the deed.

Batavia Public School District 101 covers most of the city, with small areas in Geneva District 304 and West Aurora District 129. Check your address.

The Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration, completed by buyer and seller and filed in the county of the parcel as part of the recording.

The sale contract decides. Revenue stamps for the state tax come through the county recorder, and a home rule municipality or county may add its own. Your title company can list each charge.

The Chicago Heights market

Chicago Heights is a Cook County city about 30 miles south of the Chicago Loop, covering 10.38 square miles. Its neighbors include Homewood, Flossmoor, Park Forest, Glenwood, Sauk Village, Olympia Fields, Ford Heights and South Chicago Heights, so a seller's comparable sales often cross village lines.

The city peaked at 40,900 residents in 1970 and has lost people in every census since, reaching 27,480 in 2020, with an estimate of 26,533 for 2024. The 2020 count lists 9,261 households and 10,663 housing units, 13.1 percent of them vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 4.0 percent and the rental vacancy rate 13.3 percent. That is more supply than a growing suburb has, so price and condition matter a great deal to buyers.

Clearing the transfer stamp

The city charges a real estate transfer tax of $4.00 per $1,000 of sale price, and the seller is responsible for paying it. Three city offices must be cleared before the stamp is issued, and the city's instruction sheet lists the order in which to visit them.

Transfer stamp steps
StepOffice and phoneWhat happens
1Code Enforcement, 708-756-5328For-sale inspection; unpaid liens and building violations resolved
2Water Billing, 708-756-5344Final meter reading, booked at least 3 days before the loan closing; final bill
3City Clerk, 708-756-5304Other unpaid fees or citations; transfer tax payment
4Code EnforcementCertificate of Occupancy after the final inspection passes and any escrow is posted

The clerk's office needs the completed application signed by seller and buyer, a photocopy of the new deed, the Certificate of Occupancy and the state PTAX-203 declaration. Payment must be cash, money order, or a cashier's, certified, attorney or title company check. Credit cards, debit cards and personal checks are not accepted, and each payment (transfer tax, exemption fee, water, escrow) is separate.

The for-sale inspection

Code Enforcement oversees property maintenance, building safety and regulatory compliance, and it conducts residential and commercial sale and rental inspections for life-safety standards. The city's codes include the 2018 International Residential Code, the 2012 Property Maintenance Code, the 2014 Illinois Plumbing Code and the 2017 National Electrical Code.

  • Call 708-756-5328 early, because the Certificate of Occupancy depends on a passed final inspection.
  • Resolve open violations or liens, or post an escrow where the city allows it.
  • Ask whether the inspection date and result affect your closing schedule.

Repairs that a for-sale inspection finds do not disappear in a cash sale. A buyer who takes the house as-is still has to satisfy the city's requirements, so ask Code Enforcement how an as-is transfer is handled before you accept an offer.

Vacant and foreclosure properties

Chicago Heights runs a defaulted mortgage and foreclosure property registration program, administered by Hera Property Registry. Owners, mortgagees and trustees must register online and pay a fee.

If the house has sat empty, register it, resolve the violations and gather the permit history before listing. A buyer's attorney will ask about each,.

State and Cook County steps

Illinois taxes the transfer of real estate at 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, using the declaration filed in MyDec. When the deed is recorded with the Cook County Clerk, staff check for the state stamp and for any local stamp the municipality requires.

Even a quitclaim deed with no money changing hands needs stamps and an exempt-transfer notation. Chicago Heights separately charges a $100 processing fee for exempt transfers and requires an original signed, notarized deed, so a photocopy will not do.

What to bring to the clerk

Paying the fees without delays

Because the city takes only certain forms of payment, plan a trip to the bank. A cashier's check or money order for each charge keeps the counter visit short. Cash works too, but a receipt matters, so keep every one with your closing papers. Ask your title company or attorney which of the payments they will bring and which are yours.

Book the water reading first, since it has a fixed lead time of at least three days before the loan closing. The inspection and the Certificate of Occupancy come next, because the clerk will not accept the application without it.

How the order of offices affects your timeline

The steps run in sequence, so a delay at the first office pushes everything after it. If the for-sale inspection finds violations, you must resolve them or post an escrow before the Certificate of Occupancy is issued. The clerk will not issue a stamp without that certificate. Plan your closing date with room to spare, and ask your buyer whether the date can move if a repair takes longer than expected.

The water reading needs at least three days of notice before the loan closing, and the Certificate of Occupancy depends on the final inspection. Start both in the same week. Then use the days in between to gather the deed copy, the PTAX-203 and your payment forms, so the clerk visit is the last step and not another delay.

Listing, selling privately or taking a cash offer

A listing reaches the most buyers, but the city's inspection and stamp process falls on the seller either way. Selling privately saves a commission and puts the paperwork on you. A cash offer on an as-is house can shorten the timeline, particularly when the house has open violations, a vacancy problem or an estate behind it.

Compare the net from each route after repairs, carrying costs and the city's fees, and ask each buyer how they will handle the for-sale inspection.

What to ask a buyer before you sign

  • Who orders and pays for the for-sale inspection, and who fixes what it finds?
  • Who pays the $4.00 per $1,000 tax? The city holds the seller responsible, so a contract that shifts it should say so plainly.
  • Will the buyer close on a date that leaves time for the water reading and the Certificate of Occupancy?
  • If there is an escrow for open items, who posts it?

Get those answers in writing before you sign anything. A written list of duties keeps both sides clear when the clerk's counter asks for a document.

The seller. The city's rate is $4.00 per $1,000 of sale price, and it is paid at the City Clerk's office.

How do I pay the Chicago Heights transfer tax?

With cash, a money order, or a cashier's, certified, attorney or title company check. The city does not accept credit or debit cards or personal checks.

When should I schedule the final water reading?

At least three days before the loan closing. Call Water Billing at 708-756-5344.

Do I need an inspection to sell in Chicago Heights?

Yes for a standard sale. Call Code Enforcement at 708-756-5328 to schedule a for-sale inspection and to clear unpaid violations or liens. Exempt transfers may need a check on whether an inspection applies.

What does an exempt transfer cost?

The city charges a $100 processing fee for an exempt stamp. The original notarized deed is required and no photocopy is accepted.

Selling in Edwardsville?

What speeds up a quick Edwardsville sale

Three things set the pace for a quick Edwardsville sale: how much work the house needs, whether the title is clean, and how fast the Madison County documents come together. A seller who has the parcel number, the payoff letter and any permit records in hand can move much sooner than one who starts collecting them after an offer arrives.

You can hire an agent and host showings, sell the home yourself, or take an as-is cash purchase that closes on the day you choose. The cash route skips repairs and open houses. Whichever you pick, the deed, transfer declaration and tax proration work the same way, and the sections below explain them.

  • Find the parcel number (PIN) printed on your Madison County tax bill.
  • Get a payoff letter from your lender and look for liens against the property.
  • Note whether anyone rents the home, since Edwardsville tracks rentals by registration.
  • Decide whether you want to close within weeks or can wait through a listing period.

Edwardsville housing at a glance

Edwardsville is the Madison County seat, about 18 miles northeast of downtown St. Louis, with 26,463 residents. Southern Illinois University Edwardsville is based here, and the median age is a young 30.1. Most of the city lies in Edwardsville Community Unit School District 7, with small slivers in other districts, so check which district your own address falls in before writing a listing.

There are 9,828 households, and two thirds of them own their homes. The 2020 count listed 10,456 housing units with 14.2 percent of rental units vacant, so a landlord selling a house with a tenant should expect renters to have choices.

Edwardsville housing measures, 2020 to 2024
MeasureEdwardsville
Middle value of an owned home$299,800
Owner-occupied share66.6%

Midpoint owner cost, with mortgage$2,040
People per household2.38

The $299,800 figure is a midpoint across the whole city. A Saint Louis Street classic, a newer subdivision house and a rental near campus can sit far apart, so set your asking price from recent closed sales of comparable houses on nearby streets.

Storms and temperature swings

Madison County has real storm exposure. The tornado outbreak of December 10 and 11, 2021 struck Edwardsville, where an EF3 tornado collapsed an Amazon warehouse. Lenders and insurers often ask about roof age, window condition and earlier storm repairs, so save receipts and permit records.

Temperatures swing widely, from the 19 degrees Fahrenheit of a typical January to 90 in July. The city sits in Climate Zone 4A under the International Energy Conservation Code, so heating and cooling equipment gets used hard. An old unit or a stained ceiling will show up on any inspection report.

Some owners skip the roof repair and sell to a buyer who accepts the damage.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Edwardsville house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Rental registration when an Edwardsville landlord sells

Edwardsville operates a Rental Registration and Inspection Program, and each rental must be registered annually. The form sets $40 for a single-family or mobile home building, $60 for a duplex and $25 per unit in buildings of three or more. Registrations received after January 31 pay a $75 late fee, a first re-inspection is free, and later ones cost $75.

The sale itself triggers paperwork. An ownership change requires deregistration, with Property Sold as one of the listed reasons, and a purchaser has 30 days from taking title to register. The city also refuses registration to any owner with unpaid fees or fines. Contact rentalregistration@cityofedwardsville.com or 618-307-1501 with questions.

  • File the deregistration once the sale closes so city records name the right owner.
  • Pay any fees or fines owed to the city before the closing date.
  • Tell the buyer which units have tenants, because inspections are requested before occupancy.
  • Smoke detectors are required in each sleeping room, within 15 feet of sleeping rooms and on every level, and carbon monoxide detectors within 15 feet of sleeping rooms.

Recording an Edwardsville deed

The Madison County Recorder handles deeds for Edwardsville. The state charge is $.50 per $500 of taxable consideration, or part thereof, and the county charge is $.25 per $500, or part thereof. A PTAX declaration or a statement of exemption has to accompany the deed, and the exemptions sit in 35 ILCS 200/31-45.

The office has a few rules that catch do-it-yourself sellers. Every deed needs the buyer's name and mailing address for tax billing. A notarized Plat Act affidavit travels with it, and the permanent parcel number belongs on the document. If you pay by check, write the recording fee and the transfer tax on different checks. Ask the office for the current recording fee.

A closing agent can take over this paperwork, and you should read the transfer tax line on the settlement statement before signing.

Madison County property tax bills

The Treasurer bills real estate tax in four installments, due in July, September, October and December, on the 9th of each month. A late installment gains a 1.5 percent penalty for each 30 days it stays unpaid. Under 35 ILCS 200/20-15, a missing bill does not cancel the debt.

Illinois tax is paid after the year it covers, since taxes on one year's assessments are paid the next year. At closing, the settlement statement divides the bill, so ask for that split in writing. If taxes go unpaid they are sold at the annual tax sale, and redemption can run two to three years. A lien of that kind complicates any sale, so clear it first.

Assessment appeals go to the Madison County Board of Review, which accepts filings up to 30 days after assessments are published. Relief is available for general homestead, senior homestead, disabled persons and senior freeze. Phone the Chief County Assessment Office to learn which apply to your parcel.

Before closing, ask the Treasurer's office for a paid-to-date printout so the title company can confirm which installments are settled.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Edwardsville houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Permit records before selling in Edwardsville

Buyers and their lenders ask about work done to the house. Edwardsville's building permit application covers new construction, remodels, garages, roofs, and electrical, plumbing and mechanical work, and it includes a line asking whether the property is a rental. The roofing section asks for an Illinois roofing license number.

An open permit or an unpermitted addition can stall a closing. Collect records for decks, finished basements, water heaters and furnaces before you list. Ask the city whether anything on your address remains open, and finish it before you sign a purchase contract.

Frequently asked questions

What if tenants live in my Edwardsville house?

A sale is still possible. The city requires owners to register rentals each year and to deregister when the property sells, so file the Property Sold deregistration after closing. The buyer registers within 30 days of taking ownership.

How much transfer tax will an Edwardsville seller see on the settlement statement?

The state charges $.50 per $500 and Madison County $.25 per $500, each on taxable consideration or part thereof. Your closing agent turns that into dollars for the statement.

Who records the deed on an Edwardsville home?

The Madison County Recorder. The deed arrives with a PTAX declaration or exemption statement, a notarized Plat Act affidavit, the parcel number and the buyer's tax billing address. Title companies usually submit the package.

How many times a year does Madison County bill property tax?

Four times, from July through December, with a 1.5 percent monthly penalty on late installments. The Treasurer's website shows what has been paid on your parcel.

Will a cash sale close faster than a listing in Edwardsville?

Often yes, since there is no marketing period, mortgage approval or repair haggling. County paperwork, payoff and title review still apply, so a clean title sets the real pace.

Selling in Woodstock?

Why people sell in Woodstock

Woodstock is the McHenry County seat, about 51 miles northwest of Chicago, and most owners who sell are moving closer to work, downsizing, settling an estate or leaving a rental behind. The town square, the Opera House and the old county courthouse anchor a historic district, which draws buyers who like older homes.

That mix of older homes near downtown and newer subdivisions on the edges means two very different sales. A century-old house near the square may call for a roof or rewiring, while a newer one farther out tends to sell on location and school boundaries.

Woodstock housing and income

Woodstock has about 10,650 households, and nearly three in ten of them rent. Population was 25,630 at the 2020 count and is estimated at 25,740 for 2025.

Workers average a 24.6-minute commute.

Schools and the train

Woodstock Community Unit School District 200 serves the city. For many buyers, the school buildings and the train station matter as much as the house.

  • District 200 runs an early learning center (Verda Dierzen) and six elementary schools: Dean Street, Greenwood, Mary Endres, Olson, Prairiewood and Westwood.
  • Two middle schools, Northwood and Creekside, feed Woodstock High School and Woodstock North High School.
  • St. Mary Catholic grade school covers kindergarten through eighth grade in town, and many students go on to Marian Central Catholic High School.
  • Woodstock station is on Metra's Union Pacific Northwest Line, the second to last stop before Harvard, with 14 weekday trains to Chicago.

Name the train line and the school district in any listing. Cash buyers weigh the same things, plus the repair list.

Recording the deed in McHenry County

The deed is recorded with the McHenry County Recorder, and a transfer declaration (PTAX-203 or the online MyDec) has to accompany it. A document that meets state requirements and comes with the right fee is recorded the same day it is received, and documents usually come back within about two working days. Call 815-334-4110 for fee questions.

One point helps sellers here: no municipality in McHenry County charges a separate transfer tax. So the Woodstock closing does not add a city stamp like those in some other Illinois towns. The state still expects a signed declaration to travel with every deed (35 ILCS 200/31-25).

Liens and back taxes

Before closing, search for liens. The Recorder will help you look for liens and foreclosures filed against a property. The County Treasurer (815-334-4072) and County Clerk (815-334-4242) handle questions on unpaid taxes and property sold for back taxes. The Assessor's office at 815-334-4290 can confirm who owns a parcel.

If taxes or a lien turn up, the amount is paid from your proceeds at closing and the deed passes clear. Call these offices early so the figure you hear is current, and ask for it in writing.

Building permits before a sale

Open or missing permits show up in a buyer's inspection. Woodstock's Building and Planning staff issue permits for work such as roofs, furnaces, water heaters, decks, fences, garages, sheds, solar panels, plumbing and electrical work, and for windows or doors when the opening changes size. Driveways and aprons need zoning approval only.

  • Express permits are generally issued in 3 to 5 business days, and typical review for other projects is 10 to 15 business days.
  • Most building permits last 120 days, while a permit for a new principal building or an addition lasts 12 months, with a written extension possible for good cause.
  • A final inspection is required before a building is used or occupied, and inspections need at least 48 hours' notice at 815-338-4305.

If an earlier owner finished the basement or added a deck without a permit, speak with Building and Planning before you list. A cash purchaser may overlook it, but a lender's appraiser might not.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Woodstock houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Rental property rules

Title 4, Chapter 13 of the Woodstock City Code sets up a performance-based Property Management Program. An owner who is found liable for two or more code violations in one rental unit within six months must register every unit they own, at no fee, and return the form within 30 days. An owner found liable for four or more violations in a single unit within 12 months needs a city permit to keep renting.

That permit depends on interior and exterior inspections. The unit that triggered it is inspected, and so are all of an owner's units if they own eight or fewer in the city. For larger owners the city inspects the original unit plus up to 25% of the rest. The first inspection and re-inspection are free, and a third and later ones cost $40 each. The requirement ends after twelve months without another finding of liability.

If you are selling a rental, ask Building and Planning whether the property is under the program. An investor who buys it will want to know before offering.

Options for a fast sale

A quick sale is realistic when the house is priced to match the repairs it needs and the paperwork is clean. You have three paths, and the right one depends on condition and timing.

  • Agent listing: you wait on showings, an appraisal and the buyer's financing. It suits a sound house near the Square.
  • Owner sale: no commission, though the contract, disclosure and showings land on you.
  • Cash purchase: no financing step and few repair requests. It fits estate houses, tenant-occupied homes and houses with code violations.

Get any offer in writing and compare the net after repairs, taxes and carrying cost.

Whichever route you take, the steps after you accept an offer look alike. A title company searches the record for liens, you request a payoff letter from any lender, and the seller disclosure report goes to the buyer before the contract is signed. At closing you sign the deed, the proceeds come to you, and the McHenry County Recorder files the deed with its PTAX-203 declaration. A cash buyer skips the loan approval and the appraisal, so the schedule follows the title work and your move date.

Frequently asked questions

Does the City of Woodstock charge its own transfer tax?

No. No municipality in McHenry County charges a separate transfer tax. You still file a transfer declaration (PTAX-203 or MyDec) with the deed, and the recorder's fees apply.

Which office records a Woodstock deed?

Record it with the McHenry County Recorder. Call 815-334-4110 with fee questions. Documents that meet state requirements and have the correct fee are recorded the same day they are received.

Is a permit needed for a new roof or furnace in Woodstock?

Yes. The city's permit list includes roofs, furnace installs or replacements, water heaters, fences, decks and sheds. Express permits generally take 3 to 5 business days, so apply early if you want the work finished before listing.

What if my Woodstock rental has had code violations?

Registration becomes mandatory after two or more violations in one unit within six months, and a permit with inspections is required after four or more within 12 months. Registration is free, and the first inspection and re-inspection carry no charge.

Who can tell me whether property taxes are owed on a Woodstock parcel?

Ask the McHenry County Treasurer at 815-334-4072 about unpaid tax and the County Clerk at 815-334-4242 about property sold for back taxes.

Selling in South Elgin?

Three ways to sell in South Elgin

An agent listing, a private sale and an as-is cash purchase all end the same way, with a recorded Kane County deed. What differs is the calendar and the repair bill you accept on the way.

  • Agent listing: staging, photos and showings come first, and the closing date follows the buyer's lender.
  • Private sale: you price the house, field the calls and negotiate, usually with an attorney reading the contract.
  • Cash, as-is: no lender means no appraisal gap and no punch list from an inspector.

Cash fits a house that needs a roof or furnace, an inherited property nobody lives in, or a move with a hard date. A listing may bring a stronger price on a tidy home, at the cost of weeks of preparation.

South Elgin values and who lives here

South Elgin is a Kane County village on both banks of the Fox River, with an estimated 25,656 residents. Ownership is high and incomes are strong: 79.1% of homes are lived in by their owners, the middle value is $339,100, and the middle household income is $127,203. Middle gross rent is $1,640. Owner cost per month runs $2,291 with a loan and $911 without one.

The village roughly doubled in size between 1990 and 2000, so much of the housing is newer than in older river towns. Details like your own roof age and mechanicals will drive price more than any village average, so check them with a local agent. Two freight rail lines pass through, and a house near a crossing may draw comments about noise during showings. Elgin Area School District U-46 and St. Charles Community Unit School District 303 both cover parts of the village, and the line follows streets, so confirm yours before writing a listing description.

Permits for repairs before you sell

Most building work needs a permit from Community Development at Village Hall, 10 N. Water Street. The office answers at (847) 741-3894 on weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

South Elgin permit timing
Permit stageTiming
Staff review of small projects5 to 10 business days
Review sent to an outside consultantThree weeks
Permit validitySix months, with six more available for an extension fee
Inspection bookingCall by 4:00 p.m. for next-day service

The village exempts painting, wallpaper, tile, carpet, tree trimming and broken window repair. Construction noise is limited to the hours between 7 a.m. and 9 p.m. A radon control system needs its own permit, and renovation of any building from before 1978 falls under the federal lead-based paint repair rule. A contractor who pulls permits for you will know which code edition applies.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your South Elgin house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Unpermitted work and compliance orders

The village's permit FAQ says an informed realtor or lawyer may tell a client to hold off on a purchase until permits and inspections are on file. It also says it is unlawful to sell, transfer, mortgage or lease a structure served with a compliance order. A finished basement or deck built without paperwork is worth a call before you list, and even with an as-is buyer the contract should address it. Call Community Development to learn how an order can be cleared or passed on to a buyer. Ask for the answer in writing, and give a copy to the title company so that nobody is surprised at the table. If the work was done by a contractor, find out whether a permit was ever pulled and keep any inspection record you can find.

Assessments and appeals

Township assessors, Elgin Township or St. Charles Township for South Elgin parcels, set the starting values, and the county equalizes them. Kane's assessment office describes the base as 33.33 percent of fair cash value on January 1, drawn from three earlier years of sales.

Start any dispute with your assessor. If that fails, the Kane County Board of Review takes complaints for 30 days after the township roll is published in a local newspaper. Recognized grounds are wrong property data, a value above one third of market value, and a figure out of line with comparable houses. The state appeal board has held that the size of the bill or of a yearly jump does not qualify.

Homestead exemptions

  • General Homestead: an $8,000 cut to equalized assessed value on an owner's main residence.
  • Senior Citizen: the same $8,000 figure, available once the owner turns 65 by the last day of the assessment year.
  • Forms: call 630-208-3818 or use the online portal.

If taxes on a parcel were sold, the owner redeems them through the County Clerk's tax extension office at 630-232-5964. Your title company will tell you how taxes are divided at the table.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy South Elgin houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What the closing records and taxes

The deed goes to the Kane County Recorder, normally filed by the title agent or attorney. Section 31-15 of the Property Tax Code (35 ILCS 200/31-15) sets the state levy on a sale at 50 cents per $500 of value. The recorder collects it through revenue stamps, and the filing reaches the Department of Revenue through MyDec.

Call the Recorder for the county's share and the recording fee. Call the village to learn whether any local stamp or final water reading applies. A title company can usually settle both questions in one phone call, and the numbers will appear on your settlement statement.

Look for your plat of survey in your purchase papers. Surveys are generally part of the closing set, and permit staff request one with many applications.

What an as-is sale spares you in South Elgin

Selling to a cash buyer means you skip the permit queue for pre-sale projects, the contractor visits and the weeks of showings. A buyer who pays cash prices the defects in, so you are not asked to fix the roof or furnace first. You still need to resolve any open permit or compliance order, deliver a clean title, and have the deed recorded. Gather your deed, a recent tax bill, your survey and any permit records, and hand them to the title company at the start. If the house is empty, keep the lawn mowed and the utilities on until the deed records, because a buyer's walkthrough is often the last step before closing. Ask the buyer to put the closing date, the price and who pays each recording cost in the contract, so nothing is left to a phone call on the day.

Frequently asked questions

Must I fix my South Elgin house before it sells?

Illinois does not make a seller repair a house first. Open permits and unresolved compliance orders can still stall a closing, and an as-is buyer will price the defects in while a listing buyer may ask you to fix them.

Which township handles assessment for a South Elgin parcel?

Elgin Township or St. Charles Township, depending on the parcel. The Kane County assessment office can confirm yours from the parcel number.

Can a South Elgin house with a code violation be sold?

Only with care. It is unlawful to sell or transfer a structure that has been served with a compliance order, so call Community Development at (847) 741-3894 to learn how the order can be cleared or passed on to a buyer.

How much is the Illinois transfer stamp on a sale here?

Fifty cents per $500 of value goes to the state, paid through the recorder. County and village charges are separate, so have the recorder and your title company list every line before closing.

What homestead exemptions can a South Elgin owner claim?

The General Homestead and Senior Citizen exemptions each cut equalized assessed value by $8,000. For forms, call 630-208-3818 or use the online portal.

Selling in Belvidere?

Belvidere housing and history

Belvidere is the Boone County seat in far northern Illinois, about 12 miles east of Rockford and roughly 75 miles northwest of downtown Chicago. The Kishwaukee River runs through it, and the city is known as the City of Murals. Downtown sits on the south side of the river because a railroad built there in 1851 pulled the business district across the water. A house near State Street may be well over a century old, and buyers of older homes tend to ask about electrical service, roofs and basements.

Severe weather is part of local history. A tornado on April 21, 1967 killed 24 people and demolished over 100 homes, and an EF1 tornado hit the city on March 31, 2023. Keep roof invoices, storm-damage repair records and any insurance claim paperwork, since buyers and insurers ask for them.

Population and home values

The city counted 25,339 residents in April 2020 and is estimated at 25,462 for July 1, 2025, a 0.5 percent gain. That steady count means prices follow condition and interest rates more than population swings. With owners holding 70.9 percent of housing, most sales are family homes rather than investor stock.

Belvidere housing and household figures
Housing figureBelvidere
Median home value, owner-occupied units, 2020-2024$158,900
Owner-occupied housing rate70.9%
Median gross rent$991
Households9,589

Persons per household2.56

How the Stellantis plant affects home sales

The Belvidere Assembly Plant, built in the mid-1960s, has long been the city's best-known employer. It built the Dodge Neon until 2005 and later the Jeep Cherokee, and Stellantis idled it in February 2023. Under the 2023 UAW settlement the company agreed to reopen it, so plant news moves buyer confidence in a way few other single sites do. A local agent can tell you how the latest announcements are affecting showings on your street.

Sellers who need to move quickly often compare a listing timeline with a direct cash purchase, where there is no mortgage approval to wait on.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Belvidere house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Schools and downtown

Belvidere Community Unit School District 100 serves the city. Its two high schools are Belvidere High School and Belvidere North High School, and its middle schools are South and Central. Buyers with children will want to confirm which attendance zone the street falls in.

Downtown draws buyers with the Boone County Museum of History, the Carnegie-built Ida Public Library and festivals such as Heritage Days. If your house is walkable to State Street, say so in the listing or offer conversation.

Building Department permits and repairs

The City of Belvidere Building Department permits and inspects construction and enforces the zoning and property maintenance codes. It sits at 401 Whitney Boulevard, Suite 300, takes calls at 815-547-7177 and keeps counter hours of 8 a.m. until 5 p.m. on weekdays. Phone first if you plan a pre-sale project, since some jobs need a permit and many permit types can be applied for online.

  • The city adopted the 2021 International codes (building, residential, fire, mechanical, fuel gas, existing building and energy) by Ordinance 703H on November 19, 2024, for permit applications after January 1, 2025.
  • State law has required carbon monoxide alarms in existing and new residences since January 1, 2007, installed within 15 feet of each bedroom.
  • Projects commonly needing permits include siding, windows and doors, remodeling, additions, central air, plumbing, finished basements, and driveways, approaches, sidewalks and patios.
  • Landmarked buildings face added construction rules through the Historic Preservation Commission.
  • Work in the public right-of-way, such as curb cuts, sidewalks, or water and sewer line repairs, needs a Public Works permit at 401 Whitney Boulevard, Suite 200.

Request the permit history for your address before listing. An unfinished permit tends to surprise a buyer's inspector, whereas a cash buyer will usually take the house as-is and deal with it later.

Recording a deed in Boone County

The Boone County recorder charges $65.00 for a standard document, $67.00 for a non-standard document and $47.00 for an exempt standard document, on a schedule effective August 1, 2018. The statewide Rental Housing Support Fee increase took effect July 1, 2023, so ask the office for the total before you send a check. The office takes cash and checks, wants a return envelope with postage, and cannot give legal advice.

Since September 11, 2023, the county accepts transfer declarations only through the state's MyDec service, with the status set to closing completed before documents are submitted. A deed also needs a Plat Act Affidavit when it uses a metes and bounds description, designates roadway easements, or divides about five acres or less. Simplifile, CSC and EPN are the e-recording providers, and a title company usually files for you.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Belvidere houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Assessments, appeals and tax bills

Each township assessor values parcels as of January 1 with a target of one-third of market value, and the Supervisor of Assessments evens out the townships to 33.33 percent. An owner who disagrees files a Board of Review complaint on the county's forms, stating a market-value opinion with evidence, no later than 30 days after changes are published or September 10, whichever comes later. Evidence the board accepts includes a closing statement from a recent purchase, at least three comparable sales within a year of the assessment date, a recent appraisal, or income and expense statements for investment property. A decision can be appealed to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board in Springfield within 30 days.

Bills come from the Boone County Treasurer the year after the assessment year, in two equal installments targeted for June and September. The Treasurer is at 1212 Logan Avenue, Suite 104, 815-544-2666. Available exemptions include the general homestead exemption (an increase over 1977 value up to $6,000 of equalized value), a $5,000 senior exemption, a $2,000 disabled persons reduction, the senior freeze, and exemptions for military service. If you are selling, confirm with the Treasurer which installment is paid and how the closing agent will prorate the rest.

Putting a sale together

Start with three calls. The Building Department can tell you about open permits or code questions on the address. The Treasurer can say which installment is paid. Your title company can confirm that the transfer declaration will be filed through MyDec with the right status and that the deed has any Plat Act Affidavit it needs. With those answers in hand, a buyer's lender or inspector has fewer surprises to raise.

A cash sale skips the mortgage approval and usually the repair negotiation, which helps when a tornado repair record is thin or a permit was never closed. A listing may bring a higher price on a clean, documented house. Either way, get the terms in writing and read who pays recording fees before closing day.

Frequently asked questions

Is a tornado damage history a problem when selling in Belvidere?

It can be, mainly if repairs were incomplete or undocumented. The city was hit by an F4 tornado on April 21, 1967 and an EF1 on March 31, 2023, so buyers and inspectors often ask for roof and structural repair records. Gather permits and invoices, or consider an as-is sale if records are thin.

Is a transfer declaration required for a Boone County sale?

Yes. Boone County has accepted declarations only through the Illinois Department of Revenue's MyDec service since September 11, 2023, and the status must say closing completed before recording. Your title company or attorney normally completes it with you.

How much does recording a deed cost in Boone County?

The base schedule, effective August 1, 2018, is $65.00 for a standard document, $67.00 for non-standard and $47.00 for government-exempt documents. A Rental Housing Support Fee increase took effect July 1, 2023, so confirm the current total with the recorder.

When can I appeal a Belvidere property assessment?

Within 30 days after assessment changes are published, or by September 10, whichever is later. File a Board of Review complaint with your estimate of January 1 market value and supporting evidence such as three comparable sales or a recent appraisal.

Does Belvidere require a city inspection before closing?

Ask the Building Department at 815-547-7177 about open permits or code violations on your address before you list. Those items can affect a buyer's lender or inspector, and the department enforces the property maintenance and zoning codes.

Selling in West Chicago?

The city approval step before a West Chicago sale

A West Chicago sale has one local step that most Illinois suburbs lack: the city must approve the structure before any deed is recorded. The same paperwork applies to a listed sale, a private deal or a buyer paying cash for a property in any condition. Plan for it early, because the inspection is valid for six months and the city asks for scheduling at least two months before closing.

The city sits on the western edge of DuPage County, about 32 miles from downtown Chicago, with Illinois Route 59 running north and south and Routes 38 and 64 running east and west. Buyers who commute use the Metra station on Main Street or drive to I-88 and I-355, so mention both in your listing.

What the city inspector checks

The Community Development Department inspects the structure for basic maintenance and life safety, and no Deed Certification Number is issued without an approved inspection unless an exemption applies. A visit takes about 30 minutes and happens Monday through Friday between 9 a.m. and 3 p.m. Vacant lots are inspected too.

  • Smoke detectors must be present and working.
  • Ground fault interrupters must be installed where the checklist calls for them.
  • Stair railings must meet the minimum standard.
  • The structure must show adequate property maintenance, and vacant parcels are checked for tall grass, weeds and garbage.

The fee is a $100.00 base charge plus $0.12 per square foot, using the square footage the township supplies to the city. A vacant parcel adds a flat $20.00. If the house fails, you can fix the items and request a re-inspection at no added charge, or sell as-is and leave the repairs to the buyer.

Seller steps before the deed records

The city lays the steps out in order, and skipping one stalls the recording.

Seller steps from the City of West Chicago Property Transactions page
OrderStepFee or timing
1City inspection$100.00 base plus $0.12 per square foot; valid six months
2Final water and sewer readingCall Finance at least 2 working days before closing
3Clear city balancesInspection fees, water bills, parking tickets, ordinance violations, liens, waste services
4Deed Certification NumberForm signed by a seller or agent, presented at 475 Main Street

The number must be attached to the deed when the title is recorded. Payment at City Hall can be made by cash, check, or debit or credit card.

Certain transfers skip the inspection fee but still need a certification number. They include new construction, deeds that secure or release a debt, corrective deeds with no added consideration, and a sale where the occupant does not change. A final water reading is still required for those exempt deeds, and the city takes up to five business days to decide an exemption.

Selling as-is

When a seller declines to repair failed items, the buyer signs a Letter of Intent Agreement and posts a $1,600.00 bond with the Community Development Department. The buyer then has 90 days to finish repairs and pass an inspection, and one free 90-day extension is available if requested in person before the deadline. After an approved inspection the city refunds $1,500.00 within two to three weeks, because it keeps a $100.00 administrative fee.

This rule shapes cash offers on rough houses. A buyer who plans renovations can still close, but the bond and the 90-day clock are part of the buyer's cost, so ask any purchaser how they handle the city's requirements before you sign.

West Chicago homes and prices

West Chicago is a young, family-heavy market. Owners live in 70.9% of homes, typical values sit at $336,800, rent is $1,469 a month and household income is $99,927. Population is estimated at 25,296 for July 2025, down 1.3% from the 2020 base of 25,614, and 92.2% of residents stayed at one address over the prior year, a sign of low turnover.

Median monthly owner costs run $2,428 with a mortgage and $1,035 without one. Buyers with a monthly budget in mind will compare those numbers with your asking price.

Property tax and the closing statement

West Chicago is in DuPage County, which bills property tax a year behind. Recent bills were mailed in late April, with installments on June 1 and September 1, so confirm the current dates with the county treasurer. The treasurer's page lists the general homestead exemption and the senior exemption at $8,000 each, so check your bill for both. If a mortgage servicer pays your tax, a yellow box on the bill says so and you should not pay twice.

The title company splits the unpaid tax between seller and buyer on the settlement statement, and the state taxes the transfer itself at a half dollar per $500 of declared value. Ask the DuPage County recorder what the county adds. Illinois also requires a seller of one to four units to deliver a finished disclosure report ahead of contract signing (765 ILCS 77/20).

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy West Chicago houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling a West Chicago rental

West Chicago requires a Rental Property License for residential landlords and annual rental inspections tied to the International Property Maintenance Code standard. If you are selling a rental, confirm that your license and inspection record are current, because open city items surface at the same Community Development counter that handles the sale inspection. A sale where the occupant or tenant does not change can qualify for the inspection fee exemption, so bring the signed deed to the Director of Community Development and ask for a ruling before closing.

Putting the timeline together

Book the inspection first, since the city wants about two months of lead time and the result lasts six months. While you wait, pull your payoff figure, your tax bill and any permit papers. Call Finance for the final water reading at least 2 working days before closing, and pay any city balances so the Deed Certification Number can be issued.

A cash buyer on a house that fails the inspection can still close, since the buyer takes the as-is route with the bond. Ask them in advance how they plan to handle it. At the table you sign the deed, the title company settles the taxes and payoffs, and the certification number goes on the deed before it is recorded.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a city inspection to sell my house in West Chicago?

Yes, except for the exempt transfer types the city lists. Without an approved inspection the city issues no Deed Certification Number, and the visit costs $100.00 plus $0.12 per square foot. It stays valid for six months, so schedule it about two months before closing.

Can I sell a West Chicago house that fails the inspection?

Yes. You can repair the items and get a free re-inspection, or sell as-is. With an as-is sale the buyer posts a $1,600.00 bond and has 90 days to finish repairs and pass.

Who schedules the final water reading in West Chicago?

The seller does. Contact the city's Finance Department at least 2 working days before closing, pay the unbilled water and sewer use, and clear any other city balances before the certification number is issued.

Does West Chicago charge a local transfer tax?

The city's published steps include inspection fees and a Deed Certification Number but no local transfer tax rate. The state's share is a half dollar on every $500 declared, and the DuPage County recorder can tell you what the county adds.

When are DuPage County property tax bills due?

Illinois bills a year behind, and recent installments fell on June 1 and September 1. Confirm the current dates with the county treasurer. Your closing statement splits the unpaid portion between seller and buyer.

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Alton, IL sale

Sell Your Alton House for Cash
